questions.q: An invented phrase says बहुफलं वृक्षम्. What does it describe?
options: A fruit of a big tree
optionExplain: Right: बहु- joined to a noun makes a description 'having many …', as in बहुगुणम्; it agrees with the noun described.
बहु- is 'many', not 'no'.
वृक्षम् is singular; one tree.
फल is inside the description, not a separate noun with वृक्ष as owner.
questions.explain: बहुगुणम् is 'having many qualities'; बहुफलम् is 'having many fruits'.
questions.teaches: बहु- before a noun makes a description 'having many …': बहुकल्पम्, बहुगुणम्, बहुफलम्.

questions.q: In this verse, who is described as devoted (अनुरक्त)?
options: The physician who treats the patient
optionExplain: The physician's qualities were given in the previous unit.
Right: अनुरक्तः … परिचारकः: the attendant is devoted.
The medicine's qualities were given in the previous unit.
The patient's qualities are in line 2: wealthy, obedient and so on.
questions.explain: Line 1 is about the attendant (परिचारकः): devoted, pure, skilled, intelligent.

questions.q: Arrange the four qualities of the attendant in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: अनुरक्तः शुचिर्दक्षो बुद्धिमान्परिचारकः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three qualities of the patient in line 2, and one word from line 1 to keep apart.
questions.rule: आढ्यः = wealthy; भिषग्वश्यः = obedient to the physician; सत्त्ववान् = having mental strength. अनुरक्तः (devoted) belongs to line 1, the attendant.
questions.teaches: First member + वश्य (भिषग्वश्य) means 'under the control of' that first member.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भिषग्वश्यः?
optionExplain: भिषः is not a word.
अश्यः is not a word.
Right: Final क् becomes ग् before the voiced व.
ग्वश्यः is not a word.
questions.explain: भिषक् (physician) + वश्यः (under control): obedient to the physician.
questions.rule: क् → ग् before a voiced consonant.

questions.q: Which qualities does the verse give the patient?
optionExplain: Right: आढ्यः.
Right: भिषग्वश्यः.
Right: सत्त्ववान्.
Devoted is the attendant's quality in line 1.
Intelligent is the attendant's quality in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the patient his qualities; devoted and intelligent are the attendant's.
questions.rule: Patient: wealthy, obedient, ज्ञापक (reading uncertain), mentally strong.

questions.q: An invented phrase says गुरुवश्यः शिष्यः. What does it describe?
options: A teacher obedient to the pupil
A pupil who rules over the teacher
A pupil obedient to the teacher
optionExplain: The first member names who controls: गुरु.
That would be the reverse.
Nothing here says 'without'.
Right: वश्य gives 'under the control of' the first member, as भिषग्वश्यः is under the physician.
questions.explain: Same pattern as भिषग्वश्यः: the first member is the one who has control.
questions.rule: X-वश्य = under the control of X.
questions.teaches: X-वश्य = under X's control, obedient to X (भिषग्वश्यः, गुरुवश्यः).

questions.q: When the physician lacks qualities, what happens to the other quarters?
options: They are replaced by new ones
optionExplain: Right: गुणवन्तोऽप्यनर्थकाः: even though they have qualities, they are useless.
The verse says the opposite: they become useless.
Nothing like this is said.
Replacement is not mentioned.
questions.explain: यद्वैद्ये विगुणे पादा गुणवन्तोऽपि अनर्थकाः: when the physician lacks qualities, the quarters are useless though they have qualities.
questions.rule: Physician without qualities: other quarters useless.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 1 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: यद्वैद्ये विगुणे पादा गुणवंतोऽप्यनर्थकाः.
questions.rule: Since in the physician + lacking qualities + the quarters + even qualified + useless.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of line 1 and the verb of line 2.
questions.rule: विगुणे = lacking qualities; गुणवन्तः = having qualities; अनर्थकाः = useless; यापयेत् = may keep going.
questions.teaches: The prefixes वि- and अन- mark lack: विगुण = lacking qualities, अनर्थक = without use.

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुणवंतोऽप्यनर्थकाः?
optionExplain: गुणवान् is the singular; the quarters are plural, गुणवन्तः.
Right: अः + अ gives ोऽ (गुणवन्तोऽपि); अपि + अनर्थकाः → अप्यनर्थकाः (इ before a different vowel becomes य्).
ओपि is not a word.
आपि is not a word; the word is अपि.
questions.explain: गुणवन्तः (having qualities, plural) + अपि (even) + अनर्थकाः (useless).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ोऽ; इ + other vowel → य्.

questions.q: The medicine, attendant and patient are all qualified, but the physician lacks qualities. What does the verse say?
options: The patient alone decides the result
optionExplain: That is the opposite of the verse.
The patient is one of the quarters named useless here.
Right: वैद्ये विगुणे … पादा अनर्थकाः: the other quarters are useless.
The medicine too is one of the quarters, useless without the physician.
questions.explain: The verse says a qualified rest cannot rescue a physician without qualities.
questions.rule: Physician unqualified → qualified other quarters useless.

questions.q: An invented line says सारथौ विगुणे रथोऽनर्थकः. What does it say?
options: The charioteer is useless because the chariot lacks qualities
Though the chariot lacks qualities, the driver is useful
The chariot lacks qualities and so the driver is a fool
When the charioteer lacks qualities, the chariot is useless
optionExplain: The locative phrase is the charioteer lacking qualities.
The locative names the charioteer, not the chariot.
Nothing about a fool is said.
Right: Noun and adjective both in the locative (सारथौ विगुणे) set the condition, as वैद्ये विगुणे.
questions.explain: A noun + adjective in the locative states the condition, 'when X is so': वैद्ये विगुणे.
questions.rule: Locative noun + adjective = when X is so.
questions.teaches: A noun and its adjective both in the locative (वैद्ये विगुणे, सारथौ विगुणे) mean 'when X is so'.

questions.q: In line 1, whom do they know as the chief cause of treatment?
optionExplain: Right: तमेव: him alone, the physician of the previous unit, is the chief cause.
The medicine is only one of the quarters.
The patient is only one of the quarters.
The attendant is only one of the quarters.
questions.explain: Because the physician's lack of qualities makes the other quarters useless, they call him the chief cause.
questions.rule: The physician alone is the chief cause.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads: साध्यः असाध्यः इति व्याधिः द्विधा, तौ तु पुनः द्विधा.
questions.rule: Curable, incurable: thus disease is twofold; those two again twofold.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words of line 1 and two of line 2.
questions.rule: प्रधानम् = chief; कारणम् = cause; साध्यः = curable; असाध्यः = incurable.
questions.teaches: अ- before a word reverses it: साध्य (curable), असाध्य (incurable).

questions.q: Which is the right split of साध्योऽसाध्य इति?
optionExplain: ओसाध्य is not a word.
Right: अः + अ gives ोऽ, and असाध्यः + इति loses its visarga before इ.
The second word has the negative अ-: असाध्यः, incurable.
The disease (व्याधिः) is masculine; असाध्यम् is neuter.
questions.explain: साध्यः (curable) + असाध्यः (incurable) + इति (thus).

questions.q: A learner says: the verse divides disease into curable and incurable, and each is again divided. Is that right?
options: No: it divides disease into curable only, with no second division
No: it divides disease into three
Yes: two, then each of the two again twofold
No: it names the four classes here
optionExplain: Incurable is named too.
The verse says twofold, then twofold again.
Right: व्याधिर्द्विधा, तौ तु पुनर्द्विधा says exactly that.
The four names come in the next unit.
questions.explain: The unit gives the first division and the second division but not the names of the final classes.

questions.q: An invented line says तमेव गुरुं श्रेष्ठं विदुः. What does it say?
options: They know the best teacher but not him
He alone knows the best teacher
They do not know that teacher as the best one
They know that teacher alone as the best
optionExplain: तमेव says him alone, not a different one.
The doer of विदुः is 'they', and the accusatives are what they know.
There is no negative in the line.
Right: विदुः takes two accusatives: 'know X as Y', as तमेव प्रधानं कारणं विदुः.
questions.explain: विदुः + two accusatives = 'they know X as Y'; एव = alone.
questions.rule: विदुः X Y = they know X as Y.
questions.teaches: With विदुः (they know) two accusatives give 'know X as Y'; एव limits it to X alone.

questions.q: Which set names the four classes of disease in this verse?
options: Easily curable, curable with difficulty, to be sustained, no remedy
Easily curable, curable with difficulty, incurable, and quickly fatal
Mild, severe, to be sustained, and one that admits no remedy
Curable, incurable, recent in onset, old in standing
optionExplain: Right: सुसाध्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यः याप्यः अनुपक्रमः: these four.
Only the first two are names in the verse; incurable and fatal are not among the four.
Mild and severe are not named.
Recent and old are not named.
questions.explain: The verse names four: सुसाध्य, कृच्छ्रसाध्य, याप्य, अनुपक्रम.
questions.rule: Four classes: सुसाध्य, कृच्छ्रसाध्य, याप्य, अनुपक्रम.

questions.q: Arrange the four classes in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads: सुसाध्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यश्च याप्यो यश्चानुपक्रमः.
questions.rule: Easily curable, curable with difficulty, to be sustained, without remedy.

questions.q: Match each class to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four classes of line 1.
questions.rule: सुसाध्यः = easily curable; कृच्छ्रसाध्यः = curable with difficulty; याप्यः = to be sustained (palliable); अनुपक्रमः = admitting no remedy.
questions.teaches: सु- means 'easily', कृच्छ्र- 'with difficulty': they qualify साध्य (to be accomplished, curable).

questions.q: Which is the right split of यश्चानुपक्रमः?
optionExplain: यत् would not give श्; the word is यः (which).
Right: The visarga becomes श् before च, and च + अ gives चा, since अ + अ → आ.
नुपक्रमः is not a word.
चानुपक्रमः is not a word; and the particle is च.
questions.explain: यः (which) + च (and) + अनुपक्रमः (without remedy).

questions.q: A physician says a disease can only be sustained. Which class name of the verse says this?
optionExplain: That is 'easily curable'.
That is 'curable with difficulty'.
Right: याप्य means to be sustained (palliated).
That is 'admits no remedy'.
questions.explain: याप्यः is the third class, 'to be sustained'.

questions.q: Invented path names: सुगम्यः and कृच्छ्रगम्यः, like सुसाध्यः and कृच्छ्रसाध्यः. What do they mean?
options: Hard to go along with; easy to go along with
Already gone along; not yet gone along
Easy to leave behind; hard to leave behind
Easy to go along; to be gone along with difficulty
optionExplain: The two prefixes are swapped.
Nothing marks past or negative.
गम्य is 'to be gone along', not leaving.
Right: सु- is 'easily' and कृच्छ्र- 'with difficulty', before गम्य, 'to be gone'.
questions.explain: The pattern सु-/कृच्छ्र- + a word 'to be done' gives 'easy to' and 'hard to'.
questions.teaches: सु- (easily) and कृच्छ्र- (with difficulty) before a 'to be done' word grade how hard it is.

questions.q: This verse lists features of an easily curable disease. Which feature would you expect it to give?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says अनुपद्रवः: without complications.
The verse says the opposite: अमर्मगः, not reaching the vital spots.
The verse says the cause is slight (अल्प).
No such signs are listed in this verse.
questions.explain: An easily curable disease is described with slight causes and signs and no complications.
questions.rule: Easily curable: not reaching vital spots, slight cause and signs, no complications.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: when the quarters are well endowed
questions.explain: These four words carry four of the features in the verse.
questions.rule: अमर्मगः = not reaching vital spots; अनुपद्रवः = without complications; अल्प = slight; पादसंपदि = when the quarters are well endowed.

questions.q: How are देश and ऋतु joined in देशर्तु-?
optionExplain: That is the result for अ + अ, not for अ + ऋ.
Right: The final अ of देश with the ऋ of ऋतु becomes अर्, so देश + ऋतु is written देशर्तु.
ए is the result for अ + इ.
ओ is the result for अ + उ.
questions.explain: A short or long अ followed by ऋ becomes अर्: देश + ऋतु = देशर्तु.
questions.teaches: Before the vowel ऋ, a final अ joins it as अर् (देश + ऋतु = देशर्तु).

questions.q: Which is the right split of अमर्मगोऽल्प-?
optionExplain: ल्प is not a word; the ऽ stands for a dropped अ.
Two अ would join as आ (अमर्मगाल्प), not give ओऽ.
Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
A visarga after आ would not give ओ.
questions.explain: अमर्मगः (not reaching the vital spots) and अल्प (slight) are two words.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse give among the features?
optionExplain: Right: अमर्मगः.
Right: अनुपद्रवः.
Right: पादसंपदि.
The verse says the cause is slight.
The verse says पादसंपदि: the quarters are well endowed.
questions.explain: The verse gives no complications, not reaching the vital spots and well-endowed quarters; its causes are slight and the other factors unlike the disease.
questions.rule: Features: अमर्मग, अल्प-हेतु-लक्षण, अनुपद्रव, अतुल्य दूष्य-देश-ऋतु-प्रकृति, पादसंपद्.

questions.q: An invented line calls a disease अनल्पहेतुः, on the pattern of अनुपद्रवः. What does it say of the cause?
optionExplain: That would be अल्प, without the negative prefix.
The word negates 'slight'; it does not speak of knowing.
The word does not speak of effects.
Right: The negative prefix takes अन् before a vowel: अन् + अल्प, 'not slight'.
questions.explain: अनल्प = अन् + अल्प: the negative prefix before a vowel is अन्, as in अन् + उपद्रव = अनुपद्रव.
questions.rule: Negative prefix: अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अन् before a vowel (अनुपद्रव, अनल्प) and अ before a consonant (अमर्मग).

questions.q: In how much time does the verse say the easily curable disease is cured?
optionExplain: Right: The verse says कालेनाल्पेन साध्यते: it is cured in a short time.
That is said of another grade in the next verse.
The verse says it is cured.
No season is named for this.
questions.explain: The last words of the verse, कालेनाल्पेन साध्यते, give a short time.
questions.rule: Easily curable: cured in a short time.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: with a single doṣa and path
questions.explain: These four words describe the disease and its cure.
questions.rule: साध्यते = is cured; एकदोषमार्गः = with a single doṣa and path; सुखोपायः = having easy means; सुखसाध्यः = easy to cure.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'new' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नवः is 'new', one of the features of the easily curable disease.
questions.teaches: नव, 'new', describes the disease as recent: नवः सुखः means 'new and easy'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ग्रहेष्वनुगुणेषु?
optionExplain: नुगुणेषु is not a word.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: ग्रहेषु + अनुगुणेषु → ग्रहेष्वनुगुणेषु.
ग्रहेषो is not a form on the card: the word is the locative plural ग्रहेषु, 'in the planets'.
Again नुगुणेषु is not a word; अनुगुण (favourable) begins with अ.
questions.explain: Both words are locative plural: 'in the planets' and 'favourable', agreeing as 'with the planets favourable'.

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The first line gives the planets, then the single doṣa and path, then new, then easy.
questions.rule: Line 1: favourable planets · single doṣa and path · new · easy.

questions.q: An invented word दुःखसाध्यः is built like सुखसाध्यः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: That is सुखसाध्यः.
साध्य is 'to be cured', not 'cured by'.
Right: दुःख- is the opposite of सुख-: 'hard' where सुख- is 'easy'.
Nothing in the word says 'new'.
questions.explain: सुख- gives 'easy' and the opposite दुःख- gives 'hard': सुखसाध्य is easy to cure, दुःखसाध्य hard to cure.
questions.rule: सुख-साध्य = easy to cure; दुःख-साध्य = hard to cure.
questions.teaches: A first member सुख- makes a word 'easy to ...' (सुखसाध्य, सुखोपाय); its opposite दुःख- makes it 'hard to ...'.

questions.q: Compared with the easily curable disease, how much time does this verse give for the kṛcchra disease?
optionExplain: That belongs to the easily curable disease.
The verse gives no such claim.
No length of days is given.
Right: The verse says चिरेण, after a long time.
questions.explain: चिरेण means after a long time; the easily curable disease is cured in a short time.
questions.rule: Kṛcchra: difficult and great means, long time.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the means and the time.
questions.rule: कृच्छ्रैः = difficult; महद्भिः = great; चिरेण = after a long time; शस्त्रादि = surgery and the like.

questions.q: What do the endings of कृच्छ्रैः and उपायैः (-ऐः) show?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural of अ-ending words.
The nominative singular of these words ends in -ः after अ, not -ऐः.
The locative plural ends in -एषु.
The genitive plural ends in -आनाम्.
questions.explain: कृच्छ्रैः उपायैः means 'by difficult means'; the two words agree in case and number.
questions.rule: -ऐः on an अ-ending word = instrumental plural, 'by'.
questions.teaches: The ending -ऐः on a masculine अ-ending word is instrumental plural: 'by ...s' (उपायैः = by means).

questions.q: Which is the right split of महद्भिश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: महद्भिः + च → महद्भिश्च.
महद्भिश is not a word.
भिश्च is not a word; the form is instrumental plural.
questions.explain: महद्भिः is instrumental plural of महत् ('great') and च means 'and'.

questions.q: Reading line 2 with the kṛcchra disease, as the card does, which of these does the verse say?
options: It is cured by difficult and great means
Its means are surgery and the like
It is cured in a short time
It is cured by easy means
optionExplain: Right: कृच्छ्रैरुपायैः ... महद्भिः.
Right: चिरेण.
Right: शस्त्रादिसाधनः.
That is said of the easily curable disease.
The means here are difficult and great.
questions.explain: The verse gives difficult and great means, a long time, and surgery and the like.
questions.rule: Kṛcchra: difficult and great means, long time, surgery and the like.

questions.q: An invented phrase सुखैरुपायैः is built like कृच्छ्रैरुपायैः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: That would be a genitive plural (-आनाम्).
That would be a locative plural (-एषु).
Right: सुखैः is instrumental plural of सुख, 'easy', agreeing with उपायैः.
That would be singular, not -ऐः.
questions.explain: Same ending, same meaning: 'by easy means' (सुखैः + उपायैः, visarga before a vowel becomes र्).
questions.teaches: Two words with the same ending -ऐः agree: सुखैः उपायैः = by easy means, as कृच्छ्रैः उपायैः = by difficult means.

questions.q: By what does the verse say the yāpya disease is kept going?
optionExplain: The verse names wholesome measures (पथ्यैः), not surgery.
Fate is not named in this verse; it names wholesome measures.
A slight cause is what makes it spread in the contrary case.
Right: The verse says पथ्यैः: by wholesome (things).
questions.explain: आयुषः शेषत्वात् पथ्यैः याप्यः: because life remains, it is kept going by wholesome measures.
questions.rule: Yāpya: kept going by wholesome measures.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two halves of the verse.
questions.rule: शेषत्वात् = because of remaining; पथ्यैः = by wholesome things; सुखम् = comfort; प्रतन्यते = is spread out.

questions.q: In शेषत्वात्, what does -त्व make out of the base word शेष (what is left)?
options: A noun of state: being what is left
optionExplain: Right: -त्व makes an abstract noun, and the ending -आत् then gives 'because of'.
-त्व does not make verbs.
A person-word would not end in -त्व.
-त्व has nothing to do with number.
questions.explain: शेषत्वात् = 'because of the state of being a remainder', i.e. because life remains.
questions.teaches: -त्व added to a word makes a noun of state (शेष → शेषत्व), and -आत् on it means 'because of'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पथ्यैर्याप्यः?
optionExplain: That would break याप्य, which begins with य.
Right: A visarga before a voiced consonant such as य becomes र्.
ऐर्याप्यः is not a word.
पथ्यैरि is not a word.
questions.explain: पथ्यैः (by wholesome things) and याप्यः (the yāpya disease) are the two words.

questions.q: What does the verse say in its second line of the yāpya disease?
options: It spreads on account of a slight cause
It is cured in a short time
optionExplain: Right: दत्त्वा सुखम् अल्पम्.
Right: अल्पेन हेतुना प्रतन्यते.
The verse says slight (अल्पम्).
That is said of the easily curable disease.
Surgery is the means of the kṛcchra disease in the previous verse.
questions.explain: The second line gives slight comfort, then spreading on account of a slight cause.
questions.rule: Line 2: slight comfort, then spreading by a slight cause.

questions.q: By the pattern of पथ्यैः (by wholesome things), what would an invented अपथ्यैः mean?
optionExplain: That is पथ्यैः.
A genitive plural would end in -आनाम्.
Right: The negative prefix अ- reverses पथ्य; -ऐः is the instrumental plural.
A locative plural would end in -एषु.
questions.explain: अ + पथ्य = unwholesome; with -ऐः it is 'by unwholesome things'.
questions.rule: अ- + noun = not that noun; -ऐः = by.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix अ- reverses a word (पथ्य → अपथ्य), and -ऐः keeps the instrumental plural 'by ...s'.

questions.q: In the verse's comparison, the patient is held up like one falling. By what?
optionExplain: The verse names the person's fixed lifespan, but not as what holds him up.
Fate is not named in this verse.
Past action is the source of the disease, not the support.
Right: The verse says विष्कम्भैः धार्यते हितैः: held up by wholesome things, as by props.
questions.explain: The comparison is with a falling person or thing held by props; the props are the wholesome things.
questions.rule: Patient held up by wholesome things, like a falling one by props.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the comparison.
questions.rule: रोगः = disease; आतुरः = patient; हितैः = by wholesome things; विष्कम्भैः = by props.

questions.q: In नाशेषताम्, शेष means 'remainder'. What does अशेषता name?
options: The state of having no remainder
The state of having a remainder
optionExplain: Right: अ- negates शेष and -ता makes a noun of state.
The prefix अ- negates; it does not keep the remainder.
-ता makes a noun of state, not a person.
The word has nothing to do with action.
questions.explain: अशेषता = अ + शेष + ता, the state of no remainder, i.e. complete removal; the disease does not reach it.
questions.rule: अ + शेष + ता = state of no remainder.
questions.teaches: Noun of state = word + -ता; with अ- it names the lack: अशेषता, no remainder.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रपतन्निव?
optionExplain: निव is not a word.
Right: An ending -न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel: प्रपतन् + इव → प्रपतन्निव.
The participle ends in -न्, not -न.
न्निव is not a word.
questions.explain: प्रपतन् is a present participle, 'falling', and इव means 'as if'.
questions.rule: -न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say?
options: The disease is born of past action
The person has a fixed lifespan
The disease does not reach the state of no remainder
The disease is wholly removed by wholesome things
The person has no fixed lifespan
optionExplain: Right: कर्मजः.
Right: नियतायुषः.
Right: याति नाशेषताम्.
The verse says it does not reach no-remainder.
The verse says नियतायुः, fixed.
questions.explain: The disease is born of past action, in one of fixed life, and does not reach the state of no remainder.
questions.rule: Karmaja disease, fixed life, never a full removal.

questions.q: An invented sentence says गृहं प्रपतदिव स्तम्भैर्धार्यते. What does it say?
options: The house, once fallen, is rebuilt by pillars
The pillars are falling as if held by the house
The house, as if falling, is held up by pillars
optionExplain: Nothing says it has fallen or is rebuilt.
The instrumental स्तम्भैः marks the pillars as the holders.
Right: प्रपतत् इव is 'as if falling', and स्तम्भैः धार्यते is 'is held up by pillars'.
स्तम्भैः धार्यते says it is held by them.
questions.explain: The same comparison as the verse: something falling, held up by props or pillars.
questions.rule: X प्रपतन् इव Y-भिः धार्यते = X, as if falling, is held up by Y.
questions.teaches: A present participle with इव gives 'as if falling'; the instrumental names what holds it up.

questions.q: How does the verse say the incurable disease is to be treated?
optionExplain: The verse says it goes beyond all treatments, so none is tried first.
The verse says it goes beyond all treatments.
The verse says all treatments are passed over.
Right: The verse says प्रत्याख्येयः and उपेक्ष्यः: to be refused, to be disregarded.
questions.explain: The incurable disease passes beyond all treatments, so it is to be refused and disregarded.
questions.rule: Incurable: beyond all treatments, to be refused, to be disregarded.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four terms carry the verse's teaching.
questions.rule: असाध्यः = incurable; प्रत्याख्येयः = to be refused; उपेक्ष्यः = to be disregarded; क्रियाः सर्वाः = all treatments.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does a word like प्रत्याख्येयः express?
options: What ought to be done to it: 'to be refused'
The one who does it: 'the refuser'
optionExplain: Right: It is a gerundive: it says what should be done to the thing.
That would be a past participle.
That would be an agent noun.
That would be a present participle.
questions.explain: The gerundives प्रत्याख्येयः and उपेक्ष्यः tell what is to be done to the incurable disease.
questions.teaches: A gerundive (प्रत्याख्येय, उपेक्ष्य) says what is to be done to the thing: 'to be refused', 'to be disregarded'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of परोऽसाध्यः?
optionExplain: परो is not the word on the card: the word is परः, and ओऽ comes from अः + अ.
Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
Two अ would join as आ (परासाध्यः).
परा + असाध्यः would give परासाध्यः, not परोऽसाध्यः.
questions.explain: परः (the other) and असाध्यः (incurable) are two words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The first line names the incurable one, the treatments, 'to be refused' and 'goes beyond'.
questions.rule: Line 1: the other, incurable · all treatments · to be refused · goes beyond.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: On the pattern of तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः, an invented line joins तस्मात् + आतुरः. How is it written?
optionExplain: त् stays त only before a hard consonant, not before a vowel.
The two आ do not stay apart in this way.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel.
न् would come only before a nasal.
questions.explain: Before a vowel the final त् of तस्मात् becomes द्, as in तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: तस्मात् + उपेक्ष्यः = तस्मादुपेक्ष्यः, तस्मात् + आतुरः = तस्मादातुरः.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does the verse say should be done before treatment is begun?
options: Ask the family for a decision
Give up the case at once
optionExplain: The verse puts the examination first (पुरा).
No such step is in the verse.
Giving up is not what the second line says.
Right: The verse says व्याधिं पुरा परीक्ष्य ... ततः क्रियाम्: examine, then begin treatment.
questions.explain: आरभेत ततः क्रियाम्: one begins treatment only then, after the examination.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each member of the first-line compounds to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the features listed in the first line.
questions.rule: भ्रमः = giddiness; मोहः = delusion; अरतिः = unease; रिष्टम् = fatal sign.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: परीक्ष्य comes from परि + ईक्ष्. Why does the 'having examined' form end in -य, not -त्वा?
options: A verb with a prefix takes -य
A verb with a prefix takes -त्वा
optionExplain: Right: The 'having done' form takes -त्वा on a plain verb and -य on a verb with a prefix.
That is the rule for plain verbs, not those with a prefix.
-य marks 'having done', not the future.
-य here marks 'having done'; the verb is active.
questions.explain: परि + ईक्ष् has a prefix (परि), so 'having examined' is परीक्ष्य.
questions.teaches: The 'having done' form is -त्वा after a plain verb and -य after a verb with a prefix (परि + ईक्ष् → परीक्ष्य).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of परीक्ष्यैवम्?
optionExplain: ऐवम् is not a word.
Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ: परीक्ष्य + एवम् → परीक्ष्यैवम्.
वम् is not a word.
परीक्ष्ये is not a form on the card (the word is परीक्ष्य), and ए + ए would not join as ऐ.
questions.explain: परीक्ष्य (having examined) and एवम् (thus) are the two words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: the disease, first, having examined thus, one should begin, then treatment.
questions.rule: Line 2: disease · first · having examined thus · should begin · then treatment.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says रोगं निरीक्ष्य चिकित्सेत्. What does निरीक्ष्य express?
options: While he is looking at it
optionExplain: That would be a present participle.
That would be a gerundive.
Right: निरीक्ष्य is the 'having done' form of a prefixed verb.
That would be a past participle or agent noun.
questions.explain: As in परीक्ष्य ... आरभेत, the action in -य comes first and the main verb follows.
questions.rule: -य form = 'having done', done before the main verb.
questions.teaches: A -य form names an earlier action: रोगं निरीक्ष्य चिकित्सेत्, 'having looked at the disease, one should treat'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What three losses does the verse say the physician would incur otherwise?
optionExplain: These are not named in the verse.
The verse names his own interest, knowledge and fame.
None of these is named.
Right: The verse says स्वार्थविद्यायशोहानिम्: loss of own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.explain: The compound स्वार्थविद्यायशोहानिम् means loss of one's own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.rule: Loss of own interest, knowledge and fame.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each member of the verse's first compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the compound of the first line.
questions.rule: स्वार्थः = own interest; विद्या = knowledge; यशः = fame; हानिः = loss.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: In अबलिनः, what does the prefix अ- do to बलिन् (a strong one)?
optionExplain: Right: अ- is the negative prefix, so अबलिन् is 'one who is not strong'.
अ- does not make a word stronger.
अ- here is not a tense mark.
अ- carries no number.
questions.explain: संयोगः अबलिनः means 'the combination in a weak person'.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates the word it stands before: बलिन् strong → अबलिन् weak.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of संयोगोऽबलिनः?
optionExplain: That would be 'of the strong', without the dropped अ.
Right: The ऽ marks a dropped अ, so the second word is अबलिनः, 'of the weak'.
Two अ would join as आ; ओऽ comes from a visarga.
A final आ would not give ओऽ.
questions.explain: संयोगः (combination) and अबलिनः (in a weak person).
questions.rule: -अः + अ → ओऽ; the ऽ is the dropped अ.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say?
options: Otherwise the physician would incur loss
The combination of two curable diseases, in a weak person, goes to incurability
Two curable diseases always stay curable
The loss is only possible, not sure
optionExplain: Right: अन्यथा ... हानिम् आप्नुयात्.
Right.
Right: यशोहानिम्.
The verse says even two curable ones can go to incurability.
The verse says ध्रुवम्, surely.
questions.explain: The verse says the loss is sure and names fame; two curable diseases in a weak person can go to incurability.
questions.rule: Sure loss; two curable diseases in a weak person → incurable.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of साध्ययोः, 'of two curable ones', what does an invented रोगयोः संयोगः mean?
optionExplain: -योः is not singular.
-योः is not plural.
Right: -योः is the dual: 'of two'.
रोगयोः names two diseases, not two combinations.
questions.explain: साध्ययोः = of two curable ones; likewise रोगयोः = of two diseases.
questions.teaches: The ending -योः on an अ-ending word is dual (genitive): साध्ययोः 'of two curable ones', रोगयोः 'of two diseases'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse says one meeting is to be known as incurable only. Which meeting?
options: Of a disease and a season
Of a curable disease and a physician
Of a curable and an incurable disease
optionExplain: The verse names the meeting of a curable and an incurable one, not of two curable ones.
No such meeting is named.
No such meeting is named.
Right: The verse says साध्यासाध्यसमागमम्: the meeting of curable and incurable.
questions.explain: The meeting of a curable and an incurable disease is to be known as incurable.
questions.rule: Curable + incurable meeting → know it as incurable.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in the second line.
questions.rule: साध्यः = the curable one; असाध्यः = the incurable one; याति = goes; असाध्यताम् = to incurability.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse's word for 'curability' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: साध्यताम् is साध्य + ता, the state of being curable, here the goal of याति 'goes to'.
questions.teaches: -ता makes a noun of state (साध्य → साध्यता), and याति takes the state it goes to in the accusative.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्वसाध्यताम्?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: तु + असाध्यताम् → त्वसाध्यताम्.
त्व is not a word here; तु is the word 'but'.
That drops the negative अ and reverses the sense.
त्वा is not the word before the ending.
questions.explain: तु (but) and असाध्यताम् (to incurability): the curable one but does go to incurability.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A student writes: 'An incurable disease can become curable, but a curable one cannot become incurable.' Which correction matches the verse?
options: Each of the two can become the other
Only the curable can become incurable
Neither of the two can become the other
The sentence is already right as it stands
optionExplain: The verse allows only one direction.
Right: The verse says नासाध्यः साध्यतां याति, साध्यो याति त्वसाध्यताम्.
The curable one does go to incurability.
It reverses the verse.
questions.explain: The verse allows the change only from curable to incurable.
questions.rule: Incurable → curable: never. Curable → incurable: yes.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says न रिक्तः पूर्णतां याति, पूर्णस्तु रिक्ततां याति. What does it say?
options: The empty becomes full, but the full does not become empty
Both the empty and the full become full
The empty does not become full, but the full becomes empty
Neither the empty nor the full changes
optionExplain: The न is on the first half.
The second half has रिक्ततां, 'to emptiness'.
Right: It follows the verse's pattern: न ... याति, X तु ... याति.
The second half says the full does go to emptiness.
questions.explain: As in the verse: one change is denied (न ... याति), the other is affirmed with तु.
questions.rule: न X Y-तां याति, Y तु X-तां याति = X does not become Y, but Y becomes X.
questions.teaches: The pattern 'न A B-तां याति, B तु A-तां याति' gives a one-way rule: A never reaches the state of B, but B does reach the state of A.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse names two things from which diseases pass into another state. Which two?
options: Season, place and the patient's age
Age, sex and the strength of the patient
Mismanagement of the quarters, and fate
optionExplain: These are not named as the causes here.
These are not named in the verse.
These are not named in the verse.
Right: The verse says पादापचारात् दैवात् च.
questions.explain: पादापचारात् (from mismanagement of the quarters) and दैवात् (from fate).
questions.rule: Diseases change state through पाद-अपचार and दैव.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four main words of the first line.
questions.rule: पादापचारात् = from mismanagement of the quarters; दैवात् = from fate; गदाः = diseases; अवस्थान्तरम् = another state.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What does the ending -आत् in दैवात् show?
optionExplain: Right: -आत् on an अ-ending word is the ablative: 'from, because of'.
The instrumental singular ends in -एन.
The locative singular ends in -ए.
The accusative singular ends in -म्.
questions.explain: दैवात् and पादापचारात् are both ablative: the sources of the change.
questions.teaches: The ending -आत् on an अ-ending word is the ablative singular: 'from, because of' (दैवात् = from fate).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of यान्त्यवस्थान्तरम्?
optionExplain: वस्थान्तरम् is not a word.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: यान्ति + अवस्थान्तरम् → यान्त्यवस्थान्तरम्.
यान्तु is another verb form ('let them go') and उ would become व्, not य्; the card's word is यान्ति.
That drops the इ of the verb.
questions.explain: यान्ति (they go) and अवस्थान्तरम् (to another state).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse's second line (an unfinished sentence) in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: better, the venom of a venomous snake, a blazing fire, or else too.
questions.rule: Line 2: better · snake venom · blazing fire · or else too.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line joins कालात् + च. How is it written?
optionExplain: The two sounds are not left unjoined.
द् is for a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्, as in दैवात् + च → दैवाच्च.
श्च comes from a visarga, not from त्.
questions.explain: The same rule as दैवात् + च = दैवाच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च्: दैवात् + च = दैवाच्च, कालात् + च = कालाच्च.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The editors mark a verse's Sanskrit as garbled. What is the safest use of its translation?
options: Use it like the translation of a clear verse
Keep the longer of two translations
Always prefer the Hindi over the English
Do not rely on it for any claim
optionExplain: A clear verse has a firm reading; a damaged one does not.
Length does not make a guess right.
Both translations here disagree and are guesses.
Right: A translation of damaged words can only be a guess.
questions.explain: Where the text is damaged, the translation cannot be firmer than the text.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each item to what the card says about it.
pairs: flagged as damaged by the editors
questions.explain: The card gives only what is plain: what is flagged, what disagrees, and which words are unclear.
questions.rule: Both lines are flagged; the book's two translations disagree; line 1 has unclear words रूपेणाञ्जनात् and line 2 has परोक्षभूतवैद्याधर्म.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A sentence begun in verse 36 runs into this damaged unit. Can the unit say what is 'better' than what?
options: No; the objects cannot be recovered
Yes; the English translation says it plainly
Yes; the Hindi translation says it plainly
Yes; the legible words give the whole sentence
optionExplain: Right: The damaged words hide the objects, so the sentence cannot be completed.
The book's English is itself a guess.
The book's Hindi is itself a guess and disagrees with the English.
The legible words are too few to complete it.
questions.explain: The card says the sentence from verse 36 runs into this unit, but what is better than what cannot be recovered.
questions.rule: Do not complete a sentence from a damaged line.
questions.teaches: A sentence that runs into a damaged line is left unfinished: the missing part is not filled in by guessing.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which statement about this unit is safe to learn?
options: The verse lists the duties of a pupil
Both lines are damaged, so no meaning is fixed
The verse gives a clear rule for choosing a teacher
The verse praises refusing every patient
optionExplain: Nothing legible says this.
Right: This is what the card says.
Nothing legible says this.
Nothing legible says this.
questions.explain: The two translations point different ways, so neither can be learnt as the verse's meaning.
questions.rule: Safe: the lines are damaged; no meaning is fixed.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which of these may a student safely do with this unit?
options: Note that the editors flagged both lines
Treat the two translations as guesses
Not quote it as a teaching
Memorise the English as the verse's meaning
Quiz others on what रूपेणाञ्जनात् means
optionExplain: Right: this is a fact about the text.
Right: they disagree.
Right: nothing here is firm.
The English is only a guess.
The word is marked unclear.
questions.explain: The safe uses are facts about the damage; the meaning itself is not known.
questions.rule: Note the damage; do not teach a meaning.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A student meets another garbled line whose two translations disagree. What should a quiz built on it do?
options: Use the translation that fits one's guess
Ask nothing that depends on the damaged words
Teach the damaged words as a rule
optionExplain: A guess does not make a firm reading.
Length is not evidence.
Right: A question can rest only on what is plain.
A rule cannot rest on unclear words.
questions.explain: The same care as here: only the plain facts are used, and the unclear part is left out.
questions.rule: Damaged line: no question, no rule rests on it.
questions.teaches: Where a line is damaged and its translations disagree, a quiz asks nothing that depends on the unclear words.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The verse says the one with his purpose accomplished does what to 'everything' (सर्वम्)?
optionExplain: The verb is अतिवर्त्तते, goes beyond, not give up.
No fear is named.
The verb does not mean collect.
Right: The verse says स सर्वमतिवर्त्तते: he surpasses everything.
questions.explain: अतिवर्त्तते means goes beyond or surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four main words of the line.
questions.rule: वर्त्तते = conducts himself; सिद्धार्थः = with purpose accomplished; सर्वम् = everything; अतिवर्त्तते = surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: In अतिवर्त्तते, what does the prefix अति- add to वर्त्तते, 'conducts himself'?
optionExplain: Right: अति- means beyond or over, so अति + वृत् is 'goes beyond'.
Going back is a different prefix.
Together is another prefix.
Not is अ-, not अति-.
questions.explain: अति + वर्त्तते = goes beyond, which the verse applies to everything.
questions.teaches: The prefix अति- gives 'beyond, over': अति + वर्त्तते = goes beyond, surpasses.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of सिद्धार्थः?
optionExplain: The first member is सिद्ध, ending in short अ.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: सिद्ध + अर्थः → सिद्धार्थः.
आर्थः is not a word here.
इ + अ would give सिद्ध्यर्थः.
questions.explain: सिद्ध (accomplished) and अर्थ (purpose): 'one whose purpose is accomplished'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these phrases of the verse in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: conducts himself, who, purpose accomplished, he everything, surpasses.
questions.rule: Order: वर्त्तते · यः तु · सिद्धार्थः · सः सर्वम् · अतिवर्त्तते.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: On the pattern of सिद्धार्थः, what does an invented गतभयः mean?
optionExplain: The first member is the participle 'gone', not 'goes to'.
That would be an agent noun.
Right: A past participle plus a noun, as सिद्ध + अर्थ, names a person with that feature.
The compound describes a person.
questions.explain: गत (gone) + भय (fear) = one whose fear has gone, as सिद्ध + अर्थ = one whose purpose is accomplished.
questions.teaches: A past participle followed by a noun can describe a person: सिद्धार्थः 'whose purpose is accomplished', गतभयः 'whose fear has gone'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What name does the closing line give to chapter 2?
optionExplain: The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
The closing line names शिष्योपनयनीय, not this word.
Right: The line says इति शिष्योपनयनीयो नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः.
questions.explain: The chapter is named शिष्योपनयनीय, 'on the initiation of the student'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in the line.
questions.rule: इति = thus; नाम = named; द्वितीयः = second; शिष्योपनयनीयः = the chapter's name.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायः is the chapter, the unit that the colophon closes.
questions.teaches: अध्यायः, 'chapter', is what the colophon names with its number: द्वितीयः अध्यायः, the second chapter.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of द्वितीयोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ; the अ then drops and is marked ऽ.
ध्यायः is not a word; the ऽ stands for the dropped अ.
Two अ would join as आ (द्वितीयाध्यायः).
A final आ would not give ओऽ.
questions.explain: द्वितीयः (second) and अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Arrange these words of the closing line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line goes: thus, Śiṣyopanayanīya, named, second, chapter.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line says इति रसीयो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः (षष्ठ = sixth). What does it say?
options: Thus the fifth chapter, named Rasīya
Thus the sixth chapter, named Rasīya
Thus the sixth verse, named Rasīya
Now the sixth chapter begins, named Rasīya
optionExplain: षष्ठ is sixth, not fifth.
Right: It follows the colophon pattern: इति, the name, नाम, the number, अध्यायः.
अध्यायः is a chapter, not a verse.
इति is 'thus', closing, not 'now'.
questions.explain: The pattern is इति + name + नाम + ordinal + अध्यायः, as in the verse.
questions.rule: इति X नाम N-ः अध्यायः = thus the Nth chapter, named X.
questions.teaches: A colophon reads इति + the name + नाम + the ordinal + अध्यायः: 'thus the ... chapter, named ...'.
questions.section: असाध्य रोग और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What is the subject announced in the opening formula of chapter 3?
options: The chapter on the pupil's duty
The chapter on the daily routine
The chapter on the six tastes
optionExplain: That is a different chapter title; not named here.
Not named in this formula.
Right: दिनचर्याध्यायं: the chapter on the daily routine (dinacaryā).
Not named in this formula.
questions.explain: The formula names the daily routine as the subject.
questions.rule: अथातो दिनचर्याध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः: अब दिनचर्या का अध्याय समझाएँगे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the three parts of the formula in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the opening words, then the subject, then the verb.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of the formula to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words give: now, therefore, the chapter on the daily routine, we shall explain.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; दिनचर्याध्याय = chapter on the daily routine; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The formula is made of अथ (now), अतः (therefore), the object, and a future verb in the first person plural.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of अथातो is right?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here; the आ comes from two अ.
आतः is not the word; the card reads अतः, therefore.
That would leave ओ in the middle; the ओ is only the changed visarga.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, and the visarga after अ becomes ओ before the voiced द: अथातो.
questions.explain: अथातः comes from अथ + अतः.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; ः + voiced consonant (after अ) → ओ.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: What does the form व्याख्यास्यामः say about the speaker?
options: You must explain it to us
optionExplain: Right: 1st person plural future: we shall explain.
That would be third person singular, past.
That would be a command to someone else.
That would be singular and present.
questions.explain: The card labels व्याख्यास्यामः as 1 pl. future.
questions.rule: व्याख्यास्यामः = हम समझाएँगे (उत्तम पुरुष, बहुवचन, भविष्यत्).
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of दिनचर्याध्यायम्, what does ऋतुचर्याध्यायम् mean?
options: Chapter on the season of the routine
Chapter on the routine by season
optionExplain: The first member names the subject, not the season of something.
Right: X-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on the routine of X; here X is ऋतु, season.
चर्या is routine, not teaching.
That would be दिनचर्या, with दिन, day.
questions.explain: दिन-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on the daily routine, so ऋतु-चर्या-अध्याय is the chapter on routine by season.
questions.rule: X-चर्याध्याय = chapter on the routine of X.
questions.teaches: In X-चर्या-अध्याय the first member X says what the routine follows or concerns.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: At what time does verse 2 say a healthy person should rise?
options: At noon, when the sun is high
optionExplain: The verse names no meal time.
Not named in this verse.
Right: ब्राह्मे मुहूर्त्ते उत्तिष्ठेत्: one should rise at the Brāhma muhūrta.
The verse names no such time.
questions.explain: The verse names the Brāhma muhūrta, taken as the pre-dawn period.
questions.rule: स्वस्थ व्यक्ति ब्राह्म मुहूर्त में उठे.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: rise, examining digestion. Line 2: for the protection of life, the healthy one voids when the urge has arisen.
questions.rule: उठना → जीर्ण-अजीर्ण का विचार → आयु की रक्षा के लिए → स्वस्थ → वेग होने पर त्याग.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two optative verbs (should rise, should void), one participle (examining) and two nouns for the person.
questions.rule: उत्तिष्ठेत् / समुत्सृजेत् = विधि (should); निरूपयन् = examining; जातवेगः = urge arisen.
questions.teaches: The optative ending -एत् gives 'one should ...'; a participle in -न् says 'doing ... meanwhile'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of रक्षार्थमायुषः is right?
optionExplain: मायुषः is not a word; the म् belongs to अर्थम्.
युषः is not a word here.
That doubles the म्; the म् is single.
Right: The final म् of अर्थम् joins the vowel आ that follows.
questions.explain: रक्षार्थम् (रक्षा-अर्थम्, for the protection) + आयुषः (of life).
questions.rule: म् + स्वर: म् साथ का स्वर पकड़ लेता है: अर्थम् + आयुषः → अर्थमायुषः.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: A healthy person finds the urge has arisen. What does verse 2 say?
options: He should void it, to protect life
He should hold it back, to protect life
He should wait until the evening meal
He should first rise, then forget it
optionExplain: Right: जातवेगः समुत्सृजेत्, रक्षार्थमायुषः.
The verse says to void it, not to hold it back.
No such wait is mentioned.
The verse gives no such instruction.
questions.explain: The verse joins jāta-vega with samutsṛjet: when the urge has arisen, void.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of जीर्णाजीर्णे निरूपयन् (dual objects), what does सुखदुःखे निरूपयन् mean?
optionExplain: The dvandva names both members, सुख and दुःख.
Right: A dual dvandva as object of the participle, as जीर्णाजीर्णे.
निरूपयन् is the one doing the examining, not the object.
The ending -न् is a present participle, not 'having examined'.
questions.explain: Two names joined into one dual word are both objects of 'examining'.
questions.rule: A dvandva in the dual (-ए, neuter) names two things together.
questions.teaches: A dvandva of two items ending in the dual can be the object of a participle: 'examining A and B'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: In verse 3, which direction is faced at night when voiding?
optionExplain: North is the first direction (उदङ्मुखः), not the night one.
East is not named in this verse.
Right: दक्षिणाभिमुखो निशि: facing south at night.

questions.rule: उदङ्मुख = उत्तर; दक्षिणाभिमुख निशि = रात में दक्षिण.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.explain: Both directions are bahuvrīhi compounds ending in -मुख.

questions.teaches: A direction word + मुख (or अभिमुख) is a bahuvrīhi: 'one whose face is toward that direction'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of संवीताङ्गोऽवगुण्ठितः is right?
optionExplain: वगुण्ठितः is not a word; the ऽ stands for the अ of अवगुण्ठितः.

Right: अः + अ gives ओ with the avagraha ऽ marking the dropped अ.
questions.explain: संवीताङ्ग + अवगुण्ठित: the visarga turns into ओ, the अ is marked by ऽ.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which describes voiding at night, by verse 3?

questions.q: By the pattern of उदङ्मुखः, what does पश्चिमाभिमुखः mean?

questions.teaches: A direction word + (अभि)मुखः names the person facing that direction; use it for any new direction.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.rule: प्रचलित वेग को निकलने दे; ज़ोर लगाकर न निकाले.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.explain: First the permitted act and its object, then the forbidden act.

questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.explain: बलात् + उदीरयेत् joins as बलादुदीरयेत्; with न तु it is a prohibition.
questions.rule: न तु + ablative + उदीरयेत् = but not by that means.
questions.teaches: A prohibition 'न तु X-आत् उदीरयेत्' forbids forcing something out by the means X.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the occasions of verse 9 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The list runs: bathing, wish to eat, eaten, slept, sneezed, worship of the gods, passing over a road.
questions.rule: स्नान → भोजन की इच्छा → भोजन → नींद → छींक → देवपूजा → मार्ग.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 9 to its meaning.
pairs: in the worship of the gods
questions.explain: Four of them are absolutives in -त्वा; the last is a locative.
questions.rule: -त्वा = having done; सुरार्चने = देवताओं की पूजा में.
questions.teaches: The ending -त्वा on a root says 'having done that', before the main verb.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which verb is hidden in the printed वा चामेत्?
optionExplain: चामेत् alone is not the card's verb.
च is not a separate 'and' here; the card reads वा + आचामेत्.
वाच is not a word of the card.
Right: आ + आ gives आ, so the long vowel hides the आ of आचामेत्.
questions.explain: The verb is आचामेत्, should sip (ā-√cam, optative).
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: On which occasions does verse 9 say one should sip water?
optionExplain: Right: क्षुत्वा.
Right: सुप्त्वा.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The list is exactly: bathing, wish to eat, eaten, slept, sneezed, worship, passing over a road.
questions.rule: आचमन के अवसर श्लोक की सूची तक सीमित.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of स्नात्वा, what does ज्ञात्वा mean?
optionExplain: Right: A root in -ā takes -त्वा: स्ना + त्वा, ज्ञा + त्वा: 'having done'.
-त्वा says 'having', not 'while'.
That would be an optative like ज्ञायात्, not -त्वा.
-त्वा is not a finite past verb.
questions.explain: ज्ञात्वा: having known, as स्नात्वा is having bathed.
questions.teaches: An absolutive in -त्वा says an act is finished before the main verb: 'having known'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which direction does verse 10 add with 'वा' (or)?
optionExplain: South is not named in this verse.
Right: प्राङ्मुखो वा: or facing east.
West is not named in this verse.
No upward direction is given.
questions.explain: The earlier unit gave north; this verse adds east.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 10 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: the direction and the place and gaze; line 2: speech and garment.
questions.rule: पूर्वमुख → एकान्त → दूसरी ओर न देखना → मौन → उत्तरीय.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अन्यदृक् is the negated feature (न अन्यदृक्).
questions.rule: प्राङ्मुख = east-facing; विविक्तस्थ = in a secluded place; अजल्पन् = not talking.
questions.teaches: Words such as अन्यदृक् (bahuvrīhi) and उत्तरासङ्गी (one having an upper garment) describe the person; न or अ- negates them.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of नान्यदृक् is right?
optionExplain: न्यदृक् is not a word.
आन्यदृक् is not the word of the card.
Right: अ + अ gives आ: not looking elsewhere.
यदृक् is not the word here.
questions.explain: नान्यदृक् = न + अन्यदृक्, not looking elsewhere.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which does verse 10 say about the one who sips?
options: He stays in a secluded place
optionExplain: Right: अजल्पन्.
Right: उत्तरासङ्गी.
Right: विविक्तस्थः.
The verse says not talking at all.
questions.explain: Three plain features: silence, upper garment, secluded place.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the pattern of अजल्पन्, what does अपश्यन् mean?
optionExplain: अ- negates; it does not intensify.
-न् is a present participle, not 'having'.
The अ- makes it a negation, 'not seeing'.
Right: अ- + the present participle -न्: not doing it.
questions.explain: अ + पश्यन् = not seeing, like अ + जल्पन् = not talking.
questions.teaches: A negative अ- on a present participle in -न् says 'not doing it'.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which waters does verse 11 forbid?
options: Waters that reach the thumb's base
optionExplain: Right: नाग्निपक्कैः: not with waters heated by fire.
Clean waters are the ones required in verse 10.
That is the requirement of verse 10.
The verse forbids offering with one hand; it does not mention both hands.
questions.explain: The forbidden waters include those heated by fire.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Put the four clear kinds of forbidden waters in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First fire-heated and foul-smelling, then foam-bubble-alkaline, then offered with one hand.
questions.rule: आग पर पके → दुर्गन्धयुक्त → झाग-बुलबुले-क्षार → एक हाथ से दिए.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 11 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear qualities of the forbidden waters.
questions.rule: अग्निपक्क = fire-heated; पूति = foul-smelling; फेन = foam; क्षार = alkaline; एकहस्तार्पित = one-hand-offered.
questions.teaches: A water is described by an adjective in the instrumental plural: न X-ऐः जलैः, not with waters having X.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which split of नैकहस्तार्पितैः is right?
optionExplain: ऐकहस्त is not the word; the ऐ is the joined sound.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ: न + एक → नैक.
इकहस्त is not a word.
कहस्त is not a word here.
questions.explain: न (not) + एकहस्तार्पितैः (offered with one hand).
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which waters does verse 11 name as not to be used?
optionExplain: Right: पूतिभिः.
Right: फेन.
Right: अग्निपक्कैः.
Clean waters are the ones asked for in verse 10.
questions.explain: The verse's clear prohibitions are fire-heated, foul, foamy-bubbly-alkaline and one-hand-offered waters.
questions.rule: वर्जित जल: पक्क, पूति, फेनादि, एकहस्तार्पित.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: By the verse's pattern, what does न पङ्कतृणैर्जलैः mean?
options: Only with waters having mud and straw
Not for waters having mud and straw
Not with waters having mud and straw
Not toward waters having mud and straw
optionExplain: The न forbids; it does not allow only these.
-ैः is 'with', not 'for'.
Right: A dvandva in the instrumental plural qualifies जलैः, as फेनबुद्बुदक्षारैः.
प्रति would be needed for 'toward'.
questions.explain: पङ्क and तृण are joined as a dvandva in the instrumental plural, describing the waters.
questions.rule: न + instrumental plural with जलैः = not with waters of that kind.
questions.teaches: An adjective compound in the instrumental plural before जलैः says what the water is like; न forbids it.
questions.section: प्रातः उत्थान, मल-मूत्र त्याग और आचमन

questions.q: Which does line 1 of verse 12 forbid?
optionExplain: That is asked for in verse 10.
That is asked for in verse 10.
That is allowed in verse 10.
Right: न शब्दवान्: not making sound.
questions.explain: Line 1 forbids a wet hand, impure hands and feet, and making sound.

questions.q: Put the names of verse 12, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line lists vaṭa, asana, arka, khadira, karañja, kavīra.
questions.rule: वट → असन → अर्क → खदिर → करंज → कवीर.

questions.q: Match each phrase of verse 12, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each phrase is a person-describing word that the न rejects.
questions.rule: आर्द्रैकपाणि = one hand wet; अमेध्यहस्तपाद = impure hands and feet; शब्दवान् = making sound.
questions.teaches: The suffix -वान् means 'having': शब्दवान् is 'one having sound', that is, making sound.

questions.q: Which split of नार्द्रैकपाणिः is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ gives आ, and आ + ए gives ऐ.
That uses wrong parts; the card has आर्द्र and एक.
र्द्रैकपाणिः is not a word.
ऐकपाणिः is not a word; the ऐ is the joined sound.
questions.explain: न (not) + आर्द्र (wet) + एकपाणिः (one hand).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; आ + ए → ऐ.

questions.q: Which are forbidden in line 1 of verse 12?
optionExplain: Right: आर्द्रैकपाणिः.
Right: अमेध्यहस्तपादः.
Right: शब्दवान्.
The verse forbids impure ones, not clean.
questions.explain: The three forbidden states are all in line 1.
questions.rule: तीन निषेध: गीला एक हाथ, अपवित्र हाथ-पैर, शब्द.

questions.q: By the pattern of शब्दवान्, what does बलवान् mean?
optionExplain: -वान् does not negate.
Right: -वान् = having: बल + वान्.
The suffix names the one who has it, not the thing.
That is the meaning of शब्दवान्, not बलवान्.
questions.explain: बलवान् is the one who has strength, as शब्दवान् has sound.
questions.teaches: The suffix -वान् makes a word for 'one having X'.

questions.q: Which three tastes does verse 13 list?
optionExplain: None of these is named in the verse.
Sweet and salty are not named.
Right: कषायतिक्तकटुकम्: astringent, bitter, pungent.
Sour is not named.
questions.explain: The verse names three tastes in a dvandva.

questions.q: Put the parts of verse 13 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the names and what is born of them; then the tastes; then the last words, another root of this kind.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 13, line 2, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three taste words, then the thing and its qualifier.
questions.rule: कषाय = astringent; तिक्त = bitter; कटु = pungent; मूल = root; ईदृश = of this kind.
questions.teaches: Taste words are listed in a dvandva; ईदृश (of this kind) points back to the described type.

questions.q: Which split of मूलमन्यदपीदृशम् is right?
optionExplain: These pieces are not words.
दपीदृशम् is not a word.
यदपि and the rest do not fit the card's words.
Right: म्+अ, त्→द् before a vowel, and इ + ई gives ई.
questions.explain: The line reads: root, another, also, of this kind.
questions.rule: म् + स्वर, त् + स्वर → द्, इ + ई → ई.

questions.q: What else does verse 13 include besides the named ones?
options: Any other root of this kind
Only the bark of the trees
optionExplain: Right: मूलमन्यदपीदृशम्: another root also of this kind.
The verse adds 'another also'.
The verse says 'of this kind', not sweet.
Bark is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The last words widen the list to other roots of the same kind.

questions.q: By the pattern of कषायतिक्तकटुकम्, what does मधुरलवणम् name?
optionExplain: The dvandva lists both tastes, not one qualifying the other.
Right: A neuter dvandva of two taste words.
Neither word is the owner of the other.
The compound names both.
questions.explain: मधुर and लवण are two taste names joined.
questions.rule: A dvandva of taste words names the tastes together.
questions.teaches: Taste names can be joined in a dvandva to list several tastes at once.

questions.q: By verse 14, what is said of knots in the stick being described?
options: It has one at the tip
It has one at each end
It has a few small ones
optionExplain: The verse says nothing of a knot at the tip.
That is the opposite of अग्रन्थि.
Right: ऋज्वग्रन्थि: the stick is straight and without knots.
The word is अ-ग्रन्थि, without knots.
questions.explain: The verse calls the stick straight (ऋजु) and without knots (अग्रन्थि).

questions.q: Put these four items of verse 14, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: known taste, crushed tip, straight-and-knotless (ऋज्वग्रन्थि, two qualities), grown in good soil.
questions.rule: Line 1 has five qualities in this order; line 2 has three.

questions.q: The word for 'straight' in verse 14 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: ऋजु = straight, joined with अग्रन्थि as ऋज्वग्रन्थि (उ + अ → व).
questions.teaches: ऋजु means straight; before a vowel its final उ turns into व.

questions.q: Which split of कनीन्यग्रसमस्थौल्यम् starts correctly?
optionExplain: यग्र is not a word of the card.
That would join as कनीन्याग्र, with a long आ.
आ + अ would join as कनीनाग्र.
Right: ई before a vowel becomes य्: कनीनी + अग्र gives कनीन्यग्र.
questions.explain: कनीनी (little finger) + अग्र (tip) + सम (equal) + स्थौल्यम् (thickness).
questions.rule: ई + a vowel → य् + the vowel.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry five of the eight qualities of the list.

questions.q: By the same rule, how is नदी + अग्रम् written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: ई + अ gives य् + अ, as in कनीन्यग्र.
The अ of अग्रम् cannot simply vanish.
ई + अ does not give ए.
Only one य् is added, not two.
questions.explain: The rule of कनीनी + अग्र gives नदी + अग्रम् = नद्यग्रम्.
questions.rule: ई + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.teaches: A final ई before a different vowel becomes य् and the vowel follows.

questions.q: By the first line of verse 15, how is the stick chewed?
optionExplain: That is the opposite of यतवाक्.
Right: यतवाक् means one whose speech is held back.
No walking is mentioned in the verse.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: The word यतवाक् says the speech is restrained while chewing.

questions.q: Put the words of verse 15, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line reads: in the morning, having eaten, with speech restrained, one should chew the stick.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 15, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words make up the whole first line.
questions.teaches: भुक्त्वा ends in -त्वा and means having eaten: an action finished before the main verb.

questions.q: Which split of प्रातर्भुक्त्वा is right?
optionExplain: र्भुक्त्वा is not a word.
ओ comes only from अः, not from आः.
Right: Right: प्रातः stands for प्रातर्, and र् stays before the voiced भ: प्रातर्भुक्त्वा.
The word is भुक्त्वा, with भ.
questions.explain: प्रातः + भुक्त्वा gives प्रातर्भुक्त्वा.
questions.rule: प्रातः is from प्रातर्; a visarga that stands for र् shows as र् before a voiced sound (प्रातर् + भुक्त्वा).

questions.q: Which are named in the first line of verse 15?
options: Washing the eyes with cold water
optionExplain: Right: भक्षयेत् दन्तधावनम्.
Right: यतवाक्.
This comes in a later verse, not in this line.
This comes in a later verse, not in this line.
questions.explain: The line names chewing the stick and restrained speech.

questions.q: Which word means having bathed, made like भुक्त्वा?
optionExplain: That means to bathe.
That means the bath, a noun.
That means he bathes.
Right: Root स्ना + -त्वा gives having bathed.
questions.explain: भुक्त्वा = having eaten; in the same way स्नात्वा = having bathed.
questions.teaches: -त्वा added to a root gives 'having done', an action finished before the main verb.

questions.q: By verse 16, with what is the tongue scraped?
optionExplain: Right: जिह्वानिर्लेखनेन: with a tongue-scraper.
No nail is mentioned.
The stick is for the teeth in this verse.
No salt is mentioned.
questions.explain: The tongue is scraped with a जिह्वानिर्लेखन.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 16 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 is about the teeth and gums; line 2 is about the tongue.
questions.rule: Teeth and gums first, tongue after.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three of these words give the manner (शनैः, अबाधयन्, अनुसुखम्); two name what is treated (दन्तमांस, जिह्वा).
questions.teaches: शनैः and अनुसुखम् both ask for a gentle, comfortable manner.

questions.q: Which split of लिखेदनुसुखम् is right?
optionExplain: नुसुखम् is not a word.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel.
A visarga would give लिखेरनुसुखम्, not द्.
दनुसुखम् is not a word.
questions.explain: लिखेत् (one should scrape) + अनुसुखम् (comfortably).

questions.q: Which are said of the scraping of the tongue in verse 16?
options: It is done with a tongue-scraper
It is done with the mouth full of water
optionExplain: Right: अनुसुखम्.
Right: जिह्वानिर्लेखनेन.
The verse asks for the opposite, comfort.
That belongs to the eye-sprinkling of a later verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives two things: comfort and a tongue-scraper.

questions.q: How is तत् + अपि written when joined?
optionExplain: The two words are joined, not left apart.
थ does not come from त्.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a vowel, as in लिखेदनुसुखम्.
The final consonant is lost wrongly.
questions.explain: The rule of लिखेत् + अनुसुखम् gives तत् + अपि = तदपि.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel turns into द् and the vowel joins it.

questions.q: Which three things does verse 17 say do arise?
optionExplain: These are the ones that do not arise.
These are in the next verse, not here.
These are in a later verse, not here.
Right: रुचिवैशद्यलघुता भवन्ति: these three arise.
questions.explain: The three that arise are appetite (रुचि), clearness (वैशद्य) and lightness (लघुता).

questions.q: Put the three things that arise in verse 17 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The second line lists them in this order.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 17 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words name what does not arise; two name what does.
questions.teaches: The first list is of things that go away; the second is of things that come.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 17 say does NOT arise?
optionExplain: Right: It is in the first list, with न भवन्ति.
Appetite is in the list of what arises.
Clearness is in the list of what arises.
Lightness is in the list of what arises.
questions.explain: Dirt, bad taste, tongue odour and mouth-and-teeth troubles are the ones that do not arise.
questions.rule: First list: न भवन्ति; second list: भवन्ति.

questions.q: In verse 17, which verb goes with रुचि, वैशद्य and लघुता?
optionExplain: न भवन्ति goes with the first list.
Right: Right, from the sense (the card's reading): they arise.
Then the verse would contradict itself.
Each list needs a verb, and the card gives one to each.
questions.explain: The card pairs the first verb with the first list and the second verb with the second list.
questions.rule: The pairing of verbs and lists is an inference from the sense.

questions.q: What does the compound शीतोष्णम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be a genitive compound, not a list.
No word for 'without' is present.
Right: A compound of items joined by 'and', like रुचि-वैशद्य-लघुता.
No comparison word is present.
questions.explain: शीत + उष्ण in one word: cold and heat.
questions.rule: A series of items can be packed into one compound meaning A and B (and C).
questions.teaches: A compound can list items in one word, as रुचिवैशद्यलघुता lists appetite, clearness and lightness.

questions.q: Who is told in verse 18 not to chew the stick?
optionExplain: A fracture is not named in the verse.
Leprosy is not named in the verse.
Hiccups are not named in the verse.
Right: ज्वर is named in the list.
questions.explain: The list includes the one with fever (ज्वर).
questions.rule: Named: अजीर्ण, वमथु, श्वास, कास, ज्वर, अर्दित, तृष्णा, आस्यपाक, हृदय-नेत्र-शिर-कर्ण रोग.

questions.q: Put the six troubles of verse 18, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists these six in this order.
questions.rule: अजीर्ण, वमथु, श्वास, कास, ज्वर, अर्दित.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the troubles are plain words.
questions.teaches: The verse names troubles; the card gives each name its plain meaning and no more.
