questions.teaches: A word in -त्वा (भुक्त्वा) means 'having done' and names an action finished before the next one.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वर्गापवर्गविभवान्?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ gives आ, so स्वर्ग + अपवर्ग is written स्वर्गापवर्ग.
पवर्ग is not the word here; the word is अपवर्ग.
A visarga before अ would give -ोऽ, not -ा.
The second word is अपवर्ग, liberation, not आपवर्ग.
questions.explain: स्वर्ग + अपवर्ग + विभवान् is the split on either reading (three items, or 'prosperities of heaven and liberation').
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: स्वर्ग + अपवर्ग = स्वर्गापवर्ग.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which are said of the evening meal or the eater in line 2?
options: the eater has a composed mind
the meal is eaten at dawn
optionExplain: Right: लघु.
Right: हितम्.
Right: समाहितमनाः.
The line says light, लघु, not heavy.
The line says सायम्, in the evening.
questions.explain: Line 2 says the meal is light and wholesome, taken in the evening, by one with composed mind who is pure.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: By the pattern of भुक्त्वा (having eaten), which word means having read (from पठ्)?
optionExplain: This is 'reads' (present), not 'having read'.
Right: A verb without prefix forms 'having done' with -त्वा (here -इत्वा).
This is 'read' in the past (imperfect), not 'having read'.
This is 'to be read' (a gerundive), not 'having read'.
questions.explain: भुक्त्वा = having eaten; in the same way पठ् gives पठित्वा.
questions.teaches: A verb without a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -त्वा (भुक्त्वा, पठित्वा).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: What does he do right before lying down on his own bed?
options: He bathes in the evening, before sleeping
He counts the two or three attendants
He spreads a soft pillow on the bed
optionExplain: Bathing is not mentioned in this unit.
The attendants are in line 2 as a feature of the place.
Right: शास्तारमनुसंस्मृत्य: having remembered the Instructor.
Nothing in this unit speaks of a pillow; that is in unit 121.
questions.explain: अनुसंस्मृत्य is 'having remembered': the remembering comes first, then संविशेत्, he should lie down.
questions.rule: Remember the Instructor, then lie down on his own bed.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: the Instructor, having remembered, own bed, and then, should lie down.
questions.rule: शास्तारम् · अनुसंस्मृत्य · स्वशय्याम् · च अथ · संविशेत्.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 2 describes the place and who is with him.
questions.rule: देशे = in a place; शुचौ = clean; अनाकीर्णे = not crowded; आप्त = trusted; परिचारकः = attendant.
questions.teaches: Words describing a place agree with it in case: देशे, शुचौ, अनाकीर्णे are all 'in' (locative) singular.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which is the right split of चाथ?
optionExplain: थ is not a word.
A visarga before अ would give -ोऽ.
आथ is not a word; the second word is अथ.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so च + अथ is written चाथ.
questions.explain: च (and) + अथ (then): the two अ join into आ.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: च + अथ = चाथ.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which are said of the place or the sleeper's company in this unit?
options: he has two or three trusted attendants
optionExplain: Right: शुचौ.
Right: अनाकीर्णे.
Right: द्वित्राप्तपरिचारकः.
No hill is mentioned.
No water is mentioned.
questions.explain: Line 2 says: a clean, uncrowded place, with two or three trusted attendants.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which phrase means in a clean village (ग्राम, masculine), built like देशे शुचौ?
optionExplain: Right: Noun and adjective both take the 'in' form, masculine singular.
Both are the object form (accusative), not 'in'.
Both mean 'by', not 'in'.
Both mean 'of', not 'in'.
questions.explain: देशे शुचौ = in a clean place; so ग्रामे शुचौ = in a clean village.
questions.rule: An adjective agrees with its noun in case, number, gender.
questions.teaches: An adjective takes the same case, number and gender as its noun (देशे शुचौ ; ग्रामे शुचौ).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: How high does the verse say the bed-and-seat should be?
optionExplain: The verse says knee, not waist.
Right: जानुतुल्यम् = equal to the knee.
The verse gives a knee-height.
The verse gives knee-height.
questions.explain: जानु is the knee and तुल्य is equal to: knee-high.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: knee-high, soft, auspicious, should use, bed-and-seat.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the qualities of the first line and the second.
questions.rule: युक्तोपधानम् = with a suitable pillow; स्वास्तीर्णम् = well spread; अविषमम् = even; मृदु = soft; सुखम् = comfortable.
questions.teaches: A letter अ in front of a word often gives its opposite: विषम (uneven) → अविषम (even).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: What does विस्तीर्णाविषमम् describe?
optionExplain: अविषम has the negative अ-, so it means not uneven.
विस्तीर्ण means wide, not narrow.
Right: विस्तीर्ण is wide and अविषम is even (not uneven).
Both parts are wrong: wide, and not uneven.
questions.explain: विस्तीर्ण (wide) + अविषम (not uneven, even).
questions.rule: अविषम = even, because अ- negates विषम.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which are said of the bed-and-seat in this unit?
optionExplain: Right: विस्तीर्ण.
Right: मृदु.
Right: जानुतुल्यम्.
The verse says wide.
The verse says soft.
questions.explain: The verse names wide, soft and knee-high; narrow and hard are the opposites.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Join सु + आगतम् (well come) in the way सु + आस्तीर्णम् is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: The two words are not left unjoined in this way.
That drops the आ and means something else, 'well gone'.
ओ is the result of अ + उ, not of उ + आ.
Right: उ becomes व् before a vowel, and व् + आ gives वा.
questions.explain: सु + आस्तीर्णम् = स्वास्तीर्णम्; so सु + आगतम् = स्वागतम्.
questions.teaches: Final उ before a different vowel becomes व् (सु + आस्तीर्णम् = स्वास्तीर्णम् ; सु + आगतम् = स्वागतम्).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Towards whom should the feet not be turned?
optionExplain: Right: पादावकुर्वाणो गुरून् प्रति: not turning the feet towards elders.
The attendants were in unit 120, not here.
The king comes later, in unit 125.
The deities are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: अकुर्वाणः = not doing; गुरून् प्रति = towards elders.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: in the first and last part of the night, dharma, only, should reflect.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two instructions of the verse.
questions.rule: पादौ = the two feet; गुरून् = elders; प्रति = towards; धर्मम् = dharma; एव = only.
questions.teaches: प्रति ('towards') stands after the noun it governs, which takes the object form: गुरून् प्रति.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which is the best rendering of पादावकुर्वाणो गुरून् प्रति?
options: Not turning the feet towards elders
Not turning the head towards elders
Turning the elders towards their feet
optionExplain: The अ- in अकुर्वाणः negates the action.
Right: अकुर्वाणः is the negative of कुर्वाणः, 'doing'.
The word is पादौ, feet.
The elders are the direction, not the thing turned.
questions.explain: पादौ (feet) + अकुर्वाणः (not doing, not putting) + गुरून् प्रति (towards elders).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Ravi lies down with his feet pointing towards his teacher. What does line 1 say?
options: He should turn his head that way
He should stop reflecting on dharma altogether
He should not turn his feet that way
He should leave the bed at once
optionExplain: The verse gives no rule about turning the head towards elders.
Line 2 tells him to reflect on dharma, not to stop; line 1 is about the feet.
Right: Feet not towards elders: पादावकुर्वाणो गुरून् प्रति.
Nothing in the verse says this.
questions.explain: Pointing the feet towards elders is what the participle phrase says not to do.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Join सत्यम् + एव + अनुचिन्तयेत् (reflect on truth alone) as धर्मम् एव अनुचिंतयेत् is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: The final म् joins the vowel एव; it is not doubled.
एव + अनु must join to एवानु.
The म् goes with the vowel that follows, so मे, not म + ए.
Right: म् joins the vowel after it, and एव + अनु gives एवानु.
questions.explain: धर्मम् + एव = धर्ममेव; एव + अनु = एवानु; same pattern for सत्यम्.
questions.rule: म् + vowel joins as म + vowel; अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel joins that vowel (धर्मम् + एव = धर्ममेव), and अ + अ gives आ (एव + अनु = एवानु).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: According to line 1, what should one take from the body?
optionExplain: Right: आददीत सदा ... सारम् असारतः: take the essence from the unsubstantial.
The verse names the essence, not pleasure.
The verse names the essence, not strength.
The verse names the essence, not sleep.
questions.explain: सारम् is the object of आददीत; it is taken from the body, which is असार.
questions.rule: Take the essence from what is without essence.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: should take, always, from the body, thus, essence, from the unsubstantial.
questions.rule: आददीत · सदा · देहात् · इत्थम् · सारम् · असारतः.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the main instruction and its time.
questions.rule: आददीत = should take; सदा = always; सारम् = essence; असारतः = from the unsubstantial; प्रतिक्षणम् = every moment.
questions.teaches: The negative अ- gives the opposite (सार → असार) and -तः can mean 'from' (असारतः).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which is the right split of देहादित्थम्?
optionExplain: दित्थम् is not a word; the द् belongs to the end of the first word.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: देहात् + इत्थम् = देहादित्थम्.
दित्थम् is not a word; the second word is इत्थम्, 'thus'.
A visarga before इ would drop, giving देह इत्थम्.
questions.explain: देहात् (from the body) + इत्थम् (thus).
questions.rule: Final त् + vowel → द्: देहात् + इत्थम् = देहादित्थम्.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: A student says, 'I will take the essence only on festival days.' Which word of line 1 disagrees?
optionExplain: देहात् only says from the body.
सारम् only names what is taken.
Right: सदा means always: not only on festival days.
इत्थम् only says in this way.
questions.explain: The instruction is for all times: सदा, always.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: By the pattern of असारतः (from the unsubstantial), which word means from the house (गृह)?
optionExplain: This is the object form, 'house'.
This is 'in the house'.
This is 'of the house'.
Right: A word with -तः can mean 'from', as असारतः does.
questions.explain: सार + तः (असारतः) means 'from the unsubstantial'; गृह + तः = गृहतः.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -तः can mean 'from' (असारतः, गृहतः), like the ablative form देहात्.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: What does line 2 say is declared for the one so endowed?
options: A lifespan of exactly a hundred years
A lifespan free from all work
optionExplain: Right: सुखम् आयुः हितं च उक्तम्.
No number of years is in the line.
Nothing speaks of freedom from work.
The attendants are in unit 120, not here.
questions.explain: सुखम् (happy), आयुः (lifespan), हितम् (beneficial), उक्तम् (is declared).
questions.rule: Happy and beneficial life is declared.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Put the main words of line 2 in the order of the verse (leaving out च).
questions.explain: The line runs: happy, lifespan, beneficial, is declared, the opposite, in the contrary case.
questions.rule: सुखम् · आयुः · हितम् · उक्तम् · विपरीतम् · विपर्य्यये.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the words of the long compound and the first word of line 2.
questions.rule: आरोग्य = health; विभव = prosperity; प्रज्ञा = wisdom; सुखम् = happy; क्रियावतः = of one endowed with action.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -वत् ('having') names one endowed with what comes before: क्रियावतः = of one endowed with action.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: What does विपरीतं विपर्य्यये say?
options: The very same, in the contrary case
The opposite, in the contrary case
A longer one, in the very same case
The opposite, in the same case
optionExplain: विपरीत means opposite, not same.
Right: विपरीतम् = the opposite; विपर्य्यये = in the contrary case.
Nothing speaks of length here.
विपर्य्यये is 'in the contrary case', not the same one.
questions.explain: The line repeats the idea: opposite for the opposite condition.
questions.rule: विपरीतं विपर्य्यये = the opposite in the contrary case.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: Which three are named among what the person is endowed with in line 1?
optionExplain: Right: आरोग्य.
Right: विभव.
Right: प्रज्ञा.
Not named in the line.
Not named in the line.
questions.explain: The list starts with health, prosperity, wisdom (then age and action with dharma).
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: By the pattern of क्रियावतः (of one endowed with action), what does धनवतः mean?
options: Of one who is without any wealth
Of the wealth itself, not a person
From the wealth of the house
optionExplain: That would need a word like धनहीन.
The -वत् suffix names a person who has it.
Right: -वतः (from -वत्) means 'of one who has' what comes before.
'From' would be धनात् or धनतः.
questions.explain: धन (wealth) + -वतः = of one endowed with wealth.
questions.teaches: -वत् ('having') names the one who has what comes before: क्रियावतः, धनवतः.
questions.section: सायंकाल का भोजन, शयन और आयु

questions.q: How is the king described in line 1?
optionExplain: The deities are not mentioned in this unit.
Wealth is not what the line names.
The elders appear in unit 122, not here.
Right: सर्वतेजोनिधानम्: sarva-tejaḥ-nidhānam.
questions.explain: निधान = repository; सर्वतेजः = all splendour.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: not corrupting, the mind, therefore, devoted, him, should serve.
questions.rule: अदूषयन् · मनः · तस्मात् · भक्तिमान् · तम् · उपाचरेत्.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the reason and the instruction.
questions.rule: नृपः = king; भुवि = on earth; तस्मात् = therefore; भक्तिमान् = devoted; उपाचरेत् = should serve.
questions.teaches: -मान् (from -मत्) names one who has what comes before: भक्तिमान् = one who has devotion.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: The print runs नृप and इति together. Which is the right reading of नृपइति?
optionExplain: Right: नृपः + इति; the visarga drops before इ, so it is read नृप इति.
That would give नृपमिति.
That would be 'by the king' and would give नृपेणेति.
अइति is not a word.
questions.explain: नृपः (the king) + इति (thus): the sense is 'the king is called thus'.
questions.rule: Visarga after अ + vowel (not अ): visarga drops, vowels stay apart.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Why does the verse say one should serve the king with devotion?
options: Because he lives in a clean and uncrowded place with attendants
Because he is the repository of all splendour
Because he has two or three trusted attendants at his side
Because he is always fearing death at every moment
optionExplain: That is unit 120's bed-place; it is not the reason here.
Right: तस्मात् (therefore) links line 2 to the description in line 1.
That is unit 120; not the reason here.
Fear of death is unit 123 and is not about the king.
questions.explain: The reason is stated in line 1; तस्मात् draws the conclusion.
questions.rule: King = repository of splendour; therefore serve him.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of भक्तिमान् (one with devotion), which word means one with wealth (श्री)?
optionExplain: This means 'without wealth'.
This means 'of wealth'.
Right: -मान् names one who has what comes before.
This is the noun 'wealth' itself.
questions.explain: भक्ति + मान् = one with devotion; श्री + मान् = one with wealth.
questions.teaches: -मान् (from -मत्) names one who has what comes before (भक्तिमान्, श्रीमान्).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which verb of line 2 governs the whole list of line 1?
optionExplain: This is an adjective ('beyond the natural'), not a verb.
This is a noun ('movements'), not a verb.
This is 'should lie down', from unit 120.
Right: parivarjayet = should avoid; it is the only finite verb.
questions.explain: The line-1 list is a string of nouns; parivarjayet in line 2 is its verb.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put these items of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out कोपहास).
questions.explain: The list runs: paryastikā, support, quarrel, spitting, yawning (with कोपहास between support and quarrel).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each item to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the items of the list that read the same under both readings.
questions.rule: उपाश्रय = support; विवाद = quarrel; निष्ठीवन = spitting; जृंभण = yawning; पर्यस्तिका = a way of sitting.
questions.teaches: A long compound of nouns joined by 'and' (a dvandva) ends in the plural, here -आनि, and all its items share one verb.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which of these is named in the list of line 1?
options: Walking up and down the hall
optionExplain: Right: निष्ठीवन is in the list, after विवाद.
Singing is not in the list.
Walking is not in the list.
Sleeping is not in the list.
questions.explain: निष्ठीवन is in the list, after विवाद.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which are named in the verse as things to avoid in his presence?
optionExplain: Right: जृंभण.
Right: विवाद.
Right: उपाश्रय.
Not named in the verse.
Not named in the verse.
questions.explain: The list has yawning, quarrel and leaning on a support; bowing and answering are not in it.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which phrase means all fears (भीति, feminine), built like सर्वाः चेष्टाः?
optionExplain: सर्वे is masculine plural.
Right: A feminine plural takes सर्वाः, as चेष्टाः does.
सर्वाणि is neuter plural.
This is feminine singular, 'all fear'.
questions.explain: सर्वाः चेष्टाः = all movements (feminine plural); सर्वाः भीतयः = all fears.
questions.rule: सर्व agrees with its noun in gender and number.
questions.teaches: An adjective such as सर्व takes the feminine plural form सर्वाः with a feminine plural noun (सर्वाः चेष्टाः ; सर्वाः भीतयः).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What should one do after examining each condition properly?
options: Give up all the conditions at once
Ask other people to decide for him
Arrange what is good for oneself
optionExplain: Nothing says give up.
The verse says one arranges one's own good.
Right: सम्यक् समीक्ष्यात्महितं विदध्यात्.
Nothing says wait.
questions.explain: समीक्ष्य (having examined) leads to आत्महितं विदध्यात् (should arrange one's own good).
questions.rule: Examine, then arrange one's own good.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out तास्ताः).
questions.explain: The words run: properly, having examined, one's own good, should arrange.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the words of line 1.
questions.rule: अवस्थाः = conditions; विविधाः = of many kinds; सम्यक् = properly; समीक्ष्य = having examined; आत्महितम् = one's own good.
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य: सम् + ईक्ष् gives समीक्ष्य.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of सर्वाह्यवस्था?
optionExplain: These parts are not words.
The word is हि, with a short इ.
सर्वः would be masculine singular; the word is सर्वाः.
Right: The visarga after आ drops before a voiced letter, and इ + अ gives य.
questions.explain: सर्वाः (all, feminine) + हि (indeed) + अवस्थाः (conditions).
questions.rule: Visarga after आ drops before a voiced letter; इ + अ → य.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Someone finds another path among beneficial teachings. What does line 2 say?
options: He should reject it as unneeded
He should follow only that path
optionExplain: Right: अन्योऽपि ... मार्गः ... भजेत तम्.
The line says भजेत, follow.
Nothing says wait.
The line says 'too' (अपि), not 'only'.
questions.explain: The line adds any other path among beneficial teachings and says to follow it.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of समीक्ष्य, which word means having thought over (वि + चिन्त्)?
optionExplain: -त्वा is for a verb with no prefix.
Right: A verb with a prefix forms 'having done' in -य.
This is 'thinks over' (present).
This is 'should think over'.
questions.explain: सम् + ईक्ष् → समीक्ष्य; वि + चिन्त् → विचिन्त्य.
questions.teaches: After a prefix the 'having done' word ends in -य (समीक्ष्य, विचिन्त्य), not -त्वा.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By whom is he protected, according to this half-verse?
optionExplain: The elders are in unit 122 and are not the protectors here.
The king is in units 125-126; here the protectors are deities.
Right: रक्षितो देवताभिः.
The attendants are in unit 120.
questions.explain: देवताभिः is the 'by' form of देवताः, so the deities are the protectors.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put the words after इति in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The half-verse runs: conduct, endowed, support of all beings, renowned mass of virtues, protected, by the deities.
questions.rule: चरितम् · उपेतः · सर्वजीवोपजीव्यः · प्रथितपृथुगुणौघः · रक्षितः · देवताभिः.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: one on whom all beings depend
questions.explain: These are the descriptions of the man.
questions.rule: चरितम् = conduct; उपेतः = endowed with; सर्वजीवोपजीव्यः = support of all beings; रक्षितः = protected; देवताभिः = by the deities.
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ form 'by' (many) with -आभिः: देवताभिः = by the deities.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of सर्वजीवोपजीव्यः?
optionExplain: पजीव्यः is not a word.
सर्वः before ज would give सर्वो जीव, not सर्वजीव.
A visarga after अ before a vowel other than अ drops and the vowels stay apart: that would read जीव उपजीव्यः, not जीवोपजीव्यः.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so जीव + उपजीव्यः is written जीवोपजीव्यः.
questions.explain: सर्व (all) + जीव (beings) + उपजीव्यः (one on whom they depend).
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: जीव + उपजीव्य = जीवोपजीव्य.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which are said of him in this half-verse?
options: he is a support for all beings
his mass of virtues is renowned
he is protected by the deities
he is born in a royal family
he is the ruler of the deities
optionExplain: Right: सर्वजीवोपजीव्यः.
Right: प्रथितपृथुगुणौघः.
Right: रक्षितो देवताभिः.
Not said here.
Not said here; the deities protect him.
questions.explain: The half-verse has three descriptions after 'endowed with this conduct'.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of देवताभिः (by the deities), which word means by the stories (कथा)?
optionExplain: Right: A feminine -आ noun takes -आभिः for 'by' (many).
This is 'stories', the plain plural.
This is 'by two stories' (dual), not many.
This is 'of a story'.
questions.explain: देवता + आभिः = देवताभिः; so कथा gives कथाभिः.
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ form 'by' (many) with -आभिः (देवताभिः, कथाभिः).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: How long does the verse say he lives?
options: Exactly sixty years, and no more
Only until he is old and grey
As long as the king himself lives
optionExplain: No such number is in the verse.
Right: समधिकशतजीवी = living more than a hundred.
The word says more than a hundred.
The king is not in this unit.
questions.explain: समधिक = more than; शत = hundred; जीवी = one who lives.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put the first four words of the half-verse in order.
questions.explain: The half-verse begins: living over a hundred, content, of meritorious deeds, goes.
questions.rule: समधिकशतजीवी · निर्वृतः · पुण्यकर्मा · व्रजति · (शेष अंश संदिग्ध).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: at the breaking up of the body
questions.explain: These are the words that are clear in the half-verse.
questions.rule: समधिकशतजीवी = living over a hundred; निर्वृतः = content; पुण्यकर्मा = of meritorious deeds; व्रजति = goes, attains; देहभेदे = at the breaking up of the body.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -कर्मा names a person 'whose deeds are ...': पुण्यकर्मा = whose deeds are meritorious.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of देहभेदेऽपि?
optionExplain: A visarga before अ would give -ोऽ, and the ending is -ए.
इपि is not a word.
Right: ए + अ stays ए, and the अ is shown by the sign ऽ.
The ending is -ए, not -आ.
questions.explain: देहभेदे (at the breaking up of the body) + अपि (even).
questions.rule: ए + अ → ए with ऽ: देहभेदे + अपि = देहभेदेऽपि.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A learner says this man dies young. Which word of the half-verse disagrees?
optionExplain: This says content, not about length of life.
This says meritorious deeds, not about length of life.
This is the verb 'goes, attains'.
Right: It says he lives more than a hundred (years).
questions.explain: Only समधिकशतजीवी speaks of the length of his life.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: By the pattern of पुण्यकर्मा, what does शुभकर्मा mean?
options: One who does no deeds at all in life
The deed of an auspicious person
One who hates every kind of deed
optionExplain: Right: -कर्मा names a person whose deeds are what comes before.
The first part शुभ means auspicious.
The word names the person, not the deed.
Nothing in the word means hating.
questions.explain: पुण्य (meritorious) + कर्मा = whose deeds are meritorious; शुभ + कर्मा = whose deeds are auspicious.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -कर्मा names a person whose deeds are what comes before (पुण्यकर्मा, शुभकर्मा).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What is the name of the chapter that ends here?
optionExplain: That is not named in this line.
Right: इति दिनचर्यानाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः.
That is not named in this line.
That is not named in this line.
questions.explain: दिनचर्या is the chapter's name; तृतीय is third.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Put the words of the closing line in the order of the line.
questions.explain: The line runs: thus, Dinacaryā, by name, third, chapter.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words make the colophon.
questions.rule: इति = thus; दिनचर्या = daily routine; नाम = named; तृतीयः = third; अध्यायः = chapter.
questions.teaches: The colophon pattern is: इति + chapter name + नाम + the ordinal number + अध्यायः.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: Which is the right split of तृतीयोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: ध्यायः alone is not the word.
Then the two अ would join into आ, not ओ.
Right: A visarga after अ before अ becomes ओ, with the sign ऽ.
The ending would be -आः, not -ओऽ.
questions.explain: तृतीयः (third) + अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओऽ: तृतीयः + अध्यायः = तृतीयोऽध्यायः.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: A line in another book reads इति X नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः. Which chapter does it close?
options: The third verse of chapter X
optionExplain: तृतीयः is third, not first.
अध्यायः is chapter, not verse.
तृतीयः is the third itself.
Right: तृतीयः is third and X stands where the name goes.
questions.explain: The pattern names the chapter by name and number.
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: An invented line reads इति शयनचर्यानाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः. What does it announce?
options: The third chapter, named Śayanacaryā, in this book
optionExplain: Right: द्वितीयः is second; शयनचर्या is the name.
द्वितीयः is second, not third.
The name here is शयनचर्या.
अध्यायः is chapter, not verse.
questions.explain: The same pattern as the real line: name, नाम, ordinal, अध्यायः.
questions.teaches: A colophon says इति + the chapter's name + नाम + the ordinal + अध्यायः (इति दिनचर्यानाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः).
questions.section: राजा की सेवा और अध्याय का अन्त

questions.q: What is the subject of the chapter announced in this line?
options: The eight limbs of the whole work
Conduct that goes with the seasons
Conduct that goes with the daily round
optionExplain: The line names no limbs; it names the seasons.
Right: ऋतुचर्याध्यायम् names the chapter on seasonal conduct.
Nothing here speaks of students.
That would be a daily-conduct chapter; this line says ऋतु, season.
questions.explain: ऋतुचर्या is ऋतु (season) + चर्या (conduct); the line announces this as the chapter.
questions.rule: ऋतुचर्याध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall expound the chapter on seasonal conduct.

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The line is the usual opening formula: now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall expound.

questions.q: In ऋतुचर्याध्यायम्, which vowel join sits between चर्या and अध्याय?
optionExplain: The result is long, not short.
ए comes from अ/आ + इ/ई, not from अ.
Right: Two similar vowels, short or long, merge into one long vowel.
औ comes from अ/आ + ओ/औ.
questions.explain: चर्या + अध्याय joins as चर्याध्याय: the long आ absorbs the following अ.
questions.teaches: Two similar vowels, short or long, join into one long vowel (चर्या + अध्याय = चर्याध्याय).

questions.q: What does the ending of व्याख्यास्यामः tell us?
options: First person singular, present: I am expounding it now
Third person plural, past: they expounded it earlier
Second person plural, command: you must expound it
First person plural, future: we shall expound
optionExplain: -मः is the 'we' ending, not the 'I' ending.
Nothing in the form marks the past or the third person.
-मः is not a 'you' ending.
Right: The data labels it 1 pl. fut.: -स्य- marks the future, -मः the 'we'.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the first person plural future of वि-आ-ख्या.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line runs: now-therefore, the chapter on seasonal conduct, we shall expound.

questions.q: A new chapter opens: अथातो भोजनचर्याध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः. What does it announce?
options: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on food conduct
Now, therefore, we have expounded the chapter on food conduct
Now, therefore, they shall expound the chapter on the seasons of the year
Now, therefore, I shall expound the chapter on the eight limbs of the whole work
optionExplain: Right: Same formula, with ऋतु replaced by भोजन (food).
व्याख्यास्यामः is future, not past.
भोजन is food, and -मः is 'we', not 'they'.
The chapter is on food conduct, and 'we' not 'I'.
questions.explain: The formula अथातो X-अध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः always announces a chapter on X; only X changes.
questions.rule: अथातः + X-अध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on X.
questions.teaches: The opening formula names the chapter's subject in the compound before अध्यायं; the rest stays the same.

questions.q: Whom does the verse call the Lord, without beginning or end?
optionExplain: The sun is among the elements that change in compliance with him.
Right: कालो हि नाम भगवान्: Time, indeed, is the Lord.
Space is among the elements that change in compliance with him.
Living beings are those whose birth and death are spoken of.
questions.explain: The verse's subject is काल: अनादिनिधन, 'without beginning or end'.
questions.rule: काल = the Lord, अनादि-निधन, following accumulated actions.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the claim: Time is the beginningless, endless Lord, and the elements, changing, become a cause.
questions.rule: अनादि = beginningless; निधन = end; कारणत्व = being the cause; विपरिणमन्त् = changing.

questions.q: Put the six things named at the end of the verse in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verse lists them after birth and death: ऋतु, रस, वीर्य, दोष, देह, बल.
questions.rule: ऋतु · रस · वीर्य · दोष · देह · बल.
questions.teaches: After birth and death, the verse lists six things whose failings and successes the changing elements cause: season, taste, potency, doṣa, body, strength.

questions.q: How is the printed खादय श्च to be read?
options: खादय + श्च, with श्च taken as a separate word
खादयाः + च, written as one longer plural form
खादयः + च, since visarga before च becomes श्
खादयस् + च, with a spelled स् before च
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
The data reads the plural खादयः, not खादयाः.
Right: A visarga followed by च is written श्च.
Before च a visarga becomes श्, not स्.
questions.explain: खादयः (space and the rest) + च (and) joins as खादयश्च; the space in the print is only a gap.

questions.q: What do the changing great elements become, according to the verse?
options: The Lord who has neither beginning nor end, as he stands towards all living beings
The actions that living beings have accumulated in the past, which the elements then follow
The seasons themselves, with no birth, death, taste or strength apart from the seasons
The cause and ground of birth, death and of the failings and successes of six things
optionExplain: That describes Time, not the elements.
The accumulated actions are what Time follows; the elements do not become them.
The seasons are one of six things whose failings and successes they cause.
Right: कारणत्वं प्रत्ययतां प्रतिपद्यन्ते: they attain being the cause and ground.
questions.explain: The elements change as Time wills, and so become the cause and ground of what the verse lists.
questions.rule: महाभूत change → कारण and प्रत्यय of जन्म-मरण and of the failings and successes.

questions.q: Built like जन्मवताम् (of those having birth), what does धनवताम् mean?
options: Of those who have no wealth
Of the wealth that they hold
optionExplain: Right: -वत् at the end means 'having what comes before'.
-वत् means having, not giving.
That would need a word for 'without'.
The ending marks possessors, not the wealth itself.
questions.explain: जन्मवताम् = of those having birth, i.e. of living beings; धनवताम् = of those having wealth.
questions.teaches: The ending -वत् makes a word meaning 'having X' (जन्मवत् = having birth; धनवत् = having wealth).

questions.q: In how many ways does the verse say Time is divided?
optionExplain: The verse says द्वादशधा, twelve.
Right: द्वादशधा means in twelve ways.
The verse says द्वादशधा, twelve.
The verse says द्वादशधा, twelve.
questions.explain: द्वादशधा विभज्यते: it is divided twelvefold, and the verse names the twelve.

questions.q: Put the first six divisions of Time in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The list begins: मात्रा, काष्ठा, कला, नाडिका, मुहूर्त, याम.
questions.rule: मात्रा · काष्ठा · कला · नाडिका · मुहूर्त · याम.

questions.q: In मासर्त्वयन, how do ऋतु and अयन join?
options: ऋत + अयन, with अ + अ becoming आ
ऋतो + अयन, with ओ before अ
ऋतु + अयन, with उ before अ becoming व्
ऋत्व + यन, with a word यन
optionExplain: That would give ऋतायन, with a long आ.
ओ before अ gives ओऽ, not त्व.
Right: ऋतु + अयन = ऋत्वयन.
यन is not a word here.
questions.explain: In मासर्त्वयन the ऋतु (season) and अयन (half-year course) join: ऋतु + अयन = ऋत्वयन.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व् (ऋतु + अयन = ऋत्वयन).

questions.q: Which item stands directly between पक्ष and ऋतु in the verse's list?
optionExplain: अहोरात्र stands before पक्ष.
अयन stands after ऋतु.
वर्ष is the last item, after अयन.
Right: The list runs ... अहोरात्र, पक्ष, मास, ऋतु ...
questions.explain: The order is अहोरात्र, पक्ष, मास, ऋतु, अयन, वर्ष.

questions.q: Match each division to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five are the larger divisions in the verse's list.
questions.rule: अहोरात्र = day-and-night; पक्ष = fortnight; मास = month; ऋतु = season; अयन = half-year course.

questions.q: Which is the right join of मधु + अत्र?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, as in ऋत्वयन.
In running text the two vowels must join.
उ does not turn into आ before अ.
ओ would come from अ/आ + उ, not from उ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as ऋतु + अयन = ऋत्वयन: the final उ turns into व्.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व्; so मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र.

questions.q: What does the verse call a mātrā?
optionExplain: That is an अहोरात्र, a later division.
Right: अक्षिनिमेषो मात्रा.
A season is an ऋतु, another division.
That is a month, in a later unit.
questions.explain: अक्षि (eye) + निमेष (twinkling) = the twinkling of the eye, which the verse names a मात्रा.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sentence has four words: among these, eye, twinkling, mātrā.
questions.rule: अक्षि = eye; निमेष = twinkling; मात्रा = unit of time.

questions.q: The word for 'eye' in this unit is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अक्षि is the eye: अक्षिनिमेष is the eye's twinkling.
questions.teaches: अक्षि means 'eye'; as the first member of a compound it gives 'of the eye'.

questions.q: Why is निमेषः printed as निमेषो before मात्रा?
options: A visarga before any sound is left out
The word निमेष is a dual form ending in ओ
अः before a voiced sound becomes ओ
A visarga before म always becomes श्
optionExplain: Here it becomes ओ, not nothing.
The data labels it singular, with a visarga.
Right: निमेषः + मात्रा = निमेषो मात्रा, since म is voiced.
श् stands for a visarga before च/छ.
questions.explain: तत्राक्षिनिमेषः + मात्रा joins as ...निमेषो मात्रा, and तत्र + अक्षि joins as तत्राक्षि.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: among these, the twinkling of the eye, a mātrā.

questions.q: On the pattern of अक्षिनिमेषः, what is हस्तकम्पः?
options: A hand that trembles in fear
optionExplain: That would be a bahuvrīhi-type describing reading, not the 'of the hand' reading of the card.
The first member is the owner, not the material.
Nothing here marks a dual or a plural.
Right: First member means 'of the ...': हस्त (hand) + कम्प (trembling).
questions.explain: अक्षिनिमेषः = twinkling of the eye; the same layout gives हस्तकम्पः = trembling of the hand.
questions.teaches: In such a compound the first word is read with 'of': अक्षिनिमेष = twinkling of the eye; हस्तकम्प = trembling of the hand.

questions.q: How many mātrās make one kāṣṭhā in this unit?
optionExplain: Right: पञ्चदश = fifteen.
Thirty is the number in the next unit.
Twenty is the number of the unit after that.
Twelve is the number of kinds of Time, not of mātrās.
questions.explain: ताः पञ्चदश काष्ठा: those fifteen make a kāṣṭhā.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has three words: those, fifteen, kāṣṭhā.
questions.rule: ताः = those; पञ्चदश = fifteen; काष्ठा = unit of time.

questions.q: Match each part of the number word to its meaning.
questions.explain: पञ्चदश is made of पञ्च (five) and दश (ten): fifteen.
questions.rule: पञ्च = five; दश = ten; पञ्चदश = fifteen.
questions.teaches: A number word can be built from smaller ones: पञ्च (five) and दश (ten) make पञ्चदश (fifteen).

questions.q: Why does the unit say ताः and not ते?
options: ताः is masculine plural and the mātrās are masculine
ताः is feminine plural and the mātrās are feminine
ताः is a singular form for one single mātrā
ताः is a neuter form for things without gender
optionExplain: ते is the masculine plural; मात्रा is feminine.
Right: ताः agrees with the feminine plural noun मात्राः.
ताः is plural: 'those'.
The neuter plural would be तानि.
questions.explain: A pronoun takes the gender and number of the noun it points back to.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: those, fifteen, kāṣṭhā.

questions.q: Which pronoun fills the invented line ____ दश मुहूर्ताः (ten muhūrtas), as ताः stands in ताः पञ्चदश?
optionExplain: ताः goes with feminine plural nouns.
तानि goes with neuter plural nouns.
Right: मुहूर्ताः is masculine plural, so ते is the matching 'those'.
सः is singular, 'that one'.
questions.explain: The pronoun follows the noun: feminine plural ताः, masculine plural ते, neuter plural तानि.
questions.rule: Pronoun agrees with its noun in gender and number.
questions.teaches: The pronoun 'those' agrees with its noun: ताः (feminine plural), ते (masculine plural), तानि (neuter plural).

questions.q: How many kāṣṭhās make a kalā in this unit?
optionExplain: Fifteen is the number of mātrās in a kāṣṭhā, in unit 5.
Twenty is the number in unit 7.
Two is the number in unit 8.
Right: त्रिंशत् = thirty.
questions.explain: तास्त्रिंशत्कला: those, thirty, make a kalā.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has three words: those, thirty, kalā.
questions.rule: ताः = those; त्रिंशत् = thirty; कला = unit of time.

questions.q: Put the parts and the joined form in order: first the two words, then the print.
questions.explain: The two words ताः and त्रिंशत् come first; the print joins them as तास्त्रिंशत्.
questions.teaches: Printed तास्त्रिंशत् holds two words: ताः (those) and त्रिंशत् (thirty).

questions.q: How does ताः + त्रिंशत् become तास्त्रिंशत्?
options: The visarga before त becomes स्
The visarga before त becomes श् as before च
The visarga before त becomes ष् as before ट
The visarga before त vanishes without any change
optionExplain: Right: ताः + त → तास्त.
श् stands before च/छ, not before त.
ष् stands before ट/ठ.
It turns into स्, it does not vanish.
questions.explain: Visarga + त/थ becomes स्, so ताः + त्रिंशत् = तास्त्रिंशत्.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: those, thirty, kalā.

questions.q: Which is the right join of ताः + तिस्रः (those three, feminine)?
optionExplain: श् is for a visarga before च/छ.
Right: The visarga before त becomes स्.
ष् is for a visarga before ट/ठ.
In running text the visarga must change before त.
questions.explain: Same rule as ताः + त्रिंशत् = तास्त्रिंशत्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: ताः + त्रिंशत् = तास्त्रिंशत्; ताः + तिस्रः = तास्तिस्रः.

questions.q: Which number word does the verse give for the kalās of a nāḍikā?
optionExplain: Fifteen is the number in unit 5.
Thirty is the number in unit 6.
Right: विंशतिः is the number word of this unit.
Two is the number in unit 8.
questions.explain: ताः सदशभागा विंशतिर्नाडिका: twenty, with a tenth part, make a nāḍikā.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words carry the count: those, twenty, nāḍikā.
questions.rule: ताः = those; विंशतिः = twenty; नाडिका = unit of time.

questions.q: How does the card read सदशभागा?
options: With a tenth part of a kalā, as the verse says plainly
Without any tenth part, one tenth being taken away
With ten parts, each one a full nāḍikā long
With a tenth part, though of what is not said
optionExplain: The text does not say a tenth of what.
स- here is 'with', not 'without'.
दशभाग is a tenth part, not ten parts.
Right: The card reads स-दश-भाग as 'with a tenth part' and leaves the whole open.
questions.explain: सदशभागा is read 'with a tenth part'; the card builds no sum from it.
questions.rule: सदशभागा = with a tenth part (of what, not said).
questions.teaches: The word सदशभागा is read 'with a tenth part'; the text does not name the whole, so no sum is made.

questions.q: Why is the visarga of विंशतिः written as र् in विंशतिर्नाडिका?
options: After इ a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्
After इ a visarga before a voiced sound becomes ओ, as after अ
After इ a visarga always becomes श्, whatever sound follows
After इ a visarga before न is left out, as it is after आ
optionExplain: Right: विंशतिः + नाडिका: इः + न → इर् न.
ओ is the rule after अ, not after इ.
श् stands before च/छ.
It turns into र्; it does not vanish.
questions.explain: The word ends in -तिः and the next word begins with the voiced न.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: those, with a tenth part, twenty, nāḍikā.

questions.q: Which is the right join of कविः + गच्छति (the poet goes)?
optionExplain: The visarga does not just vanish after इ.
Right: After इ a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्.
ओ is for a visarga after अ.
श् is for a visarga before च/छ.
questions.explain: Same rule as विंशतिः + नाडिका = विंशतिर्नाडिका.
questions.teaches: After इ a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्: विंशतिः + नाडिका = विंशतिर्नाडिका; कविः + गच्छति = कविर्गच्छति.

questions.q: How many nāḍikās make a muhūrta in this unit?
optionExplain: Fifteen is the number of mātrās in a kāṣṭhā.
Thirty is the number of kāṣṭhās in a kalā.
Right: नाडिकाद्वयम् = a pair of nāḍikās.
Four is not the count here; the next unit speaks of four less a quarter muhūrtas in a yāma.
questions.explain: नाडिकाद्वयं मुहूर्तश्च: a pair of nāḍikās is also a muhūrta.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has three words: a pair of nāḍikās, the muhūrta being defined, and also.
questions.rule: नाडिकाद्वयम् = pair of nāḍikās; द्वय = pair; मुहूर्त = the unit defined; च = and, also.

questions.q: How is the printed मुहूर्तश्च to be read?
options: मुहूर्त + श्च, with श्च a word
मुहूर्तस् + च, with a spelled स्
मुहूर्तः + च, since visarga before च becomes श्
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
The data reads the singular मुहूर्तः.
Before च a visarga becomes श्, not स्.
Right: A visarga followed by च is written श्च.
questions.explain: मुहूर्तः (muhūrta) + च (and, also) joins as मुहूर्तश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्, so मुहूर्तः + च = मुहूर्तश्च.

questions.q: How does the data read the compound नाडिकाद्वयम्?
options: A nāḍikā that has two parts
optionExplain: Right: tat-puruṣa: द्वय (pair) of नाडिका, i.e. a pair of nāḍikās.
A 'having' reading would need the compound to describe something else.
Nothing in the word means 'without'.
The pair belongs to nāḍikās; the muhūrta is the result.
questions.explain: The pair is a pair of nāḍikās, and this pair is a muhūrta.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: pair of nāḍikās, muhūrta, also.

questions.q: On the pattern of नाडिकाद्वयम्, what is नेत्रद्वयम्?
options: Two eyes of a pair of pairs
optionExplain: द्वय gives a pair of the first word.
Right: नेत्र (eye) + द्वयम् (pair).
The word has only one pair.
That would be a word with निमेष.
questions.explain: X-द्वयम् = a pair of X: नाडिकाद्वयम्, नेत्रद्वयम्.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in द्वयम् means 'a pair of X': नाडिकाद्वयम् = a pair of nāḍikās; नेत्रद्वयम् = a pair of eyes.

questions.q: Which unit of time is defined in this unit?
options: The muhūrta, a pair of nāḍikās
The yāma, a watch of the day
optionExplain: The muhūrta was defined in unit 8.
The pakṣa comes in a later unit.
Right: यामः is the last word and the thing defined.
The ṛtu is only named in unit 3.
questions.explain: ते ... चत्वारः पादोना यामः: those, four less a quarter, make a yāma.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the count and the unit defined, and the pointer back to the muhūrtas.
questions.rule: चत्वारः = four; पादोन = less a quarter; याम = a watch of the day; ते = those (m. pl.).

questions.q: Why does the card read ते (not ताः) as pointing to the muhūrtas?
options: It points back to the kalās, a feminine plural
It points back to the nāḍikā, a singular noun
It points forward to the yāma, a neuter noun
It points back to the muhūrtas, a masculine plural
optionExplain: ताः would go with feminine kalās.
ते is plural; and the pair was of nāḍikās, not itself.
यामः is masculine singular, and ते is plural.
Right: मुहूर्तः is masculine, so its plural 'those' is ते.
questions.explain: The pronoun agrees with its noun: muhūrtas are masculine plural, so ते.
questions.teaches: The pronoun 'those' follows its noun: masculine plural ते, feminine plural ताः.

questions.q: Why does पादोना end in -आ and not -आः?
options: A visarga after आ drops before a voiced sound
It is a typing mistake with a missing visarga
The word is singular and feminine
A visarga after आ becomes ओ
optionExplain: Right: पादोनाः + यामः becomes पादोना यामः, य being voiced.
The data treats it as the usual sandhi.
The data reads it as masculine plural.
ओ is the rule after अ, not after आ.
questions.explain: पादोनाः (masculine plural) + यामः → पादोना यामः.

questions.q: Put these words in the verse's order, leaving out the middle phrase.
questions.explain: The unit runs: those, four, less a quarter, yāma, with the obscure phrase after ते.

questions.q: Which is the right join of कन्याः + गायन्ति (the girls sing)?
optionExplain: ओ is for a visarga after अ.
Right: आः before a voiced sound drops its visarga.
श् is for a visarga before च/छ.
In running text the visarga must drop here.
questions.explain: Same rule as पादोनाः + यामः = पादोना यामः.
questions.teaches: After आ a visarga is dropped before a voiced sound: पादोनाः + यामः = पादोना यामः; कन्याः + गायन्ति = कन्या गायन्ति.

questions.q: By what does the unit say the day and the night come?
options: By two nāḍikās together, that is one muhūrta of the day
By fifteen day-and-nights taken together as one unit
By those four, the yāmas of the previous unit
By the twinkling of an eye, repeated many times over
optionExplain: Unit 8 defines the muhūrta, not the day.
That is the pakṣa of the next unit.
Right: तैश्चतुर्भिः: by those four.
That is a mātrā, from unit 4.
questions.explain: तैः चतुर्भिः (by those four) refers to the yāmas defined just before.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the whole sentence.
questions.rule: तैः = by those; चतुर्भिः = by four; अहः = day; रात्रिः = night.

questions.q: How is the printed तैश्चतुर्भिः to be read?
options: तै + श्चतुर्भिः, with श्चतुर्भिः taken as a word
तैस् + चतुर्भिः, with a spelled स् before च
तैश + चतुर्भिः, with a word तैश left whole
तैः + चतुर्भिः, since visarga before च becomes श्
optionExplain: श्चतुर्भिः is not a word.
Before च a visarga becomes श्, not स्.
तैश is not a word here.
Right: A visarga followed by च is written श्च.
questions.explain: तैः (by those) + चतुर्भिः (by four) joins as तैश्चतुर्भिः.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: तैः + चतुर्भिः = तैश्चतुर्भिः.

questions.q: In चतुर्भिरहो, what has become of the visarga of चतुर्भिः before अहः?
options: It has become र्, since इः before a vowel becomes इर्
It has become ओ, as after अ before a voiced sound
It has been dropped, as after आ before a voiced sound
It has become श्, as it does before a following च or छ
optionExplain: Right: चतुर्भिः + अहः → चतुर्भिरहः: after इ a visarga before a vowel turns into र्.
ओ is the rule after अ, not after इ.
Dropping is the rule after आ.
अहः does not begin with च or छ.
questions.explain: चतुर्भिः + अहः → चतुर्भिरहः: the visarga after इ turns into र् before a vowel.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: by those, by four, day, night.

questions.q: Which word means by five (masculine), on the pattern of चतुर्भिः?
optionExplain: -आनाम् marks 'of'.
Right: The ending -भिः marks 'by' in the plural.
-सु marks 'in'.
This is not a form that means 'by five'.
questions.explain: चतुर्भिः = by four; पञ्चभिः = by five. The ending -भिः shows 'by'.
questions.teaches: A plural ending -भिः means 'by': चतुर्भिः = by four; पञ्चभिः = by five.

questions.q: How many day-and-night periods make a pakṣa?
optionExplain: Thirty is the number of kāṣṭhās in a kalā.
Twelve is the number of kinds of Time in unit 3.
Right: पञ्चदश = fifteen.
Two is the number of fortnights in a month, in the next unit.
questions.explain: पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः पक्षः: fifteen day-and-night periods make a fortnight.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has three parts: fifteen, day-and-night, fortnight.
questions.rule: पञ्चदश = fifteen; अहोरात्र = day and night; पक्ष = fortnight.

questions.q: Which word names the unit made of fifteen day-and-nights?
optionExplain: A मास is a month, two fortnights, in the next unit.
A याम is a watch of the day, from unit 9.
An अयन is a half-year course, listed in unit 3.
Right: पक्ष is the fortnight, made of fifteen day-and-nights.
questions.explain: पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः पक्षः: fifteen day-and-night periods are called a पक्ष.
questions.teaches: The unit made of fifteen day-and-night periods is the पक्ष, the fortnight.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः?
options: पञ्चदश + अहोरात्राः, अ + अ becoming आ
पञ्चदश + होरात्राः, with a word होरात्राः
पञ्चदशे + अहोरात्राः, with ए before अ
optionExplain: Right: Two अ vowels merge into आ.
होरात्राः is not a word here.
A visarga before अ would give ओ ऽ, not आ.
ए before अ would give ए with an avagraha.
questions.explain: पञ्चदश (fifteen) + अहोरात्राः (day-and-night periods) join as पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः.

questions.q: Put the words in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: fifteen, day-and-nights, fortnight.

questions.q: Which is the right join of दश + अश्वाः (ten horses)?
optionExplain: One vowel cannot just drop.
Right: अ + अ becomes आ.
ओ comes from अ + उ/ऊ, not from अ + अ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए/ऐ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as पञ्चदश + अहोरात्राः = पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः.
questions.teaches: Two similar vowels join into a long one: पञ्चदश + अहोरात्राः = पञ्चदशाहोरात्राः; दश + अश्वाः = दशाश्वाः.

questions.q: How many fortnights make a month in this unit?
optionExplain: Fifteen is the number of day-and-nights in a fortnight.
Twelve is the number of kinds of Time.
Right: पक्षद्वयम् = a pair of fortnights.
Four less a quarter is the muhūrta count for a yāma, not for a month.
questions.explain: पक्षद्वयं मासः: a pair of fortnights is a month.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has two words, the first a compound of fortnight and pair, then month.
questions.rule: पक्ष = fortnight; द्वय = pair; मास = month.

questions.q: How does the data read the compound पक्षद्वयम्?
options: A fortnight that has two parts belonging to it as its own
Two months that are made up of fortnights, one after another
A fortnight that is left without any pair at all
A pair of fortnights (the pair belongs to the fortnights)
optionExplain: That would need a word for 'having'.
The unit's result is one month.
Nothing in the word means 'without'.
Right: द्वय (pair) of पक्ष (fortnights): the pair belongs to the fortnights.
questions.explain: पक्षद्वयम् = pair (द्वय) of fortnights (पक्ष), and this pair is a month.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in द्वयम् means 'a pair of X', as in नाडिकाद्वयम् and पक्षद्वयम्.

questions.q: Which English line translates the unit correctly?
options: A pair of fortnights is a month
A pair of months is a fortnight
A pair of day-and-nights is a month
optionExplain: Right: पक्षद्वयं मासः.
The two terms are reversed.
A year is varṣa; the unit says month.
The pair is of fortnights, not of days.
questions.explain: The unit says: the pair of fortnights is the month.

questions.q: Put the parts in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The unit runs: fortnight, pair, month.

questions.q: On the pattern of पक्षद्वयम्, what is मासद्वयम्?
options: A month that has two parts
optionExplain: द्वय gives a pair of the first word.
Right: मास (month) + द्वयम् (pair).
That is पक्षद्वयम्; this has मास.
A year is varṣa, not made from this word.
questions.explain: X-द्वयम् = a pair of X; so मासद्वयम् is a pair of months.
questions.teaches: Any word followed by द्वयम् names a pair of it: पक्षद्वयम् = a pair of fortnights; मासद्वयम् = a pair of months.

questions.q: With which fortnight does the month end, by this unit?
options: Neither, it ends in the middle
optionExplain: The unit names śukla, not kṛṣṇa.
The unit says it ends with the bright one.
Right: शुक्लान्तः: ending with the bright one.
The unit names only the bright one.
questions.explain: सः शुक्लान्तः: that month ends with the bright fortnight.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit has two words, the second a compound: that, ending with the bright one.
questions.rule: स = that; शुक्ल = bright; अन्त = end.

questions.q: Which split does the card give for शुक्लान्तः?
options: शुक्ली + अन्तः, with ई before अ
शुक्ल + आन्तः, with a word आन्तः
शुक्ल + अन्तः, with अ + अ becoming आ
optionExplain: ई before अ would give शुक्ल्यन्तः, with य्.
The card has अन्तः (end), not आन्तः.
A visarga before अ would give ओ ऽ, not आ.
Right: Two अ vowels merge into आ.
questions.explain: शुक्ल (bright) + अन्तः (end) join as शुक्लान्तः.
questions.teaches: A compound can end in अन्त 'end' with the first word naming the end: शुक्ल + अन्त = शुक्लान्त, 'ending with the bright one'.

questions.q: What does the data say the compound शुक्लान्तः describes?
options: The month, which has the bright fortnight as end
The bright fortnight, which has a month as its end
The month, which begins with the bright fortnight
The end of the bright fortnight, as a thing
optionExplain: Right: A bahuvrīhi describes another thing: the month.
The subject सः is the month.
अन्त means end, not beginning.
The word is masculine and agrees with सः.
questions.explain: सः (that month) + शुक्लान्तः (having the bright one as end).

questions.q: Put the parts in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The unit runs: that, bright, end.

questions.q: In an invented line सः पाठः प्रश्नान्तः, what does प्रश्नान्तः say?
options: The lesson begins with a question
The lesson ends with a question
The lesson is full of questions
optionExplain: अन्त means end.
Right: -अन्त at the end of such a compound means 'ending with X'.
That would need a word for 'full'.
Nothing in the word means 'without'.
questions.explain: Like शुक्लान्तः: प्रश्न (question) + अन्तः = having a question as its end.
questions.rule: X-अन्तः = having X as its end.
questions.teaches: X-अन्तः describing a noun means 'having X as its end': शुक्लान्तः = ending with the bright one; प्रश्नान्तः = ending with a question.

questions.q: How are the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa taken to make the six seasons?
options: Two by two, in any order
optionExplain: द्विसंख्यैः says two in number, not one.
The compound says two, not three.
Right: द्विसंख्यैः क्रमात्: two in number, in order.
क्रमात् says in order.
questions.explain: द्विसंख्यैः means two in number, and क्रमात् means in order.
questions.rule: Months from Mārgaśīrṣa, two by two, in order, make the seasons.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry how the seasons are counted and named.
questions.rule: द्विसंख्यैः = two in number; क्रमात् = in order; आख्याः = named; षट् = six.

questions.q: The word for 'in order' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: क्रमात् means in order; it is used here like an adverb.
questions.teaches: क्रमात् is the ablative of क्रम (order) used as 'in order, one after another'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of षडृतवो भवंति?
optionExplain: षष् is not a form of the word for six.
A singular ऋतुः would not give ऋतवो.
भवंति is plural, 'they are', not the singular भवति.
Right: ट् becomes ड् before a vowel; the visarga of ऋतवः becomes ओ before the voiced भ.
questions.explain: षट् (six) + ऋतवः (seasons) + भवन्ति (they are).
questions.rule: Final ट् before a vowel → ड्; विसर्ग after अ before a voiced sound → ओ.

questions.q: Put the six seasons in the order of the sentence.
questions.explain: The sentence names them as Hemanta, Śiśira, Vasanta, Grīṣma, Varṣā, Śarad.
questions.rule: हेमन्त · शिशिर · वसन्त · ग्रीष्म · वर्षा · शरद.

questions.q: What does the invented phrase वैशाखादिभिः मासैः mean, built like मार्गशीर्षादिभिः?
options: By the months beginning with Vaiśākha
By the months ending with Vaiśākha
Of the months beginning with Vaiśākha
optionExplain: Right: X-आदि means beginning with X; the ending -भिः is 'by', plural.
आदि means beginning, not ending.
आदि means 'and the rest', so there is more than one.
-भिः is the 'by' ending, not 'of'.
questions.explain: वैशाख + आदि + भिः: beginning with Vaiśākha, by those (months).
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -आदि means 'beginning with X' (मार्गशीर्षादि); the ending -भिः on it means 'by' in the plural.

questions.q: Which course of the sun goes with the three seasons beginning with Śiśira?
optionExplain: That goes with the remaining three.
Right: शिशिरादयः त्रयः are the sun's northward course and ādāna.
Each course gets its own three seasons.
Both courses are named in the sentence.
questions.explain: The three beginning with Śiśira are the northward course; the rest are the southward.
questions.rule: Śiśira and two more: उदगयन + आदान; the other three: दक्षिणायन + विसर्ग.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four terms are the two halves of the year in the sentence.
questions.rule: उदगयनम् = northward course; दक्षिणायनम् = southward course; आदानम् = taking-in; विसर्गः = release.

questions.q: The word for 'of the sun' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: रवेः is the genitive singular of रवि, the sun.
questions.teaches: रवि (sun) is an -इ word; its 'of' form (genitive singular) is रवेः.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रवेरुदगयनम्?
optionExplain: Without the visarga there is no र् to explain the joined form.
That would give रविरुदगयनम्, not रवेरुदगयनम्.
Right: A visarga after ए turns into र् before a vowel.
रवः is not the word for sun and would give रव उदगयनम्.
questions.explain: रवेः (of the sun) + उदगयनम् (northward course).
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ, before a vowel → र्.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence first gives the three, their course and ādāna; then the remaining ones, their course and visarga.
questions.rule: शिशिरादयः त्रयः · रवेरुदगयनम् · आदानं च · शेषाः · दक्षिणायनम् · विसर्गश्च.

questions.q: In the invented line पञ्च जनाः; तेषु द्वौ गायकौ शेषा वादकाः, who are the वादकाः?
options: The two singers themselves, named already
All five people together, singers too
Some people outside the group of five
The other three of the five
optionExplain: द्वौ गायकौ are the two singers; शेषाः are the others.
शेषाः leaves out the ones already named.
तेषु means among them, so the group is the five.
Right: तेषु picks the group of five; शेषाः means the remaining ones.
questions.explain: तेषु (among them) fixes the group; शेषाः (the remaining) are those not yet named.
questions.rule: तेषु + named part + शेषाः = the rest of that group.
questions.teaches: तेषु (among them) takes a group already named; शेषाः means all the remaining members of that group, as in the sentence 'the remaining three'.

questions.q: What do ādāna and visarga together make, according to the unit?
optionExplain: Right: तौ आदानविसर्गौ वर्षम्: the two make a year.
The two together span the six seasons, a year.
The unit names no month.
Nothing of days and nights is said here.
questions.explain: The two together are called the year.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These pairs give the words of the sentence; आदान and विसर्ग are the two members of one compound.
questions.rule: तौ = those two; आदान = taking-in; विसर्ग = release; वर्ष = year.

questions.q: The word for 'year' (the print has वर्ष) is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: वर्ष is the year; the print leaves off the final म्.
questions.teaches: वर्ष (neuter) names the year; the full nominative is वर्षम्, and the print's वर्ष is accepted.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तावादानविसर्गौ?
optionExplain: ताव is not a word.
Right: औ before a vowel becomes आव्: तौ + आ- gives ताव्-आ-.
तु would give त्वादान-, not तावादान-.
ताः would give ता आदान-, not तावादान-.
questions.explain: तौ (those two) + आदानविसर्गौ (ādāna and visarga).

questions.q: Put the parts of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: those two, ādāna and visarga, a year.

questions.q: What does the invented dual compound मातापितरौ mean, built like आदानविसर्गौ?
optionExplain: A genitive link would not end in -औ.
-औ marks two, not many.
Right: A dual in -औ joins two things: both are named.
Nothing in the form says 'like'.
questions.explain: आदानविसर्गौ names two things together; मातापितरौ does the same for mother and father.
questions.rule: Dvandva in dual -औ = the two named, together.
questions.teaches: A dvandva in the dual (-औ) names two things together, as आदानविसर्गौ does; मातापितरौ names mother and father.

questions.q: Of ādāna and visarga, which is called āgneya in this unit?
optionExplain: Visarga is not named in this unit.
Only ādāna gets the label here.
The label is given to ādāna.
Right: तयोः आदानम् आग्नेयम्: of the two, ādāna is āgneya.
questions.explain: आदानम् is the subject and आग्नेयम् says what it is.
questions.rule: तयोः आदानम् आग्नेयम् = of the two, ādāna is āgneya.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole sentence.
questions.rule: तयोः = of those two; आदानम् = ādāna; आग्नेयम् = fiery, belonging to Agni.

questions.q: The word for 'fiery, belonging to Agni' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आग्नेयम् is the neuter form agreeing with आदानम्.
questions.teaches: आग्नेय is made from अग्नि; in the sentence it is neuter, like आदानम्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तयोरादानमाग्नेयम्?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ओ turns into र् before a vowel.
That would be written तयोर्दानम्, without the long आ.
Dropping the visarga leaves no र् to join the words.
अग्नेयम् is not the word; the word is आग्नेयम्.
questions.explain: तयोः (of those two) + आदानम् + आग्नेयम्.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ, before a vowel → र्.

questions.q: Put the words of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: of those two, ādāna, fiery.

questions.q: Which word completes the invented line तयोः जलं ____, meaning the water of the two is cool, agreeing like आग्नेयम्?
optionExplain: This is masculine; जलम् is neuter.
Right: जलम् is neuter, so the describing word is neuter: -म्.
This is feminine; जलम् is neuter.
This is masculine plural; जलम् is singular neuter.
questions.explain: A describing word agrees with its noun: neuter आदानम् → neuter आग्नेयम्; neuter जलम् → neuter शीतलम्.
questions.rule: Describing word agrees with its noun in gender, number and case.
questions.teaches: A word that says what something is (आग्नेयम्) takes the gender and number of its noun (आदानम्, neuter singular).

questions.q: According to this sentence, what do the sun and the winds bring to men in ādāna?
optionExplain: Strength being built up is said of visarga, in the later unit.
Sleep is not mentioned in this sentence.
Right: नृणां दौर्बल्यमावहन्ति: they bring weakness to men.
Hunger is not mentioned in this sentence.
questions.explain: The last clause says they bring weakness to men.
questions.rule: आदान: the sun and the winds bring दौर्बल्य to men.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sentence names three tastes that are strengthened and one thing that is taken away.
questions.rule: तिक्त = bitter; कषाय = astringent; कटु = pungent; स्नेह = moisture.

questions.q: The word for 'sun' in this sentence is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अर्कः is the sun, the first subject of the sentence.
questions.teaches: अर्क is one of the words for the sun; here it is the subject with the winds (वायवः).

questions.q: Which is the right split of अत्यर्थोष्ण-?
optionExplain: That would join as अत्यर्थौष्ण, and ओष्ण is not a word here.
अष्ण is not a word, and the उ would be lost.
ए + उ would give अत्यर्थयुष्ण, not अत्यर्थोष्ण.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ: अत्यर्थ + उष्ण = अत्यर्थोष्ण.
questions.explain: अत्यर्थ (very) + उष्ण (hot): very hot.

questions.q: Put these parts of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The two subjects come first, then the three things they do as participles, then the main verb: they bring weakness.
questions.rule: अर्कः · तत्संपर्काद्वायवः · सोमजं गुणमुपशोषयंतः · जगतः स्नेहमाददानाः · रूक्षान् रसांस्तिक्तकषायकटुकानभिप्रबलयंतः · दौर्बल्यमावहंति.

questions.q: In the invented line बालाः गायन्तः गच्छन्ति, what does गायन्तः say, like उपशोषयन्तः?
options: The place the boys go to
optionExplain: Right: A -न्तः present participle says what the subject does at the same time.
गायन्तः is plural and present, not past.
A participle in -न्तः is not a place word.
It is a present participle, not a future.
questions.explain: उपशोषयन्तः (drying up) goes with the plural subjects and says what they do while the main verb happens.
questions.rule: Present participle masculine plural in -न्तः = 'doing X' with a plural subject.
questions.teaches: A present participle in -न्तः (masculine plural) describes what the plural subject is doing at the same time as the main verb, as in उपशोषयन्तः.

questions.q: Which of the two, ādāna or visarga, is called saumya here?
optionExplain: Ādāna was called āgneya in unit 17.
Right: विसर्गः तु सौम्यः: visarga, however, is saumya.
Only visarga gets the label in this sentence.
Visarga is called saumya.
questions.explain: विसर्गः is the subject and सौम्यः tells what it is.
questions.rule: विसर्गः तु सौम्यः = visarga, however, is saumya.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole sentence.
questions.rule: विसर्गः = release; तु = but, however; सौम्यः = gentle, of Soma.

questions.q: The word for 'but, however' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तु sets this sentence against the one before it.
questions.teaches: तु is a small word meaning but or however; it comes after the first word of its clause.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विसर्गस्तु?
optionExplain: ओ appears before a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
च would give विसर्गश्च; the word here is तु.
Right: A visarga before त turns into स्.
That would be written विसर्गात्तु, with त्, not स्.
questions.explain: विसर्गः (visarga) + तु (but).

questions.q: Put the words of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: visarga, however, saumya.

questions.q: In the invented pair दिनं उष्णम्; रात्रिः तु शीतला, what does तु signal?
options: A contrast with the sentence before
optionExplain: तु marks a contrast, not a repetition.
तु does not make a question.
तु says nothing about time.
Right: तु marks 'but, however': the second sentence is set against the first.
questions.explain: तु sets रात्रिः against दिनम्, as विसर्गः तु is set against आदान.
questions.rule: तु = but, however: contrast with what came before.
questions.teaches: तु, after the first word of a sentence, sets that sentence against the one before it (विसर्गस्तु after आदानम् आग्नेयम्).

questions.q: What does the sentence say happens to men's strength in visarga?
optionExplain: Right: बलं चोपचीयते नृणाम्: the strength of men is built up.
Weakness is the word of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
The sentence says it is built up.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: The last clause says men's strength is built up.
questions.rule: visarga: non-dry tastes increase; strength is built up.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sentence names three tastes and calls them not dry.
questions.rule: अम्ल = sour; लवण = salty; मधुर = sweet; अरूक्षाः = not dry.

questions.q: The word for 'strength' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: बलम् is strength, the second thing that increases.
questions.teaches: बल is strength; in the sentence it is the subject of उपचीयते (is built up).

questions.q: Which tastes does this sentence say increase in visarga? Select all.
optionExplain: Right: it is the first of the three.
Right: it is the second of the three.
Right: it is the third of the three.
Bitter is one of the dry tastes of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
Astringent is a dry taste of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
Pungent is a dry taste of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
questions.explain: Visarga: sour, salty and sweet increase; bitter, astringent and pungent are the ādāna tastes.
questions.rule: Visarga: अम्ल, लवण, मधुर. Ādāna: तिक्त, कषाय, कटु.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence gives the sun, the moon and the refreshed world first, then the tastes increase and strength is built up.
questions.rule: दक्षिणायनगेऽर्के · शशिनि चाव्याहतबले · शिशिराभिर्भाभिः शश्वदाप्यायमाने · अरूक्षा रसाः प्रवर्द्धंते · बलं चोपचीयते.

questions.q: What does the invented line मेघे गर्जति मयूराः नृत्यन्ति mean, with a locative phrase like अर्के?
options: When the cloud thunders, peacocks dance
The cloud thunders for the peacocks
After the peacocks dance, it thunders
optionExplain: मेघे गर्जति is a phrase with its own verb form, not just a place.
Right: मेघे गर्जति (locative) sets the circumstance, as अर्के … does.
Nothing marks the peacocks as the aim.
The locative phrase is the circumstance, not a later event.
questions.explain: In the verse, locative phrases like अर्के, शशिनि, जगति give the circumstances, then the main clause follows.
questions.rule: Locative noun + locative participle = 'when X is so'.
questions.teaches: A noun with a participle, both in the locative (अर्के दक्षिणायनगे), sets the circumstance 'when X is so' before the main clause.

questions.q: What does भवति चात्र do in the text?
optionExplain: The chapter continues after this line.
No season is named in this line.
Right: 'And on this matter there is the following': then verses come.
No food is named in this line.
questions.explain: The line points ahead to what is said next.
questions.rule: भवति चात्र = and on this there is (the following).

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole line.
questions.rule: भवति = there is; च = and; अत्र = here, on this.

questions.q: The word for 'here, on this' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अत्र means here or on this matter.
questions.teaches: अत्र is a small word of place: here; with a matter it means on this.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्र?
optionExplain: चा is not a word.
आत्र is not a word.
A visarga here would not give चात्र.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here).

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: there is, and, here.

questions.q: Which is the correct joining of तथा + अत्र?
optionExplain: Right: आ + अ joins as आ, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
The long आ stays long; it is not shortened.
ऐ would come from आ + ए or ऐ, not from आ + अ.
ओ would come from आ + उ, not from आ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as चात्र: a or ā meeting a or ā gives ā.
questions.teaches: When अ or आ meets अ or आ, the two become one long आ (च + अत्र = चात्र; तथा + अत्र = तथात्र).

questions.q: In Śarad and Vasanta, how is the strength of visarga and ādāna graded?
optionExplain: Low is the grade of Varṣā and Nidāgha.
Right: शरद्वसन्तयोः मध्यम्: in Śarad and Vasanta, middling.
No season is said to have none.
Varṣā goes with Nidāgha and is low.
questions.explain: The second line gives Śarad and Vasanta as middling.
questions.rule: Śarad, Vasanta: middling; Varṣā, Nidāgha: low.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the grades, the strength and a season name.
questions.rule: मध्यम् = middling; हीनम् = low, poor; बलम् = strength; निदाघः = hot season.

questions.q: The word for 'low, poor' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: हीनम् is the grade given to Varṣā and Nidāgha.
questions.teaches: हीन means lacking, low; it is neuter to agree with बलम्.

questions.q: Which two seasons does the verse pair together with the grade 'low'?
optionExplain: That pair is middling, not low.
The verse does not pair these two.
Right: वर्षा निदाघयोः are joined and given हीनम्.
The verse does not pair these two.
questions.explain: The verse gives its pairs as: Hemanta-Śiśira, Śarad-Vasanta, Varṣā-Nidāgha.

questions.q: Put the three pairs of seasons in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse takes Hemanta and Śiśira first, then Śarad and Vasanta, then Varṣā and Nidāgha.
questions.rule: हेमंते शिशिरे च · शरद्वसंतयोः · वर्षा निदाघयोः.

questions.q: What does the invented word ग्रीष्मवसन्तयोः mean, built like शरद्वसन्तयोः?
options: In the many seasons from Grīṣma
Of or in the two, Grīṣma and Vasanta
optionExplain: A joined pair names two things, not one.
-योः is dual, not many.
The ending does not mean after.
Right: A joined pair with the dual ending -योः names both together.
questions.explain: शरद्वसन्तयोः = Śarad and Vasanta, the two; ग्रीष्मवसन्तयोः works the same way.
questions.rule: Joined pair + -योः = the two named, together.
questions.teaches: Two nouns joined into one word with the dual ending -योः name both together (शरद्वसन्तयोः, 'of or in Śarad and Vasanta').

questions.q: Because of the wind's coldness, what does the north do in this verse?
options: Makes the hair stand on end
optionExplain: Right: मरुच्छैत्यादुत्तरो रोमहर्षणः: from the wind's coldness the north causes horripilation.
Steaming rivers are in a later verse.
