questions.q: In an invented phrase शत्रुजित् नृपः, what does the king do?
optionExplain: 'Born of' would be -ज.
Nothing in -जित् means loved.
Right: -जित् at the end means overcoming the first part.
Nothing in -जित् means fearing.
questions.explain: क्लेदवातजित् is क्लेद-वात-जित्, overcoming dampness and Vāta; शत्रुजित् is overcoming enemies.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -जित् means 'overcoming' the first part (क्लेदवातजित्, शत्रुजित्).

questions.q: With what does line 2 say food and drink are taken when dense clouds rise?
optionExplain: Not named in the line.
Not named in the line.
Not named in the line.
Right: सक्षौद्रं: with honey.
questions.explain: Line 2 says अन्नपानं सक्षौद्रम्: food and drink with honey.

questions.q: Match each quality of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists six qualities; these are four of them.
questions.rule: परिशुष्क = well dried; लघु = light; उष्ण = hot; लवण = salty.

questions.q: The word for 'unctuous' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स्निग्ध is unctuous, the third quality of line 1.
questions.teaches: स्निग्ध is neuter accusative singular (printed स्निग्धम्), agreeing with the understood 'food' (भोजन) of line 1.

questions.q: Which three of these does line 1 name among the qualities?
optionExplain: Sweet is not named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
Bitter is not named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 names well dried, light, unctuous, hot, sour and salty; light, sour and unctuous are among them.

questions.q: Put the six qualities in the order of line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: well dried, light, unctuous, hot, sour, salty.
questions.rule: परिशुष्कम् · लघु · स्निग्धम् · उष्ण · अम्ल · लवणम्.

questions.q: Which is the correct joined form of नील + उत्पल (blue lotus)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ gives ओ, as in घन + उदये = घनोदये.
अ + उ is not simply shortened to उ.
अ + उ does not give औ.
अ + उ does not give आ.
questions.explain: घन + उदये joins as घनोदये: a short अ meeting उ gives ओ.
questions.teaches: A final अ before उ merges into ओ (घन + उदये = घनोदये, नील + उत्पल = नीलोत्पल).

questions.q: Which three does line 2 say the dwelling is free from?
options: Heavy dust, smoke and loud noise
Cold rain, hail and strong winds
optionExplain: These are not named in line 2.
Right: निर्दंश-मशक-उन्दुर: free from these three.
These are not named in line 2.
These are not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with the compound read as निर्दंशमशकोन्दुरं (printed निर्दशमशकोंदुरं): free from biting flies, mosquitoes and rats.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 2 names the dwelling and the three things it is free from.
questions.rule: भवनम् = dwelling; दंश = biting fly; मशक = mosquito; उन्दुर = rat.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of निः + दंश (printed निर्दश)?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish.
The visarga is not kept before द.
Right: A visarga before a voiced consonant turns into र् after इ.
A visarga before द does not become स्.
questions.explain: निः + दंश = निर्दंश: after इ the visarga becomes र् before the voiced द.
questions.rule: Visarga after इ/उ + voiced sound → र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ turns into र् before a voiced sound (निः + दंश = निर्दंश).

questions.q: Which pair of words in line 2 stand as opposites, with and without?
options: भवनं and च side by side
मशक and उन्दुर side by side
च and उन्दुर side by side
optionExplain: Neither word means with or without.
Both are things the dwelling is free from.
च means 'and'; उन्दुर is rat.
Right: स- means with and निर्- means without, whatever अग्नियान exactly is.
questions.explain: स- (with) + अग्नियान begin the first compound; निर्- (without) begins the second.

questions.q: Put the three things the dwelling is free from in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends: biting flies, mosquitoes, rats.

questions.q: In an invented phrase निर्जलं सरः, what is the lake?
optionExplain: Right: निर्- at the start means without, as in निर्दंश…
Full of would be a word like जलपूर्ण.
Nothing in निर्- means beside.
Nothing in निर्- means made of.
questions.explain: निर्- (from निः) means without: निर्जल = without water, as निर्दंश… = without biting flies.
questions.teaches: The prefix निः / निर् means 'without' (निर्दंश…, निर्जलम्).

questions.q: With whom does line 2 say the person should go?
options: With the foremost horses of the guard
With the foremost servants of the house
With the foremost teachers of the school
optionExplain: Horses are not named in line 2.
Right: यायात् करेणुमुख्याभिः: should go with the foremost she-elephants.
Servants are not named in line 2.
Teachers are not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 says यायात् करेणुमुख्याभिः: should go with the foremost she-elephants.
questions.rule: करेणु = she-elephant; मुख्या = foremost; यायात् = should go.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the person's tastes and dress.
questions.rule: स्नान = bathing; उद्वर्तन = ointment-rubbing; करेणु = she-elephant; चित्रवस्त्र = colourful clothes.

questions.q: Which phrase means one should go to the village?
optionExplain: This is the plain present: 'goes to the village'.
This is a past form: 'went to the village'.
Right: यायात् is the 'should go' form of the verb √या.
यातः is a participle, 'gone'; it is not a 'should' form.
questions.explain: यायात् in line 2 is 'should go', so ग्रामं यायात् is 'should go to the village'.
questions.teaches: The 'should go' form of √या is यायात्; the plain present is याति.

questions.q: Which list is the person said to be fond of in line 1?
options: Singing, dancing, dice-play, wine-drinking and music-making
Hunting, riding, archery, wrestling and other sports
Reading, writing, speech, silence and daily prayers
optionExplain: None of these is in line 1.
None of these is in line 1.
None of these is in line 1.
Right: प्रघर्ष, उद्वर्तन, स्नान and धूमगंधागुरु are the items of line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with …प्रियः, 'fond of', after the list of tastes.

questions.q: Put these four parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: rubbing, ointment-rubbing, bathing, smoke-scent-agaru.

questions.q: In an invented phrase वनविहारप्रियः, what is the person?
options: Fond of walking in the forest
Dear to the forest and its trees
Afraid of the forest and its beasts
Lord of the forest and its trees
optionExplain: Right: -प्रिय at the end means fond of the first part.
Here the person is the one who is fond, not the one who is dear to it.
Nothing in -प्रिय means afraid.
Nothing in -प्रिय means lord.
questions.explain: …गंधागुरुप्रियः is 'fond of … agaru scent'; वनविहारप्रियः is 'fond of forest walks'.
questions.rule: X-प्रिय (describing a person) = fond of X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -प्रियः, describing a person, means 'fond of' the first part (…अगुरुप्रियः, वनविहारप्रियः).

questions.q: What does the verb त्यजेत् at the end of line 2 mean?
optionExplain: त्यज् does not mean praise.
Right: त्यजेत् is the 'should' form of त्यज्: abandon, avoid.
त्यज् does not mean collect.
त्यज् does not mean measure.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with त्यजेत्, 'should avoid', which governs the items before it.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three items and the verb that governs them.
questions.rule: तुषार = frost; व्यायाम = exercise; अर्ककर = sun's ray; त्यजेत् = should avoid.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अर्ककरांस्त्यजेत्?
optionExplain: That would be written अर्ककरास्त्यजेत्, with no anusvara.
स्त्यजेत् is not a word.
Right: न् + त् is written ंस्त्: a nasal and स् appear between.
स्त्यजेत् is not a word.
questions.explain: अर्ककरान् (the sun's rays, accusative plural) + त्यजेत् (should avoid).
questions.teaches: A final -न् before त् gives ंस्त् (अर्ककरान् + त्यजेत् = अर्ककरांस्त्यजेत्).

questions.q: Which three of these does line 2 say to avoid, leaving out the unclear word?
optionExplain: Not named in this unit.
Right: the first item of line 2.
Water belongs to line 1, not line 2.
Right: an item of line 2.
Right: the last item of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 names frost, exercise and the sun's rays before the verb त्यजेत्.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse (the unclear middle word is left out).
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: frost, exercise, the sun's rays, should avoid.

questions.q: Which phrase means one should conquer anger?
optionExplain: This is the plain present: 'conquers anger'.
This is a past form: 'conquered anger'.
Two nouns: 'anger, victory', no verb.
Right: An accusative object plus a -एत् verb: 'should conquer anger'.
questions.explain: Like अर्ककरान् … त्यजेत्, the object is in the accusative and the verb ends in -एत्.
questions.teaches: A command is an accusative object plus a verb in -एत्: क्रोधं जयेत् = 'one should conquer anger'.

questions.q: What kind of clouds does the sky have in autumn, according to line 1?
options: No clouds at all in the sky
optionExplain: Right: शुभ्र = white, अभ्र = cloud.
शुभ्र means white, not black.
The compound names clouds the sky has.
शुभ्र means white, not red.
questions.explain: शरदि व्योम शुभ्राभ्रं: in autumn the sky has white clouds.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the picture of line 1.
questions.rule: शरदि = in autumn; व्योम = sky; पंक = mud; मही = earth.

questions.q: The word for 'earth' at the end of line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: मही is the earth, the subject of both lines.
questions.teaches: मही is feminine, nominative singular; the participle किंचित्पंकांकिता before it agrees with it.

questions.q: Which sandhi result is right for शुभ्र + अभ्रं?
optionExplain: The vowels do not simply drop.
Right: अ + अ gives आ.
अ + अ does not give ओ.
अ + अ does not give ऐ.
questions.explain: A short अ meeting अ merges into long आ: शुभ्राभ्रं.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: in autumn, sky, with white clouds, marked with a little mud, earth.

questions.q: What does an invented phrase श्वेतपुष्पा लता mean?
options: A white flower that is a creeper
A creeper beside a white flower
A creeper that is not flowering
optionExplain: The compound describes the creeper, not a flower.
Nothing in the compound means beside.
Right: A feminine compound ending in the noun is 'having X', like शुभ्राभ्रं 'with white clouds'.
Nothing in the compound means without flowers.
questions.explain: शुभ्राभ्रं (sky) = 'with white clouds'; श्वेतपुष्पा (creeper) = 'with white flowers'.
questions.rule: Bahuvrīhi: adjective + noun, describes the noun it agrees with.
questions.teaches: A compound of colour + noun can describe a noun as 'having' that thing (शुभ्राभ्रं व्योम, श्वेतपुष्पा लता).

questions.q: Because of what does the sun scatter sharp rays, according to line 1?
options: The arrival of the heavy masses of clouds
The rising of the river water
The blowing of the cold wind
The departure of the masses of clouds
optionExplain: विगम is departure, not arrival.
No river is named in line 1.
No wind is named in line 1.
Right: मेघौघविगमात्: from the departure of the cloud masses.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the cause in the ablative: मेघौघविगमात्, then the effect: the sun scatters sharp rays.
questions.rule: मेघौघविगमात् (from the departure of cloud masses) → रविः विक्षिप्ततीक्ष्णकिरणः.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the two pictures of the unit.
questions.rule: रविः = sun; दिशः = directions; विमल = clear; क्रौंच = krauñca bird.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of विगमात् + रविः?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before a voiced sound becomes द्.
The त् does not stay before the voiced र.
त् does not turn into a visarga here.
त् does not turn into न् here.
questions.explain: विगमात् + रविः joins as विगमाद्रविः: the final त् voices to द् before र.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a voiced sound becomes द् (विगमात् + रविः = विगमाद्रविः).

questions.q: Which phrase describes the directions in line 2?
options: Very dark and quite empty of any high flying birds
Very clear, crowded with lines of krauñca birds
Very clear and quite empty of birds and clouds
Very dark and crowded with heavy rain clouds
optionExplain: विमल is clear, not dark.
Right: अतिविमलाः क्रौंचमालाकुलाः दिशः.
आकुल means crowded with, not empty of.
Neither dark nor clouds is in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 says the directions are very clear (अतिविमलाः) and crowded with lines of krauñca birds.
questions.rule: अतिविमल + क्रौंचमालाकुल = very clear, crowded with krauñca lines.

questions.q: Put these words of the verse in order (words not listed are left out).
questions.explain: The verse runs: from the departure of cloud masses, the sun; very clear, crowded with krauñca lines, the directions.

questions.q: Which invented phrase means: from the departure of winter?
optionExplain: This is the nominative: 'the departure of winter'.
This is the locative: 'in the departure'.
Right: -आत् is the ablative ending: 'from, because of'.
This is the accusative: 'the departure' as an object.
questions.explain: मेघौघविगमात् is 'from the departure of the cloud masses'; the same -आत् ending gives शीतविगमात्.
questions.teaches: The ending -आत् (ablative singular of an -अ noun) gives the 'from / because of' sense (मेघौघविगमात्, शीतविगमात्).

questions.q: Which two does line 1 name as jostling?
optionExplain: These are not named in line 1.
These are not named in line 1.
These are not named in line 1.
Right: मीन and हंसौघ: fish and flocks of swans.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with the jostling (घट्टनैः) of fish (मीन) and flocks of swans (हंसौघ).
questions.rule: मीन = fish; हंस + ओघ = flock of swans; घट्टन = jostling.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four plain words build the picture of the unit.
questions.rule: कमल = lotus; मीन = fish; हंस = swan; सरस् = lake.

questions.q: The word for 'swan' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: हंस is the swan, joined with ओघ in हंसौघ ('flock of swans').
questions.teaches: हंस + ओघ = हंसौघ: अ + ओ gives औ.

questions.q: What does the ending of घट्टनैः tell us?
options: Of the many jostlings: genitive plural
In the many jostlings: locative plural
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural ending of an -अ noun.
The genitive plural would end in -आनाम्.
The locative plural would end in -एषु.
The nominative plural would end in -आः or -आनि.
questions.explain: घट्टनैः means 'by the jostlings': the cause that makes the waves in line 2.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of the verse (the damaged word is left out).
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: among the lotuses, fish, flocks of swans, by the jostling.

questions.q: Which word agrees with the neuter plural पद्मानि (lotuses)?
optionExplain: This is masculine singular.
Right: A neuter plural noun takes an adjective in -आनि, as सरांसि takes विमलानि.
This is feminine singular.
This is neuter singular.
questions.explain: सरांसि (neuter plural) goes with विमलानि; पद्मानि (neuter plural) takes the same ending.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender and number; for a neuter plural noun it ends in -आनि (सरांसि विमलानि).

questions.q: In this verse, when does the earlier-accumulated Pitta become aggravated?
options: When bodies used to the sun's heat are suddenly chilled by the rain
When bodies used to the rains' cold are slowly warmed, step by step
When bodies used to the rains' cold are suddenly heated by the sun
When bodies used to the rains' cold stay in the cold for long
optionExplain: The verse has it the other way round: used to cold, then heated.
सहसा means suddenly, not slowly.
Right: That is the condition in the verse: शीत का अभ्यास, then सहसा heat by the sun's rays.
The verse speaks of heating by the sun's rays, not of staying in the cold.
questions.explain: The verse joins वर्षाशीतोचितांगानाम् with सहसा … अर्करश्मिभिः तप्तानाम्: used to the rains' cold, suddenly heated by the sun's rays.
questions.rule: Used to the rains' cold + suddenly heated by sun-rays → earlier-accumulated Pitta is aggravated.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole event: sudden, heated, accumulated, aggravated.
questions.rule: सहसा = suddenly; तप्तानाम् = of those heated; संचितम् = accumulated; प्रकुप्यति = becomes aggravated.

questions.q: The word the verse uses for what becomes aggravated is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पित्तम् is the subject of प्रकुप्यति: it is the Pitta that was accumulated earlier.
questions.teaches: In this verse the aggravated thing is पित्तम् (neuter nominative singular), qualified by संचितम् 'accumulated'.
questions.rule: पित्तम् = Pitta, the subject of प्रकुप्यति.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सहसैव?
optionExplain: आ + अ would give सहसाव, not सहसैव.
इ + ए would give सहस्येव.
ओ + ए would give सहसवेव.
Right: आ + ए → ऐ, so सहसा + एव is written सहसैव.
questions.explain: सहसा 'suddenly' + एव 'just': the two join as ऐ.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order in which they stand.
questions.explain: The verse runs: those used to the rains' cold, suddenly by the sun's rays, heated, accumulated earlier, then Pitta is aggravated.
questions.rule: वर्षाशीतोचितांगानाम् · सहसैवार्करश्मिभिः · तप्तानाम् · संचितं पूर्वम् · तदा पित्तं प्रकुप्यति.

questions.q: An invented phrase says ग्रीष्मोचितांगानाम्. What does it mean?
options: Of those whose bodies are used to summer
Of those whose bodies are hurt by summer
Of those who have left summer behind
optionExplain: Right: X-उचित-अंग names bodies used to X, as in वर्षाशीतोचितांगानाम्.
उचित means suited or used to, not hurt.
Nothing in the compound means leaving behind.
Nothing in the compound means measuring.
questions.explain: ग्रीष्म + उचित → ग्रीष्मोचित (अ + उ → ओ): used to summer; then अंग 'body' and the genitive plural.
questions.rule: शीत + उचित = शीतोचित (अ + उ → ओ); X-उचित-अंग = (those) whose bodies are used to X.
questions.teaches: A compound X-उचितांग names those whose bodies are used to X: वर्षाशीतोचितांग, and the invented ग्रीष्मोचितांग; अ + उ joins as ओ.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit name among the recommended things?
optionExplain: Steaming is not named in this unit.
Right: विरेकः is named in the first line with शस्तम्.
Oil massage is not named in this unit.
Fasting is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The first line names the flow of blood and विरेकः, purgation, as recommended.
questions.rule: शस्तम् (recommended) governs: विरेक, अस्रश्रुति, शीतं लघ्वन्नपानम्, कषायस्वादुतिक्तकम्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the list carry its meaning.
questions.rule: शस्तम् = recommended; विरेकः = purgation; अस्रश्रुतिः = flow of blood; लघु = light; शीतम् = cold.

questions.q: The word for 'purgation' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: विरेकः (purgation) is the second item of the first line.
questions.teaches: विरेकः is a masculine nominative singular, 'purgation', one of the things called recommended.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विरेकोऽस्त्रश्रुतिः (read as अस्रश्रुतिः)?
optionExplain: Then the second word would lack its first letter.
ओऽ is one sign for both words; there is no extra ओ.
Right: (छपा रूप अस्त्र, पढ़ा अस्र.) अः + अ → ओऽ (visarga becomes उ, joins अ to make ओ, and अ is dropped as ऽ).
विरेकोः is not a form; the word is विरेकः.
questions.explain: विरेकः 'purgation' + अस्रश्रुतिः 'flow of blood'.

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the verse (leaving out the first, misprinted item).
questions.explain: After the misprinted first item the verse lists purgation, flow of blood, cold, light food and drink, then astringent-sweet-bitter.

questions.q: An invented phrase says मृद्वन्नम्, on the pattern of लघ्वन्नपानम् (light food and drink). What does it mean?
optionExplain: That would put मृदु in the genitive; here it stands as a plain first part.
Nothing in the word means 'no'.
Nothing in the word means 'that makes'.
Right: A describing word first, then the noun: soft + food.
questions.explain: मृदु + अन्नम् → मृद्वन्नम् (उ + अ → व् + अ): soft food, as लघु + अन्न = लघ्वन्न 'light food'.
questions.rule: Adjective + noun make one word (लघु + अन्न = लघ्वन्न 'light food'); उ before a different vowel → व्.
questions.teaches: An adjective can join its noun in one word, with उ + अ → व्+अ: लघ्वन्न 'light food', the invented मृद्वन्न 'soft food'.

questions.q: Which of these foods does the unit name in its list?
optionExplain: Right: यव is in the first line, after गोधूम.
Sesame is not named in this unit.
Mustard is not named in this unit.
Black pepper is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The first line lists śāli, ṣaṣṭika, godhūma, yava (barley), mudga, sitā and madhu.
questions.rule: First line: शालि, षष्टिक, गोधूम, यव, मुद्ग, सिता, मधु.

questions.q: Match each word of the list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five items of the list have clear meanings.
questions.rule: गोधूम = wheat; यव = barley; सिता = sugar; मधु = honey; द्राक्षा = grapes.

questions.q: The word for 'barley' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: यव is the fourth item of the first line.
questions.teaches: यव (barley) is one of the grains in the list, between गोधूम and मुद्ग.

questions.q: Which is the right translation of line 1?
options: Śāli and ṣaṣṭika rice, maize, barley, mudga, sugar and honey
Śāli and ṣaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mudga, sugar and honey
Śāli and ṣaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mudga, salt and honey
Śāli and ṣaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mudga, sugar and milk
optionExplain: गोधूम is wheat, not maize.
Right: Each word agrees with the glosses on the card.
सिता is sugar, not salt.
मधु is honey, not milk.
questions.explain: Only one word differs in each wrong option: the right one keeps wheat, sugar and honey.
questions.rule: गोधूम = wheat; सिता = sugar; मधु = honey.

questions.q: Put these five items in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The first line runs godhūma, yava, mudga, sitā, madhu.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of द्राक्षा + आमलकम् (invented list), on the pattern of पटोल + आमलक?
optionExplain: No य joins the two; the vowels merge.
आ + आ does not give ए.
Right: आ + आ joins as one long आ, as अ + आ in पटोलामलक.
The vowels must merge, not stand side by side.
questions.explain: पटोल + आमलक → पटोलामलक; likewise द्राक्षा + आमलकम् → द्राक्षामलकम्.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by आ joins as one long आ: पटोल + आमलक = पटोलामलक; the invented द्राक्षा + आमलकम् = द्राक्षामलकम्.

questions.q: Which rays does the unit name for the night?
optionExplain: These are named for the day (दिवा).
No stars are named.
No lamp is named.
Right: निशाकरकरैः is 'by the moon's rays', with निशि 'at night'.
questions.explain: रात (निशि) goes with निशाकर, the moon, and its rays.
questions.rule: दिवा = by day with the sun's rays; निशि = at night with the moon's rays.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Day pairs with the sun's rays, night with the moon's.
questions.rule: दिवा = by day; निशि = at night; दिवाकरकरैः = by the sun's rays; निशाकरकरैः = by the moon's rays; तोयम् = water.

questions.q: The word for 'water' in this unit is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तोयम् is the water that संतप्तम्, ल्हादितम् and अविषीकृतम् describe.
questions.teaches: तोयम् is a neuter word for water; संतप्तम् and the other describing words agree with it.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निशाकरकरैर्निशि?
optionExplain: Right: ऐः before a soft consonant (here न) becomes ऐर्.
The word is in the instrumental plural -ऐः, not -आः.
There is no अनिशि; निशि stands as it is.
A visarga before a soft consonant becomes र्, not स्.
questions.explain: निशाकर-करैः 'by the moon's rays' + निशि 'at night'. The print puts a stray space after the earlier करै.
questions.rule: ऐः + soft consonant → ऐर् (करैः + निशि = करैर्निशि).

questions.q: Put these words in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse says: by day, by the sun's rays, by the moon's rays, at night, heated, water.
questions.rule: दिवा · दिवाकरकरैः · निशाकरकरैः · निशि · संतप्तम् · तोयम्.

questions.q: Using दिन (day) in place of दिवा, which compound would mean the day-maker, on the pattern of दिवाकर?
optionExplain: दिन + अन्त = day + end; not a maker.
Right: X-कर 'maker of X': दिन 'day' + कर, as दिवा + कर in दिवाकर.
दिन + भक्त = day + devotee; not a maker.
दिन + मास = day + month; not a maker.
questions.explain: दिवाकर and निशाकर show the pattern 'maker of the day / of the night'; दिनकर follows it.
questions.rule: -कर at the end of a name: the maker of the first part (दिवाकर sun, निशाकर moon).
questions.teaches: A name ending in -कर means 'maker of' the first part: दिवाकर 'day-maker' is the sun, निशाकर 'night-maker' the moon; the made-up दिनकर follows the pattern.

questions.q: How does the first line describe this water to drink?
optionExplain: Nothing like this is said.
The comparison is with nectar, not honey.
Right: पाने ऽमृतोपमम् is 'in drinking, like nectar'.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: अमृत-उपमम् means like nectar; पाने means in drinking.
questions.rule: पाने अमृतोपमम् = like nectar to drink.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line is a string of five describing words.
questions.rule: निर्मलम् = clear; शुचि = pure; कालेन = by time; पक्वम् = matured; अमृतोपमम् = like nectar.

questions.q: Put these four descriptions of the water in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: clear, pure, matured by time, like nectar to drink.
questions.teaches: The water's four descriptions come in a fixed order: clear, pure, matured by time, like nectar to drink.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पानेऽमृतोपमम्?
optionExplain: ओ is not the ending of पाने (locative of पान).
This would be written पानामृतोपमम्.
मृत would change the sense to 'dead'.
Right: ए + अ keeps ए, and the lost अ is shown by ऽ.
questions.explain: पाने 'in drinking' + अमृतोपमम् 'like nectar'.
questions.rule: ए + अ → ए, with the avagraha ऽ for the dropped अ.

questions.q: Which TWO things does the first line say of the water?
options: It is matured by time (कालेन पक्वम्)
It is bitter as a bitter drug
optionExplain: Right: शुचि is named.
Right: कालेन पक्वम्.
Nothing is said of spices.
Nothing like this is said.
Nothing is said of salt.
questions.explain: Pure (शुचि) and matured by time (कालेन पक्वम्) are both in the line.
questions.rule: The first line: clear, pure, matured by time, like nectar.

questions.q: Which joined form of पद्म + उपमम् (invented) means like a lotus?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in अमृतोपमम्.
औ would come from अ + औ.
The अ would not simply vanish.
अ + उ does not give ऊ.
questions.explain: अमृत + उपम → अमृतोपम; so पद्म + उपम → पद्मोपम.
questions.teaches: अ followed by उ joins as ओ: अमृत + उपम = अमृतोपम; the invented पद्म + उपम = पद्मोपम 'like a lotus'.

questions.q: With what is the person anointed, according to the second line?
optionExplain: The anointing is cool, not warm.
Right: शीतोशीरविलेपनः is 'anointed with cool uśīra'.
Ash is not named.
Water is not named for anointing.
questions.explain: शीत-उशीर-विलेपन: anointing with cool uśīra.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up the two lines.
questions.rule: सरसीषु = in lakes; लघु = light; शुद्ध = clean; स्रग्वी = wearing a garland; विलेपन = anointing.

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order of the verse (leaving out the unclear first phrase and the verb).
questions.explain: The verse goes: in lakes, with light clean clothes and a garland, anointed with cool uśīra.
questions.teaches: The verse's sequence is: in lakes, then light clean clothes and a garland, then the cool uśīra anointing.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शीतोशीर-?
optionExplain: ओ + उ would give शीतवुशीर.
There is no ओशीर here.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, so शीत + उशीर is written शीतोशीर.
आ + उ also gives ओ, but शीता is not the word here.
questions.explain: शीत 'cool' + उशीर: the two vowels join as ओ.

questions.q: Which TWO things does the second line say about the person's dress?
optionExplain: Right: लघुशुद्धांबर.
Right: स्रग्वी.
Not said.
A garland is named.
Colour is not said.
questions.explain: The compound लघुशुद्धांबरस्रग्वी gives light clean clothes and a garland.
questions.rule: लघु-शुद्ध-अंबर-स्रग्वी = with light, clean clothes and a garland.

questions.q: An invented word शीतचन्दनविलेपनः (चन्दन = sandal), on the pattern of शीतोशीरविलेपनः, means which?
options: One who made the sandal paste
One anointed with cool sandal paste
optionExplain: Nothing in the word means selling.
Nothing in the word means dislike.
Nothing in the word means making.
Right: -विलेपनः describes a person anointed with the first part.
questions.explain: The compound names the person by his anointing: cool + sandal + anointing.
questions.rule: X-विलेपनः (a describing compound) = anointed with X.
questions.teaches: A describing compound ending in -विलेपनः names a person anointed with the first part: शीतोशीरविलेपन, the invented शीतचन्दनविलेपन.

questions.q: What does the first line say one should enjoy at nightfall?
optionExplain: Right: सेवेत चंद्रकिरणान् प्रदोषे: should enjoy the moon-rays at nightfall.
The line speaks of the moon, not the sun.
Darkness is not named.
No lamp is named.
questions.explain: चंद्र-किरणान् is the object of सेवेत.
questions.rule: सेवेत = should enjoy; चंद्रकिरणान् = the moon-rays; प्रदोषे = at nightfall.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words carry the line.
questions.rule: सेवेत = should enjoy; चंद्रकिरणान् = the moon's rays; प्रदोषे = at nightfall; सौधम् = mansion; आश्रितः = having resorted to.

questions.q: The word for 'at nightfall' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: प्रदोषे is the locative: at the start of the night.
questions.teaches: प्रदोषे is a masculine locative singular, giving the time at which the rays are to be enjoyed.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सौधमाश्रितः?
optionExplain: माश्रित is not a word.
Right: A final म् simply carries onto the next vowel: म् + आ → मा.
सौधमा is not a word.
A visarga after -अ before आ drops and the words stay apart (सौध आश्रितः); it would not give सौधमाश्रितः.
questions.explain: सौधम् 'mansion' + आश्रितः 'having resorted to'.
questions.rule: म् + vowel → म with that vowel (सौधम् + आश्रितः = सौधमाश्रितः).

questions.q: Put these phrases of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: should enjoy, the moon-rays, at nightfall, having resorted to the mansion.

questions.q: On the pattern of सेवेत 'should enjoy', what does लभेत (from लभ्) mean?
optionExplain: -एत does not make a past.
-एत does not make a future.
Right: -एत on a verb stem: the 'should' form, as सेवेत.
-एत does not make a participle.
questions.explain: सेवेत is a 3rd person singular optative middle; लभेत is the same kind of form.
questions.teaches: A verb stem + -एत gives the 'should' form (3rd singular, optative, middle): सेवेत 'should enjoy'; the form लभेत (from लभ्) 'should obtain' follows the same pattern.

questions.q: What is to be practised at all times, according to the second line?
optionExplain: The line says all the tastes.
The line says all the tastes.
The line asks for practice, not for giving them up.
Right: सर्वरसाभ्यासः is the practice of all the tastes.
questions.explain: सर्व-रस-अभ्यासः = practice of all the tastes, नित्यम् always.
questions.rule: नित्यं सर्वरसाभ्यासः = always practice of all the tastes.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the second line.
questions.rule: नित्यम् = always; सर्व = all; रस = taste; अभ्यासः = practice; ऋतौ = in the season.

questions.q: The first word of line 2, the word of time glossed on the card, is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नित्यम् opens the second line.
questions.teaches: नित्यम् is an indeclinable word, 'always'; it is the first word of the line.

questions.q: Which split fits सर्वरसाभ्यासः (all + taste + practice)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: रस + अभ्यास is written रसाभ्यास.
भ्यासः is not a word.
यासः would not give practice.
सर्वर is not a word.
questions.explain: Three words join: सर्व 'all', रस 'taste', अभ्यास 'practice'.

questions.q: Put these phrases of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: always, practice of all tastes, each one's own predominance, in each season.

questions.q: On the pattern of ऋतौ ऋतौ, what does the invented दिने दिने mean?
options: At the end of the day
optionExplain: Doubling does not mean 'only'.
Right: Saying the word twice means 'in each'.
Doubling does not mean 'end'.
Doubling does not mean two.
questions.explain: ऋतौ ऋतौ is 'in each season'; so दिने दिने is 'in each day'.
questions.rule: A word said twice (ऋतौ ऋतौ) = 'in each'.
questions.teaches: Saying a word twice gives 'each / every': ऋतौ ऋतौ 'in each season'; the invented दिने दिने 'each day'.

questions.q: What does this unit call the ṛtusaṃdhi?
options: The first seven days of each season only
The whole month that lies between two seasons
The last seven days of one season and the first seven of the next
The seven middle days of one season
optionExplain: Both the last and the first days are counted.
The unit counts seven days, not a month.
Right: ऋत्वोः अंत्यादिसप्ताहात्: from the last and first seven days of the two seasons.
The days named are at the end and the start.
questions.explain: अंत्य and आदि fix the last and the first seven days of two seasons.
questions.rule: ऋतुसंधि = last seven days of one season + first seven days of the next.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words carry the definition and the rule.
questions.rule: ऋतुसंधिः = junction of seasons; स्मृतः = is called; पूर्वः = former; अपरः = latter; क्रमात् = in due order.

questions.q: Put these phrases of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2: there, the former regimen to be given up, the latter to be taken up, in order.
questions.teaches: At the junction, the former regimen is given up first and the latter taken up, in due order.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सप्ताहादृतु-?
optionExplain: दृतु is not a word.
A visarga would not give द्.
दृतु is not a word.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्, so सप्ताहात् + ऋतु is written सप्ताहादृतु.
questions.explain: सप्ताहात् 'from the seven days' + ऋतु- (the start of ऋतुसंधिः).
questions.rule: Final त् + vowel → द् (सप्ताहात् + ऋतु = सप्ताहादृतु).

questions.q: Which TWO statements does this unit make?
options: The former season's regimen is to be given up
The latter regimen is to be taken up in due order
The latter regimen is to be given up
The junction lasts a whole month
The junction is the middle of a season
optionExplain: Right: पूर्वो विधिस्त्याज्यः.
Right: सेवनीयोऽपरः क्रमात्.
It is the former that is given up.
Seven days at each end are named.
It is the end of one and the start of the next.
questions.explain: The second line gives up the former and takes up the latter, in order.
questions.rule: पूर्वः विधिः त्याज्यः; अपरः सेवनीयः क्रमात्.

questions.q: On the pattern of सेवनीयः 'to be taken up', what does the invented पठनीयः mean?
optionExplain: Right: -अनीय makes a 'should be done' word.
A person who reads would end in -क.
'Having read' would end in -त्वा.
-अनीय does not make 'reading'.
questions.explain: सेवनीय and त्याज्य both say 'ought to be done'; पठनीय says 'ought to be read'.
questions.rule: -अनीय or -य on a verb = 'to be done' (सेवनीयः, त्याज्यः).
questions.teaches: A verb stem + -अनीय (or -य) gives 'to be done': सेवनीयः 'to be taken up', त्याज्यः 'to be given up'; the invented पठनीयः 'to be read'.

questions.q: From what may diseases born of unsuitability arise, according to this verse?
options: From changing slowly, step by step
From abruptly abandoning and taking up
From keeping to one regimen unchanged
From eating at the wrong hour
optionExplain: सहसा means suddenly; the step by step change is in unit 76.
Right: सहसा त्यागशीलनात् is 'from abandoning and taking up, suddenly'.
The verse speaks of abandoning and taking up, not of keeping on.
The verse says nothing about the hour of eating.
questions.explain: त्याग-शीलन is abandoning and taking up; सहसा makes it abrupt.
questions.rule: असात्म्यजाः रोगाः (diseases born of unsuitability) स्युः सहसा त्यागशीलनात्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words carry the verse.
questions.rule: असात्म्यजाः = born of unsuitability; रोगाः = diseases; सहसा = suddenly; त्यागशीलनात् = from abandoning and taking up; देहिनाम् = of embodied beings.

questions.q: The word for 'suddenly' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सहसा is in line 1, before त्यागशीलनात्.
questions.teaches: सहसा is an indeclinable word, 'suddenly'; it says how the abandoning and taking up is done.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ऋतुष्वेवंविधेष्वेव?
optionExplain: These pieces are not words.
ओ before ए would give अव, not व्.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: ऋतुषु + एवं → ऋतुष्वेवं.
The locative plural -षु would be lost.
questions.explain: ऋतुषु 'in the seasons', एवंविधेषु 'of such a kind', एव 'indeed'.
questions.rule: उ + different vowel → व् + vowel (ऋतुषु + एवं = ऋतुष्वेवं).

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives the disease first, its cause, then the seasons of such a kind, then the regimen for health.
questions.rule: असात्म्यजा हि रोगाः स्युः · सहसा त्यागशीलनात् · ऋतुष्वेवंविधेष्वेव · विधिः स्वास्थ्ये च देहिनाम्.

questions.q: On the pattern of असात्म्यजाः, what does the invented जलजाः mean?
optionExplain: 'Dwelling' would be a different ending.
'Giving' would be a different ending.
'Without' would be a different word.
Right: -ज at the end of a compound means 'born of' the first part.
questions.explain: असात्म्य-जाः is 'born of unsuitability'; जल-जाः is 'born of water'.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -ज names what is born of the first part: असात्म्यजाः 'born of unsuitability'; the invented जलजाः 'born of water'.

questions.q: What does the verb निर्दिश्यते in line 1 mean?
optionExplain: Right: A present passive, third person singular: it is prescribed.
The form is present, not past.
The form is passive, not future.
The form is passive: it is prescribed, not 'he prescribes'.
questions.explain: निर्दिश्यते is a 3rd sing. present passive of निस्-दिश्: 'is prescribed'.
questions.rule: -यते on a verb stem makes the present passive: निर्दिश्यते = is prescribed.

questions.q: Match each clear word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are the clear words of line 1.
questions.rule: निर्दिश्यते = is prescribed; अन्यरूपेषु = in those of another form; विधिः = regimen; अन्य = other.

questions.q: The word for 'regimen' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: विधिः is the subject of निर्दिश्यते.
questions.teaches: विधिः (regimen, masculine nominative singular) is what is prescribed.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निर्दिश्यतेऽन्यरूपेषु?
optionExplain: ओ is not the ending of the verb.
Right: ए + अ keeps ए, and ऽ shows the dropped अ.
The verb ends in -ते.
न्यरूप is not a word.
questions.explain: The verb निर्दिश्यते + अन्यरूपेषु 'in those of another form'.
questions.rule: ए + अ → ए, with the avagraha ऽ for the dropped अ.

questions.q: Put these clear words of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out the unclear word).
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: is prescribed, in those of another form, (unclear word), regimen.

questions.q: On the pattern of निर्दिश्यते 'is prescribed', which invented form means 'is read'?
optionExplain: This is the active: he reads.
This is the 'should' form: should read.
Right: -यते on the stem gives the 'is done' (present passive) form.
This is a past: he read.
questions.explain: निर्दिश्यते is a present passive; पठ्यते (from पठ्) is the same kind.
questions.teaches: A present passive ends in -यते: निर्दिश्यते 'is prescribed'; the invented पठ्यते 'is read'.

questions.q: What does the verse say one should follow?
optionExplain: The word is चर्याम्, regimen.
The junction is in unit 76; here it is the regimen.
बलात् is 'by strength', not what is followed.
Right: भजेत् चर्याम्: should follow the regimen.
questions.explain: भजेत् 'should follow' has चर्याम् 'regimen' as its object.
questions.rule: यथोत्तरं भजेत् चर्याम् = one should follow the regimen in succession.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words carry the verse.
questions.rule: यथोत्तरम् = in order of succession; भजेत् = should follow; चर्याम् = regimen; तत्र = there; बलात् = by strength.

questions.q: The word for 'regimen' in this verse is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चर्याम् is the object of भजेत्.
questions.teaches: चर्याम् is the feminine accusative singular of चर्या, 'regimen'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भजेच्चर्याम्?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before च becomes च्, so भजेत् + चर्याम् is written भजेच्चर्याम्.
This would be written भजेचर्याम्, with one च.
A visarga would not make च्च.
र्याम् is not a word.
questions.explain: भजेत् 'should follow' + चर्याम् 'regimen'.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in order.
questions.explain: The verse runs: in succession, should follow the regimen, there, of that, by strength, thus.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of यथा + उक्तम् (invented), on the pattern of यथोत्तरम्?
optionExplain: आ + उ does not give ऊ.
Right: आ + उ joins as ओ, as in यथा + उत्तरम्.
औ would come from आ + औ.
The vowels must join.
questions.explain: यथा + उत्तरम् → यथोत्तरम्; likewise यथा + उक्तम् → यथोक्तम्.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by उ joins as ओ: यथा + उत्तरम् = यथोत्तरम्; the invented यथा + उक्तम् = यथोक्तम् 'as said'.

questions.q: What does the closing line say the chapter is?
optionExplain: चतुर्थ is fourth, not third.
The name in the line is ऋतुचर्या.
Right: ऋतुचर्यानाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः is exactly that.
चतुर्थ is fourth, not fifth.
questions.explain: The colophon gives the name ऋतुचर्या and the number चतुर्थ.
questions.rule: इति ऋतुचर्यानाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः = Thus the fourth chapter, named Ṛtucaryā.

questions.q: Match each word of the closing line to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words make up the closing line, with the name.
questions.rule: इति = thus; नाम = named; चतुर्थः = fourth; अध्यायः = chapter.

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायः is the last word before the number.
questions.teaches: अध्यायः (masculine nominative singular) is 'chapter'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चतुर्थोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: ओध्यायः is not a word.
चतुर्थो is not the form of the word here; the card has चतुर्थः (nominative), which joins with अ as ओऽ.
The ending would then give चतुर्था अध्यायः.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.explain: चतुर्थः 'fourth' + अध्यायः 'chapter'.

questions.q: Put these parts of the closing line in order.
questions.explain: The line runs: thus, named Ṛtucaryā, the fourth chapter.

questions.q: What is the joined form of तृतीयः + अध्यायः (third chapter)?
optionExplain: Right: अः + अ → ओऽ, as in चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
This drops the visarga without the ओऽ rule.
ए is not the join of अः + अ.
The two words must join.
questions.explain: चतुर्थः + अध्यायः → चतुर्थोऽध्यायः; the same for तृतीयः.
questions.teaches: A word in -अः followed by अ joins as ओऽ: चतुर्थः + अध्यायः = चतुर्थोऽध्यायः; the invented तृतीयः + अध्यायः = तृतीयोऽध्यायः.

questions.q: What does the verb 'व्याख्यास्यामः' say?
optionExplain: That would be a past form; this one is future.
Right: The ending -स्यामः is the first person plural of the future: we shall.
The ending is first person plural, 'we', not 'he'.
Nothing here forbids; it is a promise.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is first person plural future: 'we shall explain'.

questions.q: Put the words of the formula in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, the Rogānutpādanīya chapter, we shall explain.

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' in the formula is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायम् means 'chapter'; it ends in -म् because it is what 'we shall explain'.
questions.teaches: अध्याय is the word for a chapter; in the formula it stands in the accusative (अध्यायम्) as the object of the verb.

questions.q: Which is the right split of the first word, अथातो?
optionExplain: तो is not a word here; the pieces are अथ and अतः.
आतः would not give अथातो; the second part starts with a short अ.
Right: अ + अ gives आ (अथातः); the visarga then becomes ओ before the voiced र of the next word.
अथ ends in -अ and takes no visarga.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore) = अथातः, and before the voiced र the visarga becomes ओ: अथातो.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Match each word of the formula to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole announcement.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; अध्याय = chapter; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.

questions.q: Which form means we shall go?
optionExplain: This is 'we go', the present.
This is 'we went', the past.
This is 'we should go', the wish form.
Right: -ष्यामः is the 'we shall' ending, like -स्यामः in व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.explain: The future 'we shall' ends in -ष्यामः or -स्यामः.
questions.teaches: The first person plural future ends in -स्यामः or -ष्यामः (व्याख्यास्यामः, गमिष्यामः): 'we shall …'.

questions.q: Which pair is named in the FIRST line of the verse?
optionExplain: Right: क्षव and तृट् both stand in the first line.
जृंभा and अश्रु are in the second line.
निद्रा and कास open the second line.
छर्दि and रेतस् close the second line.
questions.explain: The first line lists wind, stool, urine, sneeze, thirst, hunger.
questions.rule: First line: वात, विट्, मूत्र, क्षव, तृट्, क्षुधा.

questions.q: Match each urge to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word names an urge that the verse says is not to be held back.
questions.rule: क्षव = sneeze; तृट् = thirst; क्षुधा = hunger; जृंभा = yawning; अश्रु = tears.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'one should hold back' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: धारयेत् is the 'should' form of the verb धृ in its causative: one should hold back.
questions.teaches: धारयेत् ('one should hold back') with न makes a prohibition: न धारयेत् = one should not hold back.
questions.rule: न धारयेत् = one should not hold back.

questions.q: Which is the right split of धारयेद्वात-?
optionExplain: The verb form ends in -त्; there is no word धारयेद.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound, here व.
A visarga would not turn into द्.
Nothing here gives द् from -ते.
questions.explain: धारयेत् (one should hold back) + वात (wind): त् → द् before the voiced व.
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: Put these four urges of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The second line ends: yawning, tears, vomiting, semen.

questions.q: Which invented sentence means: one should not hold back a yawn?
optionExplain: Without न this says one should hold it back.
The object is not in the accusative (-ाम्) as the verse has it.
Right: Object in the accusative + न + धारयेत्, as in the verse.
This says 'he does not hold back', a plain statement, not 'one should not'.
questions.explain: The pattern is: urge (accusative) + न + धारयेत्.
questions.rule: वेगान् न धारयेत् = one should not hold back the urges.
questions.teaches: The verse's pattern for a prohibition is: the thing in the accusative + न + धारयेत् ('one should not hold back'); drop न and the sense reverses.

questions.q: From suppressing what does the unit say gulma and udāvarta arise?
optionExplain: Stool is not the cause named in these lines.
A sneeze is not mentioned here.
Thirst is not mentioned here.
Right: अधोवातस्य रोधेन: by suppression of the downward wind.
questions.explain: The first words are अधोवातस्य रोधेन, 'by suppression of the downward wind'.
questions.rule: अधोवातस्य रोधेन = by suppression of the downward wind.

questions.q: Put the four conditions of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: gulma, udāvarta, pain, fatigue.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Plain words of the unit: the cause, and some of its results.
questions.rule: अधोवात = downward wind; रोध = suppression; रुक् = pain; क्लम = fatigue; हृद्गद = heart ailment.
questions.teaches: A list of results can be one compound joined by 'and' (गुल्मोदावर्तरुक्क्लमाः): the last member carries the plural ending shared by all.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अधोवातस्य?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced sound (व).
Then the join would stay अधवातस्य, with no ओ.
आ + व gives अधावातस्य, not अधोवातस्य.
There is no word अधोः here; the ओ comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: अधः (downward) + वातस्य (of wind): अः → ओ before the voiced व.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Put the three parts of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line runs: retention of wind, urine and stool; damage to sight and agni; heart ailments.

questions.q: Which word means by effort, as रोधेन means by suppression?
optionExplain: -स्य means 'of effort'.
Right: -एन is the 'by, through' ending on a word like रोध.
-आत् means 'from effort'.
-ए means 'in effort'.
questions.explain: रोधेन is रोध + the 'by' ending -एन; यत्न works the same way.
questions.teaches: A word like रोध takes -एन for 'by, through' (रोधेन = by suppression); likewise यत्नेन = by effort.

questions.q: With which pair does the list of means open?
optionExplain: These come later in the list.
These stand in the middle.
Right: स्नेहस्वेदविधिः comes first.
Neither is named in this unit.
questions.explain: The list opens with स्नेहस्वेदविधिः, the method of oleation and sweating.

questions.q: Put the five means in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The unit runs: oleation-sweating method, wicks, foods, drinks, enemas.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Names of the means, plus the word that recommends them.
questions.rule: वर्त्ति = wick; भोजन = food; पान = drink; बस्ति = enema; शस्तम् = recommended.
questions.teaches: Several different things may share one neuter singular 'recommended' (शस्तम्) when the list is taken as a whole.

questions.q: Which is the right split of बस्तयश्चैव?
optionExplain: चै + व is not a word split; the pieces are च and एव.
श्चै is not a word.
श्च is only the joined form, not a word on its own.
Right: Visarga + च → श्च; च + एव → चैव.
questions.explain: बस्तयः (enemas) + च (and) + एव (indeed).
questions.rule: अः + च → श्च; अ + ए → ऐ.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit name among the recommended means?
optionExplain: Not named in this unit.
Right: named.
Not named in this unit.
Right: named.
Right: named.
questions.explain: Foods, drinks and enemas are in the list; induced vomiting and nasal drops are not named here.
questions.rule: Named: स्नेहस्वेदविधि, वर्ति, भोजन, पान, बस्ति.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of वायुः + तत्र?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स् (as विधिः + तत्र = विधिस्तत्र).
The visarga does not simply vanish before त.
र् comes before voiced sounds, not before त.
श comes before च, not before त.
questions.explain: विधिः + तत्र becomes विधिस्तत्र; वायुः + तत्र becomes वायुस्तत्र.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स् (स्नेहस्वेदविधिः + तत्र = स्नेहस्वेदविधिस्तत्र).

questions.q: Which condition does the first line name for stool suppression?
optionExplain: These belong to the downward-wind unit, not this one.
Right: पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट is the twisting of the calves.
Tremor is not in this unit.
Not in this unit.
questions.explain: Line 1 names calf cramps, nasal catarrh and head pain.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Plain words of the unit.
questions.rule: शकृत् = stool; प्रतिश्याय = nasal catarrh; शिरोरुज् = head pain; परिकर्त = cutting pain; हृदय = heart.

questions.q: Put the six conditions in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives three, line 2 gives three: calf cramps, catarrh, head pain; upward wind, cutting pain, heart obstruction.
questions.rule: पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट · प्रतिश्याय · शिरोरुज् · ऊर्ध्वं वायुः · परिकर्त · हृदयोपरोधन.
questions.teaches: The unit's genitive (शकृतः) leans on an understood 'suppression'; the six results come as two lines of three.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हृदयस्योपरोधनम्?
optionExplain: The ओ is made by the join; there is no word ओपरोधनम्.
The first word is the genitive हृदयस्य.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
परोधनम् is not the word; it is उपरोधनम्.
questions.explain: हृदयस्य (of the heart) + उपरोधनम् (obstruction): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit give for stool suppression?
optionExplain: Not in this unit.
Right: प्रतिश्याय.
Not in this unit.
Right: शिरोरुज्.
Right: परिकर्त.
questions.explain: Catarrh, head pain and cutting pain are all in the unit; gulma and stone are not.
questions.rule: Named: पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट, प्रतिश्याय, शिरोरुज्, परिकर्त, हृदयोपरोधन.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of गंगा + उदक?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ/आ + ओ or औ, not from उ.
A vowel meeting a vowel is joined in careful Sanskrit.
The long आ does not simply drop with उ.
Right: आ + उ → ओ, as in पिंडिका + उद्वेष्ट = पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट.
questions.explain: पिंडिका + उद्वेष्ट gives पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट; गंगा + उदक gives गंगोदक.
questions.teaches: A word ending in अ or आ followed by उ joins as ओ (पिंडिका + उद्वेष्ट = पिंडिकोद्वेष्ट; गंगा + उदक = गंगोदक).

questions.q: What does line 1 say passes through the mouth?
optionExplain: Right: विट्प्रवृत्ति: passing of stool.
Urine is not named in line 1.
Wind is not named in line 1.
Breath is not named in line 1.
questions.explain: मुखेन विट्प्रवृत्तिः = passing of stool through the mouth.
questions.rule: मुखेन विट्प्रवृत्तिः = stool passing through the mouth.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Plain words of the unit.
questions.rule: मुख = mouth; वेदना = pain; वंक्षण = groin; अश्मरी = stone; पूर्वोक्त = stated before.

questions.q: Put these items of the unit in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: stool through the mouth, earlier ailments; line 2: limb-breaking pain, stone, pains in three places.
questions.rule: मुखेन विट्प्रवृत्तिः · पूर्वोक्ता आमयाः · अंगभंग · अश्मरी · बस्तिमैंढ्रवंक्षणवेदनाः.
questions.teaches: A sentence may run past its line: here line 2 starts a new list whose cause is stated only in the next unit.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पूर्वोक्ताश्चामयाः?
optionExplain: शचा is not a word.
Right: Visarga + च → श्च; च + आ → चा.
The word is आमयाः, not मयाः.
There is no word आश्च.
questions.explain: पूर्वोक्ताः (stated before) + च (and) + आमयाः (ailments).
questions.rule: अः + च → श्च; अ + आ → आ.

questions.q: Which are named as places of pain in line 2?
optionExplain: Not named in this line.
Right: बस्ति here names a place of pain.
Not named in this line.
Right: मेढ्र (printed मैंढ्र).
Right: वंक्षण.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with pains of the bladder, penis and groin.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of रोगः + च?
optionExplain: The visarga does not just drop before च.
स् is for त, not for च.
Right: Visarga + च → श्च, as in पूर्वोक्ताः + च = पूर्वोक्ताश्च.
ओ comes before voiced sounds; च is not voiced.
questions.explain: विट्प्रवृत्तिः + च gives विट्प्रवृत्तिश्च; रोगः + च gives रोगश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श् (विट्प्रवृत्तिः + च = विट्प्रवृत्तिश्च; रोगः + च = रोगश्च).

questions.q: From suppression of what does line 1 say the ailments may arise?
optionExplain: Stool was the topic of the earlier units, not of this line.
A sneeze is not mentioned in this line.
Thirst is not mentioned in this line.
Right: मूत्ररोधात्: from suppression of urine.
questions.explain: The line opens with स्युः मूत्ररोधात्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Plain words of the first line.
questions.rule: मूत्र = urine; रोध = suppression; औषध = remedy; प्रायः = mostly; पूर्वे = the earlier ones.

questions.q: After the wicks, put the four remedies in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: wicks, anointing, immersion baths, sweating, enema treatment.
questions.teaches: The first three members are in one compound (…अवगाहाः) and the last two stand as separate words, all naming the remedy.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मूत्ररोधात्पूर्वे?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before प stays त्.
त्पूर्वे is not a word.
There is no word आत्पूर्वे.
A visarga would show in the print, not त्.
questions.explain: मूत्ररोधात् (from suppression of urine) + पूर्वे (the earlier ones).
questions.rule: Final त् before प is unchanged.

questions.q: Which are named as the remedy in this unit?
optionExplain: Not in this unit.
Right: named.
Not in this unit.
Right: named.
Right: named.
questions.explain: Line 2 names wicks, anointing, immersion baths, sweating and enema treatment.
questions.rule: Remedy: वर्ति, अभ्यंग, अवगाह, स्वेदन, बस्तिकर्म.

questions.q: Which word means from suppression of an urge?
optionExplain: -एन means 'by'.
Right: -आत् is the 'from' ending, as in मूत्ररोधात्.
-ए means 'in'.
-स्य means 'of'.
questions.explain: मूत्ररोधात् is 'from suppression of urine'; वेगरोधात् is 'from suppression of an urge'.
questions.teaches: A word like रोध takes -आत् for 'from, because of' (मूत्ररोधात् = from suppression of urine; वेगरोधात् = from suppression of an urge).

questions.q: What does line 2 recommend before the meal?
optionExplain: Wicks are not named in this unit.
Sweating is not named in this unit.
Right: प्राग्भक्ताच्छस्यते घृतम्: ghee is recommended before the meal.
Enemas are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The line says ghee is recommended before the meal.
questions.rule: प्राग्भक्तात् = before the meal; घृतम् = ghee.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the unit.
questions.rule: प्राग्भक्तात् = before the meal; घृत = ghee; विड्भेदि = stool-loosening; मूत्रज = arising from urine; शस्यते = is recommended.

questions.q: The word for 'ghee' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: घृतम् is the thing recommended; it is the subject of शस्यते.
questions.teaches: घृत is the word for ghee; ending -म् shows the neuter singular subject of 'is recommended'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विड्विबन्धोत्थेषु?
optionExplain: थेषु is not a word.
The ओ comes from the join; there is no word ओत्थेषु.
A visarga before उ would leave a gap (विड्विबन्ध उत्थेषु), not give ओ.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
questions.explain: विड्विबन्ध (retention of stool) + उत्थेषु (arising from): अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Leaving out the doubtful 'पाने च' and the small words, put the phrases of the unit in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: food and drink, stool-loosening, in the ailments from stool retention; line 2: from urine, ghee before the meal.
questions.rule: अन्नपानम् · विड्भेदि · विड्विबन्धोत्थेषु यक्ष्मसु · मूत्रजेषु · प्राग्भक्ताच्छस्यते घृतम्.

questions.q: Which word means in forests?
optionExplain: Right: -एषु is the 'in' ending in the plural, as in मूत्रजेषु 'in those arising from urine'.
-ऐः means 'by'.
-आनाम् means 'of'.
-एन means 'by' (singular).
questions.explain: मूत्रजेषु is the 'in (those)' form; वन works the same: वनेषु.
questions.teaches: A plural word with -एषु means 'in …' (विड्विबन्धोत्थेषु, मूत्रजेषु = in those arising from…); likewise वनेषु = in forests.

questions.q: Which is the right split of एतच्च?
optionExplain: च्च is not a word.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्.
A visarga before च would give श्च.
श्च is not a word; the word is च, 'and'.
questions.explain: एतत् (this) + च (and): त् + च → च्च.

questions.q: Match each plain word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Only the clear words are tested.
questions.rule: एतत् = this; च = and; संज्ञितम् = is named; धारणात् = from holding back; पुनः = again.

questions.q: The word for 'again' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पुनः means 'again'; the visarga may be dropped when typing.
questions.teaches: पुनः is a word that never changes its ending; it means 'again'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of धारणात्पुनः?
optionExplain: त्पुनः is not a word.
There is no word आत्पुनः.
Right: A final त् before प stays त्.
A visarga would show in the print, not त्.
questions.explain: धारणात् (from holding back) + पुनः (again).
questions.rule: Final त् before प is unchanged.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: avapīḍaka, this, and, is named, from holding back, again.
questions.rule: अवपीडकम् · एतत् · च · संज्ञितम् · धारणात् · पुनः.

questions.q: Which is the joined form of तत् + च?
optionExplain: The join changes the त.
द् is for voiced sounds; च is not voiced.
No letter is added or dropped like this.
Right: Final त् before च becomes च्, as in एतत् + च = एतच्च.
questions.explain: एतत् + च gives एतच्च; तत् + च gives तच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च् (एतत् + च = एतच्च; तत् + च = तच्च).

questions.q: Which urge does the unit's first word, उद्गारस्य, name?
optionExplain: Right: उद्गार is a belch.
A sneeze is the topic of unit 11.
Cough is in the list of results, not the urge here.
Hiccups are in the list of results, not the urge here.

questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the six results in the order of the verse.

questions.rule: अरुचि · कंप · विबंध · आध्मान · कास · हिध्मा.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Names of the results listed.
questions.rule: अरुचि = distaste for food; कंप = tremor; आध्मान = distension; कास = cough; हिध्मा = hiccups.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates: अरुचि is the lack of taste or liking for food.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which is the right split of हृदयोरसोः?
optionExplain: रसोः is not the word; it is उरसोः.
Right: The pair 'heart and chest' (हृदय-उरस्) in the dual, 'in heart and chest': अ + उ → ओ.
The ओ is made by the join; there is no word ओरसोः.
A visarga before उ would give हृदय उरसोः, not ओ.
questions.explain: हृदय (heart) + उरसोः (the pair 'heart and chest' in the dual: in heart and chest): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which of these does the unit name as results?
optionExplain: That is in the stool unit.
Right: कंप.
That is in the sneeze unit.
Right: कास.
Right: हिध्मा.
questions.explain: Tremor, cough and hiccups are in the list; calf cramps and head pain are not.
questions.rule: Results: अरुचि, कंप, विबंध, आध्मान, कास, हिध्मा.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which word means like a snake?
optionExplain: -स्य means 'of a snake'.
-एण means 'by a snake'.
Right: -वत् at the end means 'like, as for', as in हिध्मावत्.
-तः means 'from a snake'.
questions.explain: हिध्मावत् is 'like hiccup'; सर्पवत् is 'like a snake'.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -वत् means 'like, as for' the first part (हिध्मावत् = as for hiccups; सर्पवत् = like a snake).
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: From holding back which urge does the first line list its results?
optionExplain: A belch was the topic of unit 10.
Cough is not the urge in this unit.
A yawn is not the urge in this unit.
Right: क्षुतेः: from a sneeze.
questions.explain: The first line ends with क्षुतेः, 'from a sneeze'.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the four results of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: head pain, weakness of the senses, stiffness of the neck, ardita.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the two lines.
questions.rule: शिरोर्ति = head pain; इन्द्रिय-दौर्बल्य = weakness of the senses; मन्या-स्तंभ = stiffness of the neck; अंजन = collyrium; नावन = nasal drops.
questions.teaches: In a compound the last member names the thing, the earlier ones qualify it: मन्या-स्तंभ is 'stiffness of the neck'.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which is the right split of the printed शिरोर्ति?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced sound; here the अ of अर्ति is absorbed.
ओर्ति is not a word.
र्ति is not a word.
उर्ति is not a word.
questions.explain: शिरः (head) + अर्ति (pain): शिरोऽर्ति, printed here without the avagraha.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Leaving out the last member (arka), put the four means in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: sharp smoke, collyrium, sniffing, nasal drops, (then arka).
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which word means by fruits?
optionExplain: -एन means 'by a fruit' (singular).
Right: -ऐः is the plural 'by' ending, as in विलोकनैः.
-एषु means 'in fruits'.
-आनाम् means 'of fruits'.
questions.explain: विलोकनैः is 'by lookings'; फलैः is 'by fruits'.
questions.teaches: A plural word in -ऐः means 'by, through' (विलोकनैः = by looking, among many means; फलैः = by fruits).
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What does the verse say to do with a held-back sneeze?
optionExplain: The verse says the opposite.
The verse gives an action: bring it on.
Right: प्रवर्त्तयेत्क्षुतिं सक्ताम्: one should bring on the held-back sneeze.
No waiting is mentioned.
questions.explain: प्रवर्त्तयेत् = one should bring on; क्षुतिं सक्ताम् = the held-back sneeze.
questions.rule: प्रवर्त्तयेत् क्षुतिं सक्ताम् = one should bring on the held-back sneeze.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the phrases of the unit in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The unit runs: bring on the sneeze; sweating and anointing; wind-relieving food; ghee after the meal.
questions.rule: प्रवर्त्तयेत्क्षुतिं सक्तां · स्वेदाभ्यंगौ च शीलयेत् · योज्यं वातघ्नमन्नं च · घृतं चोत्तरभक्तकम्.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the unit.
questions.rule: सक्त = held back; स्वेद-अभ्यंग = sweating and anointing; योज्य = to be applied; उत्तरभक्तक = after the meal; शीलयेत् = one should practise.
questions.teaches: A word in -य like योज्य can mean 'to be done' (to be applied): the thing is fit or due to be used.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which is the right split of चोत्तरभक्तकम्?
optionExplain: त्तरभक्तकम् is not a word.
The ओ is made by the join; there is no word ओत्तरभक्तकम्.
A visarga would not join to give चोत्त-.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
questions.explain: च (and) + उत्तरभक्तकम् (after the meal): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which does the unit say should be done or applied?
optionExplain: The unit says after, not before.
Right: स्वेदाभ्यंगौ शीलयेत्.
Not named in this unit.
Right: स्वेदाभ्यंगौ शीलयेत्.
Right: घृतं चोत्तरभक्तकम्.
questions.explain: Sweating, anointing and ghee after the meal are named; ghee before the meal and looking at the sun are not.
questions.rule: Named: स्वेद, अभ्यंग, वातघ्न अन्न, उत्तरभक्त घृत.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which word means two feet, as स्वेदाभ्यंगौ names a pair?
optionExplain: Right: The dual of an a-word ends in -औ, as in स्वेदाभ्यंगौ.
-आः is the plural 'feet'.
-म् is one foot.
-एन means 'by a foot'.
questions.explain: स्वेदाभ्यंगौ names a pair; पादौ is the pair of feet.
questions.teaches: The dual of a word in -अ ends in -औ in the nominative and accusative (स्वेदाभ्यंगौ = two things; पादौ = two feet).
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: From restraining which urge does this verse say dryness, deafness and giddiness arise?
optionExplain: Anger is not named in this verse.
Right: तृष्णाया निग्रहात्: from restraining thirst.
Laughter is not named in this verse.
Weeping is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The second line opens with तृष्णाया निग्रहात्, 'from restraining thirst'; the troubles of the first line follow from it.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each trouble named in line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are five of the six troubles that follow from restraining thirst; the sixth is अंगसाद, limb-weariness.
questions.rule: शोष = dryness; बाधिर्य = deafness; संमोह = bewilderment; भ्रम = giddiness; हृद्गद = heart ailment.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the six troubles of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: dryness, limb-weariness, deafness, bewilderment, giddiness, heart ailments.
questions.rule: शोष → अंगसाद → बाधिर्य → संमोह → भ्रम → हृद्गद.
questions.teaches: A compound that strings together nouns of one kind (a dvandva) names separate items; here शोष, अंगसाद, बाधिर्य, संमोह, भ्रम, हृद्गद are six troubles.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: One word is wrong in: 'In that case every warming procedure is beneficial.' Which?
optionExplain: सर्वः means every.
विधिः means procedure.
Right: शीतः means cooling, not warming.
हितः means beneficial.
questions.explain: The line says शीतः सर्वः विधिः हितः: every cooling procedure is beneficial.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: of thirst, from restraining, in that case, cooling, every, procedure, beneficial.
questions.rule: तृष्णाया · निग्रहात् · तत्र · शीतः · सर्वो · विधिः · हितः.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: By the pattern of तृष्णाया निग्रहात्, what does an invented क्रोधस्य निग्रहात् mean?
options: Of the one who restrains anger
optionExplain: निग्रहात् is 'from restraining', not a person.
The genitive names what is restrained; the anger is not the result.
There is no 'with' and no 'to restrain' in the phrase.
Right: क्रोधस्य = of anger; निग्रहात् = from restraining.
questions.explain: A genitive naming the urge (तृष्णाया, क्रोधस्य) plus निग्रहात् says 'from restraining that urge'.
questions.rule: [urge in genitive] + निग्रहात् = from restraining [that urge].
questions.teaches: The urge stands in the genitive and निग्रहात् (ablative) says 'from restraining': तृष्णाया निग्रहात् = from restraining thirst.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which four words describe the meal named in line 2?
optionExplain: Right: लघु स्निग्धमुष्णमल्पं च भोजनम्.
All four are the opposite of the verse's words.
The second word is स्निग्ध, unctuous, not dry.
The third word is उष्ण, warm, not cold.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives four describing words for भोजन: लघु, स्निग्ध, उष्ण, अल्प.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four describing words and the noun they go with.
questions.rule: लघु = light; स्निग्ध = unctuous; उष्ण = warm; अल्प = small in quantity; भोजन = meal.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What does the ending of योज्यम् show?
optionExplain: A gerundive looks forward ('is to be'), not back.
Right: The data labels योज्यम् a gerundive of √युज्, 'to be applied'.
A doer would end in -ता or -क, not -ज्यम्.
A wish would be an optative verb, like -एत्.
questions.explain: योज्य comes from √युज् with the -य ending that says 'to be done'; the neuter -म् agrees with भोजनम्.
questions.rule: A form in -य built from a root (योज्य from √युज्, कार्य from √कृ) = is to be done.
questions.teaches: A form in -य built on a root (योज्य from √युज्, कार्य from √कृ) is a gerundive: 'is to be applied / done'.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: One word is wrong in: 'A light, unctuous, warm and large meal is to be applied.' Which?
optionExplain: लघु means light.
उष्णम् means warm.
Right: अल्पम् means small in quantity, not large.
स्निग्धम् means unctuous.
questions.explain: The fourth word is अल्पम्, small in quantity.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the six troubles of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: limb-breaking, distaste for food, exhaustion, emaciation, colic pain, giddiness.
questions.rule: अंगभंग → अरुचि → ग्लानि → कार्श्य → शूल → भ्रम.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: An invented phrase says लघु उष्णं जलम्. What does it describe?
options: A light that warms the water
Water of the light and the warmth
Water that is neither light nor warm
optionExplain: Nothing in the phrase makes जलम् an object of warming.
There is no 'of' ending on the two adjectives.
There is no word of negation.
Right: लघु and उष्णं are neuter and agree with the neuter जलम्.
questions.explain: Describing words take the gender, case and number of their noun, as लघु स्निग्धमुष्णमल्पं go with भोजनम्.
questions.teaches: Describing words agree with their noun (here neuter singular): लघु स्निग्धम् उष्णम् अल्पम् भोजनम्, so लघु उष्णं जलम् = light, warm water.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What does line 2 call desirable in that case?
optionExplain: Right: स्वप्नः and संवाहनानि are both named; च joins them.
Neither is named in this verse.
संवाहनानि च adds massage.
स्वप्नः names sleep as well.
questions.explain: Line 2 says तत्र इष्टः स्वप्नः संवाहनानि च: sleep and massage are desirable.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each trouble of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The five troubles of line 1 in plain words.
questions.rule: मोह = bewilderment; मूर्च्छा = fainting; अक्षिगौरव = heaviness of the eyes; आलस्य = laziness; जृंभिका = yawning.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What is the right split of तत्रेष्टः in line 2?
optionExplain: ष्टः is not a word.
Right: अ + इ join as ए: तत्र + इष्टः = तत्रेष्टः.
एष्टः is not a word; the second word is इष्टः.
तत्रा is not the word; it is तत्र.
questions.explain: The printed तत्रेष्टः is तत्र (in that case) + इष्टः (desirable).
questions.teaches: Short अ followed by इ joins as ए: तत्र + इष्टः = तत्रेष्टः.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Which of these does the verse name as desirable in that case? Pick all that apply.
optionExplain: Named in line 2.
Named in line 2.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 names sleep and massage only.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the five troubles of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: bewilderment, fainting, heaviness of the eyes, laziness, yawning.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Join वृक्षः + च the way अंगमर्दः + च is joined in line 2. Which is right?
optionExplain: The visarga does not become ओ before च.
The visarga does not simply drop out.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: अंगमर्दः + च = अंगमर्दश्च.
Before च the visarga is श्, not स्.
questions.explain: The printed अंगमर्दश्च shows the join of a visarga with च.
questions.teaches: A visarga followed by च becomes श्: अंगमर्दः + च = अंगमर्दश्च, so वृक्षः + च = वृक्षश्च.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What does the verse say increases when a cough is suppressed?
optionExplain: Thirst is not named in this verse.
Yawning is not named in this verse.
Hunger is not named in this verse.
Right: तद्वृद्धिः: the increase of that (the cough).
questions.explain: तत् refers back to the cough, so तद्वृद्धिः is its (the cough's) increase.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the effects in plain words; the sixth is शोष, wasting.
questions.rule: श्वास = breathlessness; अरुचि = distaste for food; हृदामय = heart ailment; हिध्मा = hiccup; तद्वृद्धि = its increase.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: What is the right split of कार्योऽत्र in line 2?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ, and the अ is marked by ऽ.
अ + अ would give आ (कार्यात्र), not ओऽ.
-औ before अ would give आव्, not ओऽ.
इत्र is not a word.
questions.explain: कार्यः (to be done) + अत्र (here) = कार्योऽत्र.
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before a following अ, which is marked by ऽ: कार्यः + अत्र = कार्योऽत्र.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: One word is wrong in: 'From suppressing a cough: its decrease, breathlessness, distaste for food.' Which?
optionExplain: श्वास is breathlessness.
Right: वृद्धि is increase, not decrease.
अरुचि is distaste for food.
रोध is suppression.
questions.explain: The first effect is तद्वृद्धिः, its increase.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: Put the six effects in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the increase, breathlessness, distaste and heart ailments; line 2 adds wasting and hiccup.
questions.rule: तद्वृद्धि → श्वास → अरुचि → हृदामय → शोष → हिध्मा.
questions.section: डकार, छींक, प्यास, भूख, नींद, खाँसी, जम्भाई

questions.q: An invented phrase says ज्वरहा क्रियाक्रमः. By the pattern of कासहा विधिः, what does it name?
options: A course of treatment that brings fever
A fever that ends the course
A course of treatment that relieves fever
The fever of the course of treatment
optionExplain: -हा does not mean bringing.
The fever is the thing relieved, not the doer.
Right: -हा names what removes the first part: कासहा = cough-relieving.
There is no 'of' ending.
