-एत् does not give a past action.
There is no causing ending.
पठेत् is a verb, not a describing word.
questions.explain: The data labels भजेत् a third person singular optative: 'one should'.
questions.teaches: A verb ending in -एत् (optative) says 'one should': भजेत् = one should take, पठेत् = one should read.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: By what does line 2 say all diseases arise?
options: By holding back the urges only
By forcing out and holding back
By forcing out the urges only
By neither; they arise from food
optionExplain: उदीरण, forcing out, is named as well.
Right: वेगोदीरणधारणैः: both forcing out and holding back the urges.
धारण, holding back, is named as well.
Food is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: वेग + उदीरण + धारणैः: the instrumental plural gives 'by' for both.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words from the two lines.
questions.rule: उदीरण = forcing out; धारण = holding back; क्षीण = wasted; आर्त = afflicted; रोगाः = diseases.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: What is the right split of वेगोदीरणधारणैः?
optionExplain: दीरण is not a word.
वेगा would give आ in the join, not ओ.
Right: अ + उ join as ओ: वेग + उदीरण = वेगोदीरण.
ओदीरण is not a word; the ओ comes from the join.
questions.explain: वेग (urge) + उदीरण (forcing out) + धारणैः (by holding back).
questions.teaches: Short अ followed by उ joins as ओ: वेग + उदीरण = वेगोदीरण.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: One word is wrong in: 'Some diseases arise from forcing out and from holding back the urges.' Which?
optionExplain: रोगाः means diseases.
उदीरण is forcing out.
वेग is urge.
Right: सर्वे means all.
questions.explain: Line 2 says सर्वेऽपि रोगाः, all diseases.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: Put the parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: afflicted by thirst and colic, one should give up, wasted, vomiting stool, suppressor of urges.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: An invented phrase says सत्यवादिनम्. By the pattern of वेगरोधिनम्, what does it name?
optionExplain: Right: -इनम् names the one who does it: वेगरोधिनम् = one who holds back urges.
There is no 'of' ending.
There is no negation.
"By" would be an ending like -ेन or -ैः.
questions.explain: रोधिन् is a doer of रोध, holding back; सत्यवादिन् is a doer of speaking truth.
questions.teaches: The ending -इन् (accusative -इनम्) names the one who does the action: वेगरोधिनम् = one who holds back urges, सत्यवादिनम् = one who speaks the truth.
questions.section: आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेग

questions.q: In line 2, what is said to become provoked (प्रकुप्यति)?
optionExplain: साधन is the thing specified in line 1; it is not what is provoked.
Right: पवनः is the subject of प्रकुप्यति: the wind (vāta) becomes provoked.
No such person is named in the line.
तत्र means 'there'; it is not the subject of the verb.
questions.explain: पवनः (wind) is nominative, and प्रकुप्यति (becomes provoked) is its verb.
questions.rule: पवनः प्रकुप्यति = the wind becomes provoked.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins: specified, remedy, there, chiefly.
questions.rule: निर्दिष्टम् = specified; साधनम् = remedy; तत्र = there; भूयिष्ठम् = chiefly.

questions.q: The word for 'generally, mostly' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: प्रायः means generally or mostly: it marks what happens as a rule, not without exception.
questions.teaches: प्रायः = 'generally': the line does not say the wind is provoked every time.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तैस्ततश्चानेकधा?
optionExplain: स्ततः is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga of तैः.
नेकधा is not a word; the आ belongs to च + अनेकधा.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्; a visarga before च becomes श्; च + अ joins as चा.
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga of ततः.
questions.explain: Four words: तैः (by them), ततः (therefore), च (and), अनेकधा (in many ways).
questions.rule: Visarga + त → स्त; visarga + च → श्च; अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse (leaving out च and यत्).
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: by them, therefore, in many ways, generally, the wind, becomes provoked.
questions.rule: तैः · ततः · अनेकधा · प्रायः · पवनः · प्रकुप्यति.

questions.q: Which word means two-fold (in two ways), made like अनेकधा (in many ways)?
optionExplain: द्वयम् is a noun, 'a pair'.
द्वितीयः is 'second', an ordinal.
द्विकम् is 'a set of two', not 'in two ways'.
Right: -धा after a number word means 'in so many ways': द्वि + धा = in two ways.
questions.explain: -धा after a number or quantity word gives 'in ... ways': अनेकधा, द्विधा.
questions.teaches: The ending -धा after a number or quantity word means 'in ... ways' (अनेकधा, द्विधा).

questions.q: Which three things does the verse tell the afflicted person to use?
optionExplain: Right: अन्न-पान-औषध is a joined list of exactly these three.
The compound names food and drink as well.
औषध (medicine) is the third member of the list.
Rest and sleep are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: अन्नपानौषधम् = अन्न (food) + पान (drink) + औषध (medicine).

questions.q: Put the three members of अन्नपानौषधम् in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: food, drink, medicine.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two lines are built from these words.
questions.rule: आर्तः = afflicted person; युञ्जीत = should employ; विकारेषु = in the disorders; यथास्वम् = according to each one's own; चिकित्सितम् = treatment.
questions.teaches: यथास्वम् = 'according to each one's own'; युञ्जीत is a 'should' form of the verb 'to employ'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of युञ्जीतार्तोऽनुलोमनम्?
optionExplain: अर्तो is not a word; the word is आर्तः.
Right: अ + आ joins as आ, and आर्तः + अ becomes आर्तोऽ with an avagraha.
नुलोमनम् is not a word; अनुलोमनम् begins with अ.
तः is not a word here; the word is आर्तः.
questions.explain: Three words: युञ्जीत (should employ), आर्तः (afflicted person), अनुलोमनम् (anulomana).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; आर्तः + अ → आर्तोऽ (visarga after अ, before अ, gives ओ plus avagraha).

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: food-drink-medicine, for it, should employ, the afflicted, anulomana.

questions.q: Which means according to one's strength, made like यथास्वम्?
optionExplain: यथा- stands at the start of the word, not at its end.
अ- would mean 'without strength'.
Right: यथा- at the start gives 'according to': यथा + बलम् = according to strength.
-वत् means 'having strength', not 'according to'.
questions.explain: यथास्वम् = यथा + स्वम्: 'according to one's own'. In the same way यथाबलम् = according to strength.
questions.teaches: A word beginning with यथा- means 'according to ...' (यथास्वम्, यथाविधि, यथाकालम्, यथाबलम्).

questions.q: On what, though it is spotless, does mud necessarily form?
optionExplain: No cloth is named in the unit.
No river is named in the unit.
No mirror is named in the unit.
Right: मणौ is 'on a gem': mud forms even on the spotless gem.
questions.explain: मणौ = on a gem; the verse says mud necessarily forms there, even on a gem without mud.
questions.rule: मणि: even when spotless, mud forms.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the comparison and the advice.
questions.rule: क्रमात् = in due course; अवश्यम् = necessarily; यथाकालम् = at the proper time; मलानाम् = of the impurities.

questions.q: The word for 'mud' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पंकः is mud: it forms necessarily on the gem, even when the gem is spotless.
questions.teaches: पंक = mud; अपंक = without mud (spotless).

questions.q: Which is the right split of क्रमादपंकेऽपि?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्; ए + अ joins as ए with an avagraha.
दपंके is not a word; the द् comes from the final त् of क्रमात्.
That would lose the अ of अपंके, 'without mud'.
इपि is not a word; the word is अपि.
questions.explain: Three words: क्रमात् (in due course), अपंके (spotless), अपि (even).
questions.rule: Final त् + vowel → द्; ए + अ → ए + avagraha (ऽ).

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out अपंकेऽपि).
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: in due course, on the gem, mud, necessarily, comes to be, since.
questions.rule: क्रमात् · मणौ · पंकः · अवश्यम् · भवेत् · यतः.

questions.q: Which word means faultless (without fault), made like अपंक (without mud)?
optionExplain: स- means 'with', so this is 'with fault'.
Right: अ- before a noun can mean 'without': अ + दोष = without fault.
बहु- means 'many': 'with many faults'.
-वत् means 'having': 'having faults'.
questions.explain: अपंक is अ + पंक: 'without mud'. In the same way अ + दोष = without fault.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- on a noun can give 'without' that noun (अपंक 'without mud', अदोष 'without fault').

questions.q: What do they produce, according to this unit?
options: Remedies that are hostile to diseases
Diseases that are hostile to remedies
Medicines that come after a long time
optionExplain: The words are the other way round: the diseases are hostile to remedies.
The verse does not say this.
Right: भेषजद्वेषिणः गदान् = diseases hostile to remedies.
Medicines are not what they produce; गदान् means diseases.
questions.explain: कुर्वते (they produce) takes गदान् (diseases) as its object, and भेषजद्वेषिणः describes them.
questions.rule: गदान् भेषजद्वेषिणः = diseases hostile to remedies.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: चयकाष्ठाम् = limit of accumulation; उपेक्षिताः = neglected; प्रायशः = mostly; सुचिरेण = after a very long time; गदान् = diseases.

questions.q: What does प्रायशः tell us about how the line speaks?
optionExplain: That would be 'सदा'; प्रायशः leaves room for exceptions.
Nothing in the word means 'never'.
The line says after a very long time, not at once.
Right: प्रायशः means mostly: the line states a tendency.
questions.explain: प्रायशः (mostly) hedges the claim; सुचिरेण अपि (even after a very long time) adds how late it may be.
questions.teaches: प्रायशः and प्रायः mean 'mostly, as a rule': they state a tendency, not 'always'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of ह्युपेक्षिताः?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: हि + उ = ह्यु.
हु + उ would join as हू, not ह्यु.
ए + उ would give हयु, not ह्यु.
पेक्षिताः is not a word; the word is उपेक्षिताः.
questions.explain: हि (for, indeed) + उपेक्षिताः (neglected).
questions.rule: इ + different vowel → य् + vowel: हि + उ = ह्यु.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: mostly, after a very long time, even, hostile to remedies, diseases.

questions.q: Which form means after entering (having entered), made like उपारुह्य (having reached)?
optionExplain: -त्वा goes on a verb without a prefix; with a prefix it becomes -य.
Right: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य: प्र + विश् = प्रविश्य.
This is 'entered' (a past participle), not 'having entered'.
This is the noun 'entering'.
questions.explain: उपारुह्य is उप + आ + रुह्, with a prefix, so it ends in -य.
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य (उपारुह्य, प्रविश्य); without a prefix it takes -त्वा.

questions.q: Which name opens the list in line 1?
optionExplain: कुष्ठ is the third name in the line.
मेह is the fourth name in the line.
Right: The line begins अतिस्थौल्य-अग्निसदन-कुष्ठ-मेह-हृतौजसः.
अग्निसदन is the second name in the line.
questions.explain: अतिस्थौल्य (excessive stoutness) comes first, then अग्निसदन.

questions.q: Put the names of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: excessive stoutness, decline of fire, kuṣṭha, meha, loss of ojas.

questions.q: Match each name to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the named conditions, with their plain meaning.
questions.rule: अतिस्थौल्य = excessive stoutness; अग्निसदन = decline of the digestive fire; श्वयथु = swelling; पाण्डुता = paleness.
questions.teaches: Where the words have a plain meaning, the card gives it; कुष्ठ, मेह and श्वास are kept as names.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हृतौजस्-?
optionExplain: औजस् is not the word; the word is ओजस्.
जस् is not a word.
ए + ओ would give हृतयोजस्-, not औ.
Right: अ + ओ joins as औ: हृत + ओजस् = हृतौज-.
questions.explain: हृत (carried off) + ओजस् (ojas): 'those whose ojas is carried off'.
questions.rule: अ + ओ → औ: हृत + ओजस्- = हृतौजस्-.

questions.q: Put these names from line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The end of line 2 runs: śvāsa, swelling, paleness.

questions.q: Which word means weakness, made like पाण्डुता (paleness) from पाण्डु (pale)?
optionExplain: Right: -ता added to an adjective names the state: दुर्बल (weak) + ता = weakness.
This is the adjective 'weak', or 'a weak man', not the state.
This is 'weak' (neuter) or 'the weak thing', not the state.
This is the nominative plural, 'weak ones', not the state.
questions.explain: पाण्डुता = पाण्डु + ता: the state of being pale. In the same way दुर्बल + ता = the state of being weak.
questions.teaches: The ending -ता on an adjective names the state or quality (पाण्डु 'pale' → पाण्डुता 'paleness').

questions.q: Which name closes line 2, and so the whole list of this unit?
optionExplain: दंडक closes line 1, not line 2.
Right: Line 2 ends ...अर्शो-भगंदरान्.
अर्श comes just before the last name.
आलस्य is the third name of line 2.
questions.explain: भगंदरान् is the last word of the unit.

questions.q: Put these names of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: तृप्ति, प्रमीलक, आलस्य, ग्रहणी, अर्श, भगंदर.
questions.rule: तृप्ति · प्रमीलक · आलस्य · ग्रहणी · अर्श · भगंदर.

questions.q: The word for 'laziness' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आलस्य is laziness; the list gives it among the names of line 2.
questions.teaches: आलस्य = laziness.

questions.q: Which is the right split of जठरोच्छ्राय?
optionExplain: ओ + उ would give जठरवुच्छ्राय, not जठरोच्छ्राय.
च्छ्राय is not a word.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ: जठर + उच्छ्राय = जठरोच्छ्राय.
ओच्छ्राय is not a word; the word is उच्छ्राय.
questions.explain: जठर (belly; a name in the list) + उच्छ्राय (swelling).

questions.q: Match each word of this list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four names have a plain meaning in the data; the others are kept as names.
questions.rule: आमोह = bewilderment; स्तंभ = stiffness; उच्छ्राय = swelling; तृप्ति = satiety.

questions.q: Which is the accusative plural of रोग (m., a disease), made like दंडकान्?
optionExplain: This is the nominative plural.
This is the genitive singular.
This is the instrumental singular.
Right: The accusative plural of a masculine a-stem ends in -आन्.
questions.explain: दंडकान् and भगंदरान् are masculine a-stems in the accusative plural.
questions.teaches: A masculine noun in -अ has its accusative plural in -आन् (दंडकान्, भगंदरान्, रोगान्): these words are objects.

questions.q: Which name opens line 1?
optionExplain: Right: Line 1 begins प्लीह-विद्रधि-विसर्प.
विसर्प is the third name.
पीनस is the last name of line 1.
छर्दि opens line 2, not line 1.
questions.explain: प्लीह comes first, then विद्रधि and विसर्प.

questions.q: Put the names of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: plīha, vidradhi, visarpa, mada, saṃnyāsa, pīnasa.
questions.rule: प्लीह · विद्रधि · विसर्प · मद · संन्यास · पीनस.

questions.q: The word for 'vomiting' that opens line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: छर्दि is vomiting, the first name of line 2 (printed छर्द्दि).
questions.teaches: छर्दि = vomiting.

questions.q: What does the ending of पीनसान् show?
options: It is the nominative plural, so the names are the doers
Accusative plural: the names are objects
It is the genitive singular, 'of pīnasa'
It is a verb ending, 'they cause'
optionExplain: The nominative plural would end in -आः.
Right: -आन् marks the accusative plural of a masculine a-stem.
The genitive singular would end in -स्य.
A noun ending in -आन् is not a verb.
questions.explain: The six names of line 1 are objects; their verb is not in this unit.

questions.q: Which two names stand in line 1?
optionExplain: Laziness is named in unit 30, not here.
Right: the third name of line 1.
Right: the last name of line 1.
Paleness is named in unit 29, not here.
questions.explain: Line 1 names plīha, vidradhi, visarpa, mada, saṃnyāsa and pīnasa.
questions.rule: Line 1: प्लीह · विद्रधि · विसर्प · मद · संन्यास · पीनस.

questions.q: Which is the accusative plural of मुनि (m., a sage), an i-stem like विद्रधि?
optionExplain: This is the accusative singular.
This is the nominative plural.
Right: A masculine i-stem has its accusative plural in -ईन्.
This is the instrumental singular.
questions.explain: विद्रधि is a masculine i-stem; its accusative plural would be विद्रधीन्, as मुनि gives मुनीन्.
questions.teaches: A masculine noun in -इ has its accusative plural in -ईन् (मुनि → मुनीन्), just as an a-stem has -आन्.

questions.q: Which part of the body does कंठामयान् name?
optionExplain: The stomach is not named in this unit.
The eyes are not named in this unit.
The heart is not named in this unit.
Right: कंठ-आमयान् = diseases of the throat (कंठ).
questions.explain: कंठामयान् = कंठ (throat) + आमयान् (diseases).

questions.q: Put these three words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins: diseases of the throat, head-pain, loss.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words are taken from the stems in the two lines.
questions.rule: मूर्द्धरुजम् = head-pain; प्रणाशम् = loss; तेजः = lustre; वर्णः = complexion; बलम् = strength.
questions.teaches: The genitive plural in तेजोवर्णबलानाम् goes with प्रणाशम्: the loss of lustre, complexion and strength.

questions.q: Why does तेजोवर्णबलानाम् have ओ in तेजो-?
options: A visarga after अ turns to ओ
The visarga becomes श् before व
ओ is the case ending of the word
optionExplain: Right: Final -अः (-अस्) before a voiced consonant (here व) gives ओ.
It drops after आ before a voiced sound, but after अ it becomes ओ.
श् appears before च or छ, not before a voiced व.
The ओ comes from the sandhi; it is not an ending.
questions.explain: तेजस् (lustre) + वर्ण (complexion) + बलानाम् (of strengths): the first joint is अः + voiced → ओ.

questions.q: What does अपि mean in बृंहणैरपि?
optionExplain: अपि does not mean 'only' or 'because of'.
Right: अपि means 'even': the phrase reads 'even with nourishing means'.
Nothing in अपि means 'never' or 'remove'.
बृंहणैः (by nourishing means) is present, so 'without' is wrong.
questions.explain: तृप्यतः बृंहणैः अपि = of one who is being satiated with nourishing means, even.

questions.q: Which means of the riches, made like बलानाम् (of strengths)?
optionExplain: This is the nominative or accusative plural.
This is the instrumental singular.
Right: The genitive plural of a neuter a-stem ends in -आनाम्: धन → धनानाम्.
This is the nominative or accusative singular.
questions.explain: तेजोवर्णबलानाम् is a genitive plural of a-stem words; धन (wealth) gives धनानाम्.
questions.teaches: The genitive plural of an a-stem noun ends in -आनाम् (बलानाम्, धनानाम्); a loss (प्रणाश) 'of' things takes this case.

questions.q: What does line 1 say about suitable foods (उचिताः आहाराः)?
options: Suitable foods make everything increase at once
Suitable foods are the only thing that increases
Even with them, they do not increase in him
optionExplain: The line has न: they do not increase.
The line does not say to avoid them.
The line does not say that.
Right: उचितैः अपि आहारैः ... वर्धन्ति न = even with suitable foods they do not increase.
questions.explain: The line has अपि (even) and न (not): the increase does not happen even with suitable foods.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words build the clause.
questions.rule: उचितैः = suitable; यस्मात् = since; अस्य = of him; वर्धन्ति = they increase.

questions.q: What does अपि do in उचितैरपि आहारैः?
options: It means 'because': foods are the cause
optionExplain: Right: अपि after उचितैः gives 'even with suitable'.
अपि does not mean 'only'.
'Because' would be यस्मात् or यतः.
The foods are present: they are suitable.
questions.explain: उचितैः आहारैः अपि = even with suitable foods.
questions.teaches: अपि after a word gives 'even' or 'also': उचितैरपि आहारैः = even with suitable foods.

questions.q: Why is there र् in आहारैर्यस्मात्?
options: आहारैः + यस्मात्: the visarga becomes ओ
Visarga after ऐ becomes र् before य
optionExplain: ओ comes only after अ, not after ऐ.
Right: After any vowel except अ and आ, a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्.
It is आहारैः, the instrumental plural, with sandhi.
A visarga drops after आ, not after ऐ.
questions.explain: आहारैः (by foods) + यस्मात् (since): the visarga becomes र् before a voiced य.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ + voiced → र्.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: with mouths smeared by doṣas, rasa, rasa-carrying, vessels.

questions.q: Which means by the physicians (वैद्य, m.), made like आहारैः?
optionExplain: This is the accusative plural, 'the physicians'.
This is the genitive plural, 'of the physicians'.
Right: The instrumental plural of a masculine a-stem ends in -ऐः.
This is the locative plural, 'among the physicians'.
questions.explain: आहारैः, उचितैः are instrumental plural of a-stem words, 'by foods', 'by suitable'.
questions.teaches: The instrumental plural of an a-stem noun ends in -ऐः (आहारैः, वैद्यैः) and means 'by ...'.

questions.q: Which doṣas does line 2 say sometimes become provoked?
options: Those that were never present at all
Those conquered by fasting and pācana
optionExplain: Purifying measures are not named in this unit; unit 35 speaks of 'those who' are purified.
Nothing in the line speaks of absent doṣas.
The line names fasting and digestive measures, not nourishing ones.
Right: जिताः लंघनपाचनैः = conquered by laṅghana and pācana.
questions.explain: दोषाः कदाचित् कुप्यंति, जिताः लंघनपाचनैः: the doṣas conquered by those two measures.
questions.rule: जिताः लंघनपाचनैः = conquered by fasting and digestive measures.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words from both lines, with their plain meanings.
questions.rule: कदाचित् = sometimes; कुप्यंति = become provoked; जिताः = conquered; यथाविधि = according to rule; स्वस्थस्य = of a healthy person.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वस्थस्यैव?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ: स्वस्थस्य + एव = स्वस्थस्यैव.
स्यैव is not a word.
व is not a word here.
ऐव is not a word; the word is एव.
questions.explain: स्वस्थस्य (of a healthy person) + एव (even, only).
questions.teaches: When a word ending in -अ meets a word beginning with ए, they join as ऐ (स्वस्थस्य + एव = स्वस्थस्यैव).

questions.q: Why is the first part of जितालंघनपाचनैः written जिता- without a visarga?
options: It is a spelling mistake that must be corrected
It is जिताः; after आ a visarga before a voiced sound drops
It is a different word, जित
The visarga becomes ओ before ल
optionExplain: It is regular sandhi, not a mistake.
Right: जिताः + लंघन: the visarga after आ drops before the voiced ल.
The card reads it as जिताः (conquered), nominative plural.
ओ comes after अ, not after आ.
questions.explain: जिताः (conquered) + लंघनपाचनैः: the visarga after आ drops before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: Visarga after आ + voiced consonant → dropped.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out the object).
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: therefore, one should employ, of a healthy person, even, according to rule.

questions.q: Which means one should go (√गम्), an optative like युंज्यात् (one should employ)?
optionExplain: This is the present, 'goes'.
This is the past participle, 'gone'.
Right: The third singular optative active ends in -एत् for many verbs: गच्छेत्.
This is the noun 'going'.
questions.explain: युंज्यात् (should employ) is a 3rd singular optative form; गच्छेत् is the same kind.
questions.teaches: The 3rd singular optative active means 'should ...' and ends in -एत् (भवेत्, गच्छेत्) or -यात् (युंज्यात्).

questions.q: What does line 1 say about those purified by purifying measures?
options: They must be purified again each time
There is no re-arising for them
optionExplain: The line does not say this.
That is said of the conquered doṣas in unit 34, not here.
Nothing about avoiding foods is in this unit.
Right: न तेषां पुनरुद्भवः = for them there is no re-arising.
questions.explain: संशोधनैः शुद्धाः = purified by purifying measures; न ... पुनरुद्भवः = no re-arising.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words from the two lines.
questions.rule: संशोधनैः = by purifying measures; शुद्धाः = purified; पुनरुद्भवः = re-arising; यथाक्रमम् = in due order; यथायोगम् = as suitable.

questions.q: प्रयोजयेत् ('one should apply') is formed from प्र + which root?
optionExplain: Right: प्रयोजयेत् is the causative of प्र + युज्, 'to join, to apply'.
जि means 'to conquer'; that is the root of जिताः in unit 34.
शुध् means 'to be pure'; that is the root of शुद्धाः.
कुप् means 'to be angry, to be provoked'; that is the root of कुप्यंति.
questions.explain: प्रयोजयेत् = प्र + युज् in the causative, 3rd singular optative.
questions.teaches: प्रयोजयेत् is a causative optative of प्र + युज्, related to युञ्जीत and युंज्यात् of earlier units; the causative stem has -अय- (प्रयोजय-).

questions.q: Which is the right split of पुनरुद्भवः?
optionExplain: रुद्भवः is not a word.
Right: The final र् of पुनर् stays and joins the vowel उ: पुनर् + उद्भवः.
रुद्भवः is not a word; the second word is उद्भवः.
आ + उ would give पुनोद्भवः, not पुनरुद्भवः.
questions.explain: पुनर् (again) + उद्भवः (arising): a compound 'again-arising'.
questions.rule: Final र् + vowel: the र् joins the vowel.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse (leaving out अतऊर्ध्वम्).
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: in due order, as suitable, ... one should apply.

questions.q: Which means awakened (past participle of √बुध्), made like शुद्ध from √शुध्?
optionExplain: This is not the form the root takes.
This is the noun 'awakening'.
Right: A root ending in -ध् with the past ending -त gives -द्ध: शुध् → शुद्ध, बुध् → बुद्ध.
This is the agent noun 'one who awakens or knows'.
questions.explain: शुद्धाः (purified) is the past participle of √शुध्; √बुध् forms its past participle the same way.
questions.teaches: A past participle from a root in -ध् takes the form -द्ध (शुध् → शुद्ध 'purified', बुध् → बुद्ध 'awakened').

questions.q: In line 1, who applies the rasāyana preparations and vṛṣya formulations?
options: The one who has been purified
optionExplain: That is unit 35's शुद्धाः, not the applier.
That person is in line 2, where a nourishing regimen is meant for him.
स्वस्थ is in unit 34, not here.
Right: कालवित् is the subject: the knower of time.
questions.explain: कालवित् (knower of time) is nominative and is the one who applies.
questions.rule: कालवित् = the knower of the right time.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words that carry the two lines.
questions.rule: कालवित् = knower of time; भेषजक्षपिते = in one depleted by medicines; पथ्यम् = wholesome; आहारैः = by foods; रसायनानि = rasāyana preparations.

questions.q: The word for step by step, gradually, ending line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: क्रमात् is the ablative of क्रम (order, sequence) used as 'step by step'.
questions.teaches: क्रमात् = step by step, gradually.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वृष्ययोगांश्च?
optionExplain: Right: न् before च becomes ंश्: वृष्ययोगान् + च = वृष्ययोगांश्च.
श्च is not a word; the word is च.
A visarga before च would give श्च without an anusvara.
श is not a word here.
questions.explain: वृष्ययोगान् (vṛṣya formulations, accusative plural) + च (and).

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: in one depleted by medicines, wholesome, by foods, nourishing, step by step.

questions.q: Which means knower of the Veda, made like कालवित् (knower of time)?
optionExplain: -कृत् means 'maker of'.
Right: -वित् at the end of a compound means 'knower of' what comes before.
-दः means 'giver of'.
-भृत् means 'bearer of'.
questions.explain: कालवित् = काल (time) + वित् (knower). In the same way वेद + वित् = knower of the Veda.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -वित् means 'knower of' the first part (कालवित्, वेदवित्).

questions.q: What does line 1 of this unit list?
options: Kinds of enema, massage and bathing of the body
Signs by which a disease is known in a patient
Foods such as rice, wheat, mung, meat and ghee
Names of the seasons and the months of the year
optionExplain: Massage and enemas come in the next unit.
No sign of any disease is named here.
Right: Line 1 names शालि, षष्टिक, गोधूम, मुद्ग, मांस and घृत.
No season is named in this unit.
questions.explain: Line 1 is a list of foods, ending with आदि, 'and the like'.
questions.rule: शालि · षष्टिक · गोधूम · मुद्ग · मांस · घृत · आदि.

questions.q: Put the foods of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs शालि, षष्टिक, गोधूम, मुद्ग, मांस, घृत and then आदि.
questions.rule: शालि · षष्टिक · गोधूम · मुद्ग · मांस · घृत.

questions.q: Match each food name of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four names stand inside the long joined word of line 1.
questions.rule: गोधूम = wheat; मुद्ग = mung; मांस = meat; घृत = ghee.
questions.teaches: A list of foods can be joined into one long word that ends in आदिभिः, 'with these and the like'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of संयोगाद्रुचि-?
optionExplain: A visarga here would give संयोगा रुचि, not द्.
द्रुचि is not a word on the card.
A final म् would stay म् or become a dot, not द्.
Right: A final त् before a voiced sound such as र becomes द्.
questions.explain: संयोगात् (from the combination, ablative) + रुचि (relish) join as संयोगाद्रुचि.
questions.rule: त् + voiced sound → द्: संयोगात् + रुचि = संयोगाद्रुचि.

questions.q: What does the ending -भिः of ...घृतादिभिः show?
optionExplain: Right: The ending -भिः marks the instrumental plural.
The genitive plural ends in -आम् (-ईनाम्), not -भिः.
The locative plural ends in -षु, not -भिः.
The nominative plural has no -भिः; -भिः is the instrumental sign.
questions.explain: The foods are the means: the ending -भिः says 'with ... and the like'.

questions.q: Following रुचिपक्तिदैः, what does the invented word सुखदैः mean?
optionExplain: -द does not mean free from.
Right: A compound ending in -द gives 'giving' the first part, here happiness.
The idea is 'giving' happiness, not being happy.
The ending -ऐः is instrumental, not 'of'.
questions.explain: In रुचिपक्तिदैः the end -द means 'giving' relish and digestion; सुखदैः works the same way.
questions.rule: X-द (from दा, to give) = giving X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -द means 'giving' the first part: रुचिपक्तिद = giving relish and digestion; सुखद = giving happiness.

questions.q: What does the person obtain, as the second line of this unit puts it?
options: Wealth, children and a large household
Victory in war and lasting fame abroad
Comfort and keenness of all the fires
Sweet speech and bodily beauty at all times
optionExplain: None of these is named in this unit.
Neither is named in this unit.
Right: The line says शर्म and सर्वपावकपाटवम्.
Neither is named in this unit.
questions.explain: लभते शर्म सर्वपावकपाटवम्: he obtains comfort and keenness of all the fires.
questions.rule: लभते = obtains; शर्म = comfort; सर्वपावकपाटवम् = keenness of all fires.

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: with massage, rubbing, bathing, then nirūha, sneha and basti.
questions.rule: साभ्यंग · उद्वर्तन · स्नान · निरूह · स्नेह · बस्ति.

questions.q: Which is the right split of साभ्यंगोद्वर्तन-?
optionExplain: भ्यंग is not a word.
A visarga would not disappear like this before उ.
None of these parts is a word.
Right: स + अ gives आ; and अभ्यंग + उ gives ओ.
questions.explain: स (with) + अभ्यंग (oil massage) + उद्वर्तन (rubbing) join as साभ्यंगोद्वर्तन.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: Two short a-sounds join into आ (स + अभ्यंग = साभ्यंग), and अ + उ joins into ओ (अभ्यंग + उद्वर्तन = अभ्यंगोद्वर्तन).

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the result of the verse.
questions.rule: शर्म = comfort; पावक = fire; पाटव = keenness; लभते = obtains.

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 1?
optionExplain: Right: it opens the list, inside साभ्यंग.
Right: it is the third item.
Right: it closes the list.
Not in line 1.
Not in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 names massage, rubbing, bathing and the two kinds of basti; emesis and nasal drops are not in it.
questions.rule: Line 1: अभ्यंग, उद्वर्तन, स्नान, निरूह, स्नेह, बस्ति.

questions.q: By the pattern of साभ्यंग, what does the invented word सपुत्रः mean?
optionExplain: Right: स- in a compound can mean 'together with' the rest.
'Without' would be अ- or निः-, not स-.
Nothing in स- means 'born of'.
That would be पुत्रस्य.
questions.explain: साभ्यंग = स + अभ्यंग, 'together with massage'; सपुत्र = 'together with a son'.
questions.teaches: In a compound the prefix स- (sa-) can mean 'together with' the rest: साभ्यंग = with oil massage; सपुत्र = with a son.

questions.q: Line 2 lists bhūtas, poison, wind, fire, wounds and fractures. What do they share?
options: Each is a remedy that something removes
Each is a source from which something arises
Each is a food that something is eaten with
Each is a season in which something occurs
optionExplain: Nothing in the line calls them remedies.
Right: संभवाः means 'arising from': the list gives the sources.
None of the six is a food here.
None of the six is a season.
questions.explain: भूतविषवाय्वग्निक्षतभंगादिसंभवाः = arising from bhūtas, poison, wind, fire, wounds, fractures and the like.
questions.rule: -संभव = arising from; the list gives the sources.

questions.q: Put the sources of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs भूत, विष, वायु, अग्नि, क्षत, भंग and then आदि.
questions.rule: भूत · विष · वायु · अग्नि · क्षत · भंग.

questions.q: Match each source of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words stand in the long joined word of line 2.
questions.rule: भूत = beings or spirits; विष = poison; क्षत = wound; भंग = fracture.
questions.teaches: In this list भूत means beings or spirits, and the other nouns are plain words for poison, wound and fracture.

questions.q: Which is the right split of धीवर्णेंद्रिय-?
optionExplain: न्द्रिय is not a word.
एन्द्रिय is not a word; the ए comes from joining.
Right: अ + इ joins as ए: वर्ण + इन्द्रिय = वर्णेन्द्रिय.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: धी (intellect), वर्ण (complexion) and इन्द्रिय (sense) are joined; अ + इ became ए.
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए: वर्ण + इन्द्रिय = वर्णेन्द्रिय.

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 2 as sources?
optionExplain: Right: it is the second item.
Right: it is the fourth item.
Right: it is the sixth item.
Not in line 2.
Not in line 2.
questions.explain: Poison, fire and fractures are in the list; cold and hunger are not.
questions.rule: Line 2: भूत, विष, वायु, अग्नि, क्षत, भंग, आदि.

questions.q: By the pattern of ...संभवाः, what does the invented word जलसंभवाः mean?
optionExplain: Dwelling would be a different ending, such as -स्थ.
'Leading to' is not what -संभव says.
Nothing in -संभव means protecting.
Right: -संभव at the end means 'arising from' the first part.
questions.explain: In भूतविष...संभवाः the end -संभव means 'arising from'; जलसंभवाः works the same.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -संभव means 'arising from' the first part: भंगादिसंभव = arising from fractures and the like; जलसंभव = arising from water.

questions.q: What does line 1 call the diseases coming from desire, anger, fear and the like?
options: Diseases of the body alone, by any cause
optionExplain: Right: The line says तेस्युरागंतवो गदाः: they would be the adventitious diseases.
The verse does not use निज in this unit.
Nothing in the line is about a season.
The line gives no such name.
questions.explain: आगन्तु means adventitious; गद means disease; the line calls the diseases from desire, anger and fear by that name.

questions.q: Put the three named causes of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs काम, क्रोध, भय and then आद्याः, 'and the like'.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words come from line 1 and two from line 2.
questions.rule: आगन्तु = adventitious; गद = disease; त्याग = abandonment; उपशम = calming.
questions.teaches: The nouns त्यागः and इन्द्रियोपशमः of line 2 are single words; त्याग means abandonment and उपशम means calming.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तेस्युरागंतवो?
optionExplain: रागंतवः is not a word.
Right: A visarga after उ before a vowel becomes र्: स्युः + आ = स्युरा.
None of these parts is a word.
A र् would not be written twice here.
questions.explain: ते (they) + स्युः (would be) + आगंतवः (adventitious); the printed तेस्युरागंतवो joins स्युः + आगंतवः; the final visarga of आगंतवः shows as ओ before the voiced ग of गदाः.
questions.rule: उः + vowel → उर् + vowel: स्युः + आगंतवः = स्युरागंतवः.

questions.q: The word for 'diseases' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: गदाः is the plural of गद, disease.
questions.teaches: गदाः (diseases) ends the clause of line 1.

questions.q: By the pattern of कामक्रोधभयाद्याः, what does the invented word रूपरसगंधाद्याः mean?
options: The end of form, taste and smell
Form, taste, smell and the like
The best among form, taste and smell
optionExplain: आद्य means first, not end.
'Without' would use a negating अ-.
Right: -आद्याः means 'having these as the first', that is 'and the like'.
आद्य here gives 'first of a group', not 'best'.
questions.explain: In कामक्रोधभयाद्याः the end -आद्याः turns the list into 'desire, anger, fear and the like'.
questions.rule: X-Y-आद्याः = X, Y and the like.
questions.teaches: A list ending in -आद्याः means 'these and the like': कामक्रोधभयाद्याः = desire, anger, fear and the like.

questions.q: Which rite does line 2 name first, and where is it said to be prescribed?
options: A fire sacrifice prescribed in the hymns of the Ṛgveda
A penance prescribed in the old books of sacred law
A purifying bath prescribed in the Yajurveda texts
A pacificatory rite prescribed in the Atharva (Veda)
optionExplain: The line names the Atharva, not the Ṛgveda.
The line names the Atharva.
The line names the Atharva, and a pacificatory rite.
Right: अथर्वविहिता शान्तिः is the first item of line 2.
questions.explain: अथर्वविहिता शान्तिः = the pacificatory rite prescribed in the Atharva (Veda).
questions.rule: अथर्वविहिता शान्तिः = pacificatory rite prescribed in the Atharva.

questions.q: Put the three things whose knowledge opens line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The word runs देश, काल, आत्म and then विज्ञानम्, 'knowledge'.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words build the two items of line 2.
questions.rule: प्रतिकूल = unfavourable; अर्चन = worship; शान्ति = pacificatory rite; विहित = prescribed.
questions.teaches: विहित means 'prescribed': अथर्वविहिता is 'prescribed in the Atharva'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रतिकूलग्रहार्चनं?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ joins as आ: ग्रह + अर्चन = ग्रहार्चन.
आर्चनं is not a word.
ग्रहार् and चनं are not words.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: प्रतिकूल (unfavourable) + ग्रह (graha) + अर्चनं (worship) make one word.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: ग्रह + अर्चन = ग्रहार्चन.

questions.q: Which of these are named in this unit?
optionExplain: Right: देश opens line 1.
Right: काल is next.
Right: it closes line 2.
Massage is in unit 38.
Bathing is in unit 38.
questions.explain: Place, time and the worship of unfavourable grahas are in the unit; massage and bathing belong to unit 38.
questions.rule: Unit 41: देश, काल, आत्मा; अथर्वविहिता शान्तिः; प्रतिकूलग्रहार्चनम्.

questions.q: By the pattern of अथर्वविहिता, what does the invented phrase वेदविहितं कर्म mean?
options: An action rejected by the Veda
An action prescribed in the Veda
An action done before the Veda
An action that is the Veda itself
optionExplain: विहित does not mean rejected.
Right: -विहित means 'prescribed in' the first part.
Nothing in विहित gives 'before'.
विहित says 'prescribed', not 'identical with'.
questions.explain: In अथर्वविहिता the first part says where, the second says 'prescribed'; वेदविहित is built the same.
questions.teaches: A compound X-विहित means 'prescribed in X': अथर्वविहिता = prescribed in the Atharva; वेदविहित = prescribed in the Veda.

questions.q: What does the unit say has been shown in brief?
options: A cure for each single disease
A rule for the seasons of the year
optionExplain: No cure for single diseases is named.
No list of medicines is named here.
Right: विधिरेषः प्रदर्शितः with अनुत्पत्त्यै and समासेन.
No season is named here.
questions.explain: The second line says: for non-arising, this procedure has been shown in brief.

questions.q: Put the parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs अनुत्पत्त्यै, समासेन, विधिः एषः, प्रदर्शितः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the two statements of the unit.
questions.rule: पृथक्पृथक् = separately; समासेन = in brief; अनुत्पत्त्यै = for non-arising; प्रदर्शितः = shown.
questions.teaches: Words such as पृथक्पृथक् (doubled for 'each separately') and समासेन ('in brief') tell how a matter has been treated.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विधिरेषः?
optionExplain: रेषः is not a word.
षः is not a word.
अषः is not a word on the card.
Right: A visarga after इ before a vowel becomes र्.
questions.explain: विधिः (procedure) + एषः (this) join as विधिरेषः.
questions.rule: इः + vowel → इर् + vowel: विधिः + एषः = विधिरेषः.

questions.q: How does line 1 say the means of not being touched by bhūtas has been indicated?
optionExplain: Right: पृथक्पृथक् means separately.
The line says the opposite: separately.
The line says it has been indicated already.
The line says a means has been indicated.
questions.explain: निर्दिष्टश्च पृथक्पृथक्: and indicated, each separately.

questions.q: By the pattern of अनुत्पत्त्यै, what does the invented रक्षायै in विधिः रक्षायै mean?
optionExplain: 'By' would be रक्षया.
Right: A feminine word in -आ has the dative singular -आयै, and it says 'for'.
'In' would be रक्षायाम्.
'From' would be रक्षायाः.
questions.explain: अनुत्पत्त्यै is the dative of अनुत्पत्ति: 'for non-arising'; रक्षायै is the dative of रक्षा.
questions.teaches: The dative singular of a feminine word in -आ ends in -आयै (रक्षायै); a feminine -इ word can end in -त्यै (अनुत्पत्त्यै) or -तये: it says 'for ...', purpose.

questions.q: For what does this line say, regarding disorders that have already arisen?
optionExplain: The word is शान्तये, pacification.
The line says pacification.
Right: उत्पन्नानां च शान्तये: and for the pacification of those arisen.
The line says pacification.
questions.explain: उत्पन्नानां are those that have arisen; शान्तये is 'for pacification'.
questions.rule: उत्पन्नानां च शान्तये = for the pacification of those arisen.

questions.q: Put the parts of the line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs निजागंतुविकाराणाम्, उत्पन्नानाम्, च, शान्तये.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the whole line.
questions.rule: निज = innate; आगन्तु = adventitious; विकार = disorder; शान्ति = pacification.
questions.teaches: निज (innate) and आगन्तु (adventitious) are the two kinds of disorder the line names; शान्ति is the aim for those that have arisen.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निजागंतुविकाराणां?
optionExplain: The card splits निज + आगंतु (adventitious); निजा + गंतु leaves a stray आ and breaks the compound.
Neither part is a word.
A visarga would not vanish like this.
Right: अ + आ joins as आ: निज + आगंतु = निजागंतु.
questions.explain: निज (innate) + आगंतु (adventitious) + विकाराणां (of disorders) join into one word.
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ: निज + आगंतु = निजागंतु.

questions.q: The word for 'for pacification' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शान्तये is the dative singular of शान्ति: 'for pacification'.
questions.teaches: शान्तये ends the line and gives the purpose.

questions.q: By the pattern of शान्तये, what does the invented word शुद्धये mean?
optionExplain: Right: The dative singular of a word in -इ ends in -अये and says 'for'.
'By' would be शुद्ध्या.
'In' would be शुद्धौ.
The subject would be शुद्धिः.
questions.explain: शान्तये is the dative of शान्ति; शुद्धये is the dative of शुद्धि.
questions.teaches: A feminine word in -इ can take the dative singular in -अये: शान्ति → शान्तये, 'for pacification'; शुद्धि → शुद्धये, 'for purification'.

questions.q: Which accumulation does the verse say is purified in spring?
options: The doṣa accumulation of the rainy season
The doṣa accumulation born of winter
The accumulation of poison in a wound
optionExplain: That one is purified at the passing of the clouds.
Right: शीतोद्भवं दोषचयं वसंते विशोधयन्.
Nothing like this is in the verse.
Nothing like this is in the verse.
questions.explain: In spring, the accumulation of doṣa born of winter is purified.
questions.rule: वसंते = in spring; शीतोद्भवं दोषचयं = the winter-born doṣa accumulation.

questions.q: Put the three accumulations purified in the verse in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: born of winter, born of summer, then that of the rainy season.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: at the passing of the clouds
questions.explain: These four words say when and how the purifying is done.
questions.rule: वसंते = in spring; घनात्यये = at the passing of the clouds; आशु = quickly; सम्यक् = properly.
questions.teaches: घनात्यये is घन (cloud) + अत्यये (at the passing): a locative that says 'when'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रोगानृतुजान्न?
optionExplain: A visarga before ऋ would give रोगा ऋ..., not रोगान्.
आनृतुजान् is not a word.
Right: रोगान् + ऋतुजान्: final न् is kept before a vowel and written joined (रोगानृतुजान्); ऋतुजान् + न is written ऋतुजान्न with no change.
तुजान् is not a word.
questions.explain: रोगान् (diseases) + ऋतुजान् (born of seasons) + न (not) join as रोगानृतुजान्न.
questions.rule: Final न् + vowel stay joined: रोगान् + ऋतुजान् = रोगानृतुजान्.

questions.q: What does the verse say the one who purifies in this way does not incur?
optionExplain: Wounds are not named in this verse.
Fear is not named in this verse.
Poison is not named in this verse.
Right: रोगानृतुजान्न जातु: never the diseases born of seasons.
questions.explain: प्राप्नोति रोगानृतुजान्न जातु = he never incurs the diseases born of seasons.
questions.rule: ऋतुजान् रोगान् न जातु = never the season-born diseases.

questions.q: By the pattern of ग्रीष्मजम्, what does the invented phrase मेघजं जलम् mean?
optionExplain: Right: -ज at the end means 'born of' the first part.
That would be जलजो मेघः, the order reversed.
-ज says 'born of', not 'filling'.
Nothing in -ज says 'going to'.
questions.explain: ग्रीष्मज = born of summer, शीतोद्भव = born of winter, ऋतुज = born of seasons; मेघज = born of the cloud.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -ज (or -उद्भव) means 'born of' the first part: ग्रीष्मज = born of summer; ऋतुज = born of seasons; मेघज = born of the cloud.

questions.q: What does the verse say the person with these habits becomes?
optionExplain: Debt is not mentioned.
Right: भवत्यरोगः closes the verse.
Fame is not mentioned.
Learning is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The last words are भवत्यरोगः: he becomes free from disease.
questions.rule: भवति अरोगः = becomes free from disease.

questions.q: Put these habits in the order of the verse (leaving out दातासमः).
questions.explain: The verse runs: follower of wholesome food and conduct, acts after consideration, unattached, devoted to truth, forbearing, attends upon the trustworthy.
questions.rule: हिताहारविहारसेवी · समीक्ष्यकारी · विषयेष्वसक्तः · सत्यपरः · क्षमावान् · आप्तोपसेवी.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विषयेष्वसक्तः?
optionExplain: ओ + अ would give विषयेषोऽसक्तः.
वसक्तः is not a word.
Right: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व्: विषयेषु + अ = विषयेष्वसक्तः.
That would give विषयेषु सक्तः, 'attached', without the व.
questions.explain: विषयेषु (in sense-objects) + असक्तः (unattached); उ + अ became व् + अ.
questions.rule: उ + different vowel → व् + vowel: विषयेषु + असक्तः.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व् and the vowel joins it: विषयेषु + असक्तः = विषयेष्वसक्तः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are four of the habits of the verse.
questions.rule: समीक्ष्यकारी = acting after consideration; असक्तः = unattached; सत्यपरः = devoted to truth; क्षमावान् = forbearing.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say of the person?
optionExplain: Right: समीक्ष्यकारी.
Right: विषयेष्वसक्तः.
Right: आप्तोपसेवी.
The verse speaks of wholesome food, not of giving it up.
The verse says he attends upon trustworthy persons.
questions.explain: The first three are in the verse; the last two say the opposite of what it states.

questions.q: By the pattern of आप्तोपसेवी, what does the invented गुरुसेवी mean?
options: One who is served by a teacher
The teacher of one who serves
One who attends upon a teacher
optionExplain: The teacher is the one attended, not the server.
-सेवी does not mean leaving.
-सेवी names the one who serves.
Right: -सेवी names one who follows or attends the first part.
questions.explain: हिताहारविहारसेवी = one who follows wholesome food and conduct; आप्तोपसेवी = one who attends upon the trustworthy.
questions.rule: X-सेवी = one who follows or attends X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -सेवी names one who follows or attends the first part: हिताहारविहारसेवी; आप्तोपसेवी; गुरुसेवी.

questions.q: Which word of line 1 means 'unobtainable'?
optionExplain: Right: अलभ्य = unobtainable (a-labhya).
This means 'in those having means'.
This means 'showing regard'.
This means 'in objects'.
questions.explain: अर्थेषु अलभ्येषु: in unobtainable objects.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: one who has conquered the senses
questions.explain: Three words come from line 1 and one (जितेन्द्रिय) from line 2; these are the plain compounds.
questions.rule: अलभ्य = unobtainable; अकृतप्रयत्न = making no effort; कृतादर = showing regard; जितेन्द्रिय = one who has conquered the senses.

questions.q: Put the three phrases of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: in unobtainable objects making no effort, showing regard, always in those having means.
questions.teaches: A line can be read in three phrases: the first with no effort, the second 'showing regard', the third 'always in those having means'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अर्थेष्वलभ्येष्वकृतप्रयत्नं?
optionExplain: वलभ्येष is not a word.
Right: A final उ before a different vowel becomes व्.
ओ + अ would give ओऽ.
That would drop the negating अ- and change the meaning.
questions.explain: अर्थेषु + अलभ्येषु + अकृतप्रयत्नं: उ + अ became व्, so the words are joined.

questions.q: Which words of line 1 begin with the negating अ-?
optionExplain: Right: a-labhya, unobtainable.
Right: a-kṛta-prayatna, effort not made.
कृत + आदर: the आ comes from joining, not from a negation.
It begins with उ, not a negation.
questions.explain: Only अलभ्येषु and अकृतप्रयत्नं carry the negating अ-.

questions.q: By the pattern of उपायवत्सु, what does the invented धनवत्सु mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would use a negating अ-.
That would be a dative, धनाय.
Right: -वत् means 'having' the first part.
That would be धनात्.
questions.explain: उपायवत्सु = in those having means (upāya); धनवत्सु = among those having wealth.
questions.teaches: A word in -वत् means 'having' the first part: उपायवत् = having means; धनवत् = having wealth.

questions.q: For whom does the verse say these are for happiness?
optionExplain: No king is mentioned.
No physician is mentioned.
No student is mentioned.
Right: धीरस्य सदासुखाय names the steadfast person.
questions.explain: भवंति धीरस्य सदासुखाय = they are always for the happiness of the steadfast person.
questions.rule: धीरस्य सदा सुखाय = for the steadfast, always for happiness.

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: favourable time, agreeable sense-objects, righteous acts and happy action, controllable mind, clear intellect.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words describe time, objects, mind and intellect.
questions.rule: अनुकूल = favourable; मनोज्ञ = agreeable; विधेय = controllable; विशद = clear.
questions.teaches: Each item of the verse gets one describing word: time is अनुकूल, objects मनोज्ञ, mind विधेय, intellect विशद.

questions.q: The printed word विषया ends in -आ. What is the full form?
options: विषयाः, with the visarga dropped before a voiced sound
विषयः, a single object, which would need a singular verb
विषयाम्, an object as the one acted on
optionExplain: Right: A trailing -आ can be -आः with the visarga dropped before a voiced consonant.
One object would be विषयः, not विषया.
The verb भवंति is plural and needs a plural subject.
This would end in -ए, not -आ.
questions.explain: विषयाः मनोज्ञाः: sense-objects, agreeable; the next word starts with the voiced म.
questions.rule: -आ for -आः before a voiced sound: not a typo.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse list as being for the steadfast person's happiness?
optionExplain: Right: सत्त्वं विधेयम्.
Right: विशदा च बुद्धिः.
Right: कालोऽनुकूलः.
Not in the verse.
Not in the verse.
questions.explain: A controllable mind, a clear intellect and a favourable time are listed; unrestrained senses and great wealth are not.
questions.rule: कालः · विषयाः · क्रियाः · कर्म · सत्त्वं · बुद्धिः.

questions.q: By the pattern of सुखानुबंधि, what does the invented लाभानुबंधि कर्म mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would use a negating अ-.
Right: -अनुबंधि at the end means 'followed by' the first part.
-अनुबंधि means 'followed by' the first part (the gain comes after the action); the option reverses that order.
The word is built on 'followed by', not 'born of'.
questions.explain: सुखानुबंधि कर्म = action followed by happiness; लाभानुबंधि कर्म = action followed by gain.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -अनुबंधि means 'followed by' the first part: सुखानुबंधि = followed by happiness; लाभानुबंधि = followed by gain.

questions.q: What is the name of the fifth chapter, as this closing line gives it?
optionExplain: That is the name of chapter 3.
That is the name of chapter 4.
Right: रोगानुत्पादनीयो नाम पंचमोऽध्यायः.
That is the name of chapter 2.
questions.explain: The line names the chapter रोगानुत्पादनीय.

questions.q: Put the words of the closing line in the order of the line.
questions.explain: The line runs इति, रोगानुत्पादनीयः, नाम, पंचमः, अध्यायः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the frame of the closing line.
questions.rule: इति = thus; नाम = by name; पंचम = fifth.
questions.teaches: In this closing line the frame is इति + title + नाम + number + अध्यायः.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रोगानुत्पादनीयो नाम?
optionExplain: म् before न would stay as म् or a dot, not ओ.
आः before a voiced sound drops to आ, not ओ.
ए stays ए, it does not become ओ.
Right: अः before a voiced sound such as न becomes ओ.
questions.explain: The title word ends in -अः; before नाम it became -ओ.

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' in the closing line is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायः means chapter.
questions.teaches: अध्यायः ends the line.

questions.q: Following पंचमोऽध्यायः, how is षष्ठः (sixth) before the word अध्यायः written in sandhi, as two words?
optionExplain: Right: षष्ठः + अध्यायः: अः + अ becomes ओऽ.
ए would be the locative, 'in the sixth chapter'.
That is a single compound word, not the two-word sandhi of the pattern.
The visarga before अ becomes ओऽ here, not a gap.
questions.explain: पंचमः + अध्यायः gives पंचमोऽध्यायः; षष्ठः + अध्यायः gives षष्ठोऽध्यायः.
questions.teaches: The masculine ordinal ends in -अः; before अध्यायः it joins as ओऽ: पंचमोऽध्यायः, षष्ठोऽध्यायः.

questions.q: To whom is homage paid in the first line of the Śārīrasthāna?
optionExplain: Dhanvantari is greeted in the next line, unit 2.
Right: श्रीगणेशाय = to the auspicious Gaṇeśa.
Ātreya is named in unit 4 as a speaker, not greeted.
No teacher is named in this line.
questions.explain: The line is श्रीगणेशाय नमः: homage to the auspicious Gaṇeśa.
questions.rule: श्रीगणेशाय नमः = homage to the auspicious Gaṇeśa.
questions.section: मंगलाचरण तथा विवाह व गर्भाधान की आयु

questions.q: What form does the card give व्याख्यास्यामः?

questions.q: By the rule of अथातः, how is अत्र + अस्ति (here is) written when joined?

questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By the rule of वातौपशमन, how is वन + औषधि written when joined?
optionExplain: अ + औ does not give ओ.
Right: अ + औ → औ, as in वात + औपशमन.
No व् is inserted after अ.
अ + औ does not split into आ + उ.
questions.explain: वात + औपशमन → वातौपशमन; so वन + औषधि → वनौषधि.
questions.teaches: अ or आ before औ merges into औ (वृद्धि vowel stays).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 16, how does the belly look when the held-back ārtava increases it?
options: As if struck by a blow
As if occupied by an embryo
optionExplain: No blow is named in the unit.
Pus is not named in this unit.
Right: गर्भाधिष्ठितम् इव: as if an embryo were in it.
No poison is named in this unit.
questions.explain: It increases the belly, free of complications, as if occupied by an embryo.
questions.rule: इव = as if; गर्भाधिष्ठित = occupied by an embryo.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 16 in their printed order.
questions.explain: Subject, then the cause of holding back, then held back, then the belly, then 'as if occupied by an embryo'.
questions.rule: आर्तव → आहारविहार → स्तम्भित → उदर → गर्भाधिष्ठित इव.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 16 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Three words describe the cause (gentle, bulk-promoting diets and regimens); two describe the result.
questions.teaches: बृंहण means bulk-promoting, nourishing: such diets and regimens hold the ārtava back.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In unit 16, what holds the ārtava back?
optionExplain: In unit 14 these make it flow, not stop.
Vāta-pacifying (ones) belong to unit 15.
Those make the blood flow in unit 18.
Right: सौम्यैः बृंहणात्मभिः आहारविहारैः स्तम्भितम्.
questions.explain: The ārtava is held back by gentle diets and regimens of a bulk-promoting nature.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: What does the word इव tell us about the belly in unit 16?
options: It only looks occupied by an embryo
It truly holds a living embryo
It holds two embryos at once
It shrinks after a few days
optionExplain: Right: इव = as if: the likeness is in looks only.
इव marks a likeness, not a fact.
Nothing of the kind is said.
The verb says it grows (वर्धयति).
questions.explain: गर्भाधिष्ठितम् इव: as if occupied by an embryo, so not truly.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: An invented line reads बालः सिंह इव गर्जति. What does it say?
options: The lion roars like a boy
The boy roars like a lion
The boy is a lion who roars
The boy roars at a lion
optionExplain: इव follows सिंह, so the lion is the likeness.
Right: इव after सिंह = like a lion.
इव makes it a likeness, not an identity.
No 'at' (object) is expressed.
questions.explain: As गर्भाधिष्ठितम् इव = as if occupied by an embryo, सिंह इव = like a lion.
questions.rule: X इव = like X, as if X.
questions.teaches: इव follows the word it compares with: X इव = like X.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In unit 17, who call the woman pregnant?
optionExplain: No physician is named in this line.
No midwife is named in this line.
Right: मूढाः आहुः: the deluded say so.
No parent is named in this line.
questions.explain: The deluded call her pregnant though she is not.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put the printed words of unit 17 in their order.
questions.explain: Because of which, her (not pregnant), pregnant they call, the deluded.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 17 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The four words make the line: because of which the deluded call her pregnant.
questions.teaches: आहुः is a plural verb: they say, they call; its subject here is मूढाः.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which split of आहुर्मूढाः is right?
optionExplain: आहुर is not the verb form; it is आहुः.
र्मूढाः is not a word.
म् + म would stay म्म, not र्म.
Right: Visarga after उ becomes र् before the voiced म.
questions.explain: आहुः (they call) + मूढाः (the deluded).
questions.rule: Visarga after उ → र् before a voiced sound.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In unit 17, what does येन (because of which) point back to?
options: The belly grown as if pregnant
optionExplain: Right: Unit 16's swollen belly is what misleads them.
That is advice in unit 14, not a cause of the mistake.
Those calm the vātodara in unit 15.
The blood flows later, in unit 18.
questions.explain: The card takes येन as the appearance of unit 16: the belly grows as if occupied by an embryo.
questions.rule: येन = by which / because of which (unit 16).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By the rule of आहुर्मूढाः, how is गुरुः + वदति written when joined?
optionExplain: That is not a possible spelling.
Right: Visarga after उ → र् before the voiced व.
Visarga becomes स् only before त/थ.
The visarga does not drop after उ.
questions.explain: आहुः + मूढाः → आहुर्मूढाः; so गुरुः + वदति → गुरुर्वदति.
questions.teaches: A visarga after उ (or इ, ए ...) becomes र् before a voiced consonant.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 18, what do the ignorant say when they do not see the embryo's body?
options: It was never there at all
It was carried off by beings
optionExplain: The ignorant say nothing of Vāta here.
The ignorant do not say this; they blame beings (भूत).
Right: भूतहृतम् इति अज्ञाः ब्रुवते.
No such claim is made.
questions.explain: The ignorant say: carried off by beings (bhūta).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 18 in their printed order.
questions.explain: Cause of the flow, the flow, not seeing the body, the claim, the speakers.
questions.rule: विपरीतैः/यदृच्छया → प्रवृत्ते रक्ते → अपश्यन्तः → भूतहृतम् इति → अज्ञाः ब्रुवते.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 18 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: These five words make up the claim and who makes it.
questions.teaches: अपश्यन्तः = not seeing (present participle, plural), describing the ignorant.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which split of भूतहृतमित्यज्ञाः is right?
optionExplain: इत्य and ज्ञाः are not the card's words.
भूतहृतमि is not a word.
यज्ञाः would mean sacrifices; the word is अज्ञाः.
Right: म् joins the vowel; इ + अ → य: इत्यज्ञाः.
questions.explain: भूतहृतम् (carried off by beings) + इति (thus) + अज्ञाः (the ignorant).
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 18, how may the blood come to flow?
optionExplain: Right: विपरीतैः.
Right: यदृच्छया.
Those calm the vātodara in unit 15.
Those held the ārtava back in unit 16.
questions.explain: The blood flows through contrary (ones) or by chance (वा = or).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Built like प्रवृत्ते रक्ते, what does उदिते सूर्ये mean?
options: The sun is going to rise
By means of the rising sun
optionExplain: Right: Two locatives together give the time: when X has happened.
The pair gives a time, not a place in the light.
The participle उदित is past, not future.
That would need an instrumental, not a locative.
questions.explain: प्रवृत्ते रक्ते = when the blood flows; उदिते सूर्ये = when the sun has risen.
questions.rule: Noun + participle both in the locative = when (that happens).
questions.teaches: A noun and a participle together in the locative tell when something happens.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 19, what can rakṣas (demons) take away?
options: The whole body of the embryo
optionExplain: The unit says: not of the body.
Right: ओजसः अपहरणं रक्षोभिः सम्भवति.
Breast milk is not named here.
Semen is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The taking away of ojas by rakṣas occurs, but not of the body.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 19 in their printed order.
questions.explain: Since … occurs … the taking away of ojas … by rakṣas … but not of the body.
questions.rule: यस्मात् → सम्भवति → ओजसः अपहरणम् → रक्षोभिः → न तु कायस्य.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 19 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: These five words carry the claim: ojas may be taken by demons, the body not.
questions.teaches: यस्मात् = since: the unit gives the reason against the claim of unit 18.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which split of ओजसोऽपहरणम् is right?
optionExplain: पहरणम् is not a word of the card.
That would give ओज उपहरणम्, and उपहरणम् is not the card's word.
Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the second अ is shown by ऽ.
आ + अ would give ओजसापहरणम्.
questions.explain: ओजसः (of ojas) + अपहरणम् (taking away) → ओजसोऽपहरणम्.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In unit 19, what role does the word यस्मात् play?
options: It names the demons who act
It states the remedy for the loss
It gives the reason against unit 18
optionExplain: The demons are रक्षोभिः.
The argument goes on in the next units.
No remedy is given here.
Right: Since …: it begins the argument against 'carried off by beings'.
questions.explain: यस्मात् (since) opens the reason why the body is not carried off.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By the rule of ओजसोऽपहरणम्, how is रामः + अपि written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: अः + अ → ओ, and the lost अ is marked ऽ.
अः + अ does not give आ.
र् comes after a vowel other than अ/आ.
The visarga does not stay before अ here.
questions.explain: ओजसः + अपहरणम् → ओजसोऽपहरणम्; so रामः + अपि → रामोऽपि.
questions.teaches: Final अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped, written ऽ.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 20, what is not seen?
options: The flow of blood from the woman
The removal of anyone's body by humans
The swelling of the woman's belly
The taking of ojas by rakṣas
optionExplain: The flow is seen; unit 18 speaks of it.
Right: न च दृश्यते कस्यचिन्मानुषैर्देहापहारः.
The swelling is seen; unit 16 speaks of it.
Unit 19 says that can occur.
questions.explain: The removal of anyone's body by humans is not seen.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put these words of the clear clause of unit 20 in their printed order.
questions.explain: And not is seen, of anyone, by humans, removal of the body.
questions.rule: न च → दृश्यते → कस्यचित् → मानुषैः → देहापहारः.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 20 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: These words make the clear part of the unit and link it to unit 19.
questions.teaches: दृश्यते is passive: is seen; the thing seen (देहापहारः) is in the nominative.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which split of कस्यचिन्मानुषैः is right?
optionExplain: आनुषैः is not a word of the card.
चिन्मानुषैः is not a word.
Right: त् before a nasal (म) becomes न्.
म् + म would give म्म, not न्म.
questions.explain: कस्यचित् (of anyone) + मानुषैः (by humans).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which are in unit 20 as the card reads it?
options: The removal of a body by humans is not seen
The word हि (for) links it to the reason in unit 19
Demons are often seen carrying bodies away
Ojas is taken away by humans
optionExplain: Right: न च दृश्यते … देहापहारः.
Right: हि = for; the card reads this unit as continuing unit 19.
The unit says no removal of a body is seen.
Unit 19 speaks of rakṣas, not humans, taking ojas.
questions.explain: No removal of anyone's body by humans is seen; हि ties this to unit 19.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By the rule of कस्यचिन्मानुषैः, how is तत् + मात्रम् written when joined?
optionExplain: Before म the त् becomes न्, not the retroflex ण्.
त् does not become म्.
In sandhi the त् does not stay before म.
Right: त् before म becomes न्.
questions.explain: कस्यचित् + मानुषैः → कस्यचिन्मानुषैः; so तत् + मात्रम् → तन्मात्रम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a nasal consonant becomes न्.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In the supposition of unit 21, what do some powerful ones proceed to do?
options: Make the blood flow by chance
optionExplain: Right: गर्भस्य शरीराक्षेपे प्रवर्तन्ते.
Ojas belongs to unit 19.
The chance flow belongs to unit 18.
The swelling belongs to unit 16.
questions.explain: If some proceed to cast off the body of the embryo …
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Put these phrases of unit 21 in their printed order.
questions.explain: If … some powerful ones … proceed to cast off the embryo's body, then how … would neglect its mothers?
questions.rule: यदि → केचित् → शरीराक्षेपे प्रवर्तन्ते → तदा कथम् इव → उपेक्षेरन्.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 21 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: यदि … तदा frames the argument; the other words fill it.
questions.teaches: यदि … तदा = if … then: a supposition followed by its consequence.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: Which split of तज्जननीः is right?
optionExplain: तज् is not a word; the pronoun is तत्.
Right: त् before ज becomes ज्: तज्जननीः.
ज्जननीः is not a word.
A visarga before ज would not give ज्ज.
questions.explain: तत् (its) + जननीः (mothers).
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: In the clear part of unit 21, whom would they neglect?
optionExplain: No father is named in the unit.
No physician is named in the unit.
Right: तज्जननीः उपेक्षेरन्: would neglect its mothers.
The ignorant are in unit 18, as speakers.
questions.explain: The question asks how they would neglect its mothers.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By the rule of तज्जननीः, how is तत् + जलम् written when joined?
optionExplain: Before ज the त् goes on to ज्.
च् appears before च/छ, not before ज.
In sandhi the त् does not stay before ज.
Right: त् before ज becomes ज्.
questions.explain: तत् + जननीः → तज्जननीः; so तत् + जलम् → तज्जलम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before ज (or झ) becomes ज्.
questions.section: वातोदर और मिथ्या गर्भ: भूतहरण का खंडन

questions.q: By unit 22, pure ārtava resembles what?
options: Ghee, oil or honey in colour
optionExplain: Right: शशरुधिर-लाक्षारस-उपमम्.
Those colours describe śukra in unit 10.
Milk and cane juice belong to unit 10's simile (ghee in milk, jaggery in cane juice).
Neither is named in this unit.
questions.explain: Pure ārtava resembles hare's blood and lac juice.
questions.rule: शश = hare; रुधिर = blood; लाक्षा = lac.
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: Put these words of unit 22 in their printed order.
questions.explain: Ārtava, resembling hare's blood and lac juice, washed, losing colour, they call pure.
questions.rule: आर्तवम् → उपमम् → धौतम् → विरज्यमानम् → शुद्धम् आहुः.
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: Match each word of unit 22 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two words give the colour simile, two the washing test, and one the verdict.
questions.teaches: Pure ārtava is known by its colour and by losing that colour when washed.
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: By unit 22, what happens to pure ārtava when it is washed?
optionExplain: That is the opposite of विरज्यमान.
Right: धौतं विरज्यमानम्: washed, it loses its colour.
The word says it loses colour.
No smell is named in this unit.
questions.explain: Washed, pure ārtava loses its colour.
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: Ārtava of this kind they call ____, pure (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शुद्धम् आहुः: they call it pure.
questions.teaches: शुद्ध = pure; here neuter accusative शुद्धम्, agreeing with आर्तवम्.
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: By the rule of रसोपमम्, how is चन्द्र + उपमम् written when joined?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
अ + उ does not give ऊ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in रस + उपमम्.
The अ cannot simply vanish.
questions.explain: रस + उपमम् → रसोपमम्; so चन्द्र + उपमम् → चन्द्रोपमम् (resembling the moon).
questions.teaches: अ or आ before उ or ऊ merges into ओ (गुण).
questions.section: शुद्ध आर्तव, प्रजनन-आयु और दंपती का शोधन

questions.q: By unit 23, a man of which ages has no emission of semen and the rest?
optionExplain: Those are the woman's limits in unit 24.
These numbers are not in the unit.
These numbers are not in the unit.

questions.q: Built like पयःसर्पिः, what does the invented मधुसर्पिः mean?
optionExplain: Right: A pair compound like पयःसर्पिः: मधु (honey) and सर्पिः (ghee).

questions.explain: पयःसर्पिः = milk and ghee; मधुसर्पिः = honey and ghee.
questions.rule: A pair (dvandva) compound = X and Y.
questions.teaches: A dvandva compound joins two names with the sense 'X and Y'.

questions.q: In योनौ (from योनि), what does the ending -औ mark here?
optionExplain: -औ is dual in अ-stems, but योनि is an इ-stem; here it is loc. sg.
The instrumental of योनि is योन्या.
Right: The gram label is f. loc. sg.: योनौ = in the yoni.
The genitive plural is योनीनाम्.
questions.explain: For इ-stem nouns like योनि, -औ is the locative singular: योनौ = in the yoni.
questions.rule: -औ is not always dual: इ-stem loc. sg. ends in -औ.
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which statement about the second line of unit 54 is right?
options: It tells one to drink the decoction after holding the paste
It names the yoni as what is washed
It gives the amount of the decoction
Nominal sentence; what is washed is unstated
optionExplain: No verb of drinking stands in the line.
The note: presumably the yoni, but the text does not say.
No amount is given in this unit.
Right: No verb; the note says the yoni is only presumed.
questions.explain: सरलमुद्गपर्णीकषायः प्रक्षालनम्: the decoction is the wash; the object of the wash is left unstated.
questions.rule: Nominal sentence: X (nom.) is Y (nom.), no verb.
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: By the ending of योनौ, what does an invented अग्नौ (from अग्नि, fire) mean?
optionExplain: Right: अग्नि is an इ-stem like योनि; -औ is the locative singular.
-औ is dual in अ-stems like देव (देवौ); the dual of अग्नि is अग्नी.
By the fire is अग्निना.
Of the fires is अग्नीनाम्.
questions.explain: योनि → योनौ (in the yoni); so अग्नि → अग्नौ (in the fire).
questions.teaches: Masculine and feminine इ-stems (अग्नि, योनि) form the locative singular in -औ (feminine ones also in -याम्: योन्याम्).
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of क्वाथमुत्पलपद्मक is right?
optionExplain: मुत्पल is not a word of the card; the plant is उत्पल.
अः + उ would give क्वाथ उत्पल, with no म्.
Right: Final म् before a vowel joins it: क्वाथम् + उ → क्वाथमु.
ए + उ would give क्वाथ उत्पल or क्वाथयुत्पल, not क्वाथमु.
questions.explain: क्वाथम् (decoction, acc.) + उत्पल-पद्मक-क्वाथम् (the decoction of utpala and padmaka).
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel → म joined to the vowel.
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: What does the card say about वासशर्करम् (with vāsa and sugar)?

questions.explain: The card keeps the reach of वासशर्करम् open: one decoction or all three, or two more items.
questions.rule: Where the note leaves a reading open, the card does too.
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: By the rule of क्वाथमुत्पल, how is the invented जलम् + उष्णम् written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: Final म् before the vowel उ joins it: जलमु-.
Anusvāra stands for म् only before a consonant.
That would be जल + उष्णम् (अ + उ → ओ), not जलम्.
र् comes from a visarga, not from म्.
questions.explain: क्वाथम् + उत्पल → क्वाथमुत्पल; so जलम् + उष्णम् → जलमुष्णम्.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel is written joined to it; before a consonant it may be written as anusvāra.
questions.section: वात, पित्त, कफ आर्तवदोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: By घृतेन, what does the invented तैलेन वा (तैल = oil) mean?

questions.q: कषायेण has ण after ष. By the same rule, how is the instrumental of क्षीर (milk) spelt?
optionExplain: After र् with no blocking letter, न must become ण.
The ending is -एण, not -ऐण.
Right: र् followed only by a vowel before न turns it into ण.

questions.section: कुणप, ग्रंथि, पूय आदि दोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 68 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: ग्रन्थि and पूय name the two faults; भस्म and न्यग्रोध belong to the remedies.
questions.rule: ग्रन्थि = knot; पूय = pus; भस्म = ash; न्यग्रोध = banyan.
questions.section: कुणप, ग्रंथि, पूय आदि दोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these words of unit 68 in their printed order.
questions.explain: Fault, then its two remedies; second fault, then its two groups.
questions.teaches: Each line names a fault in the locative (-रेतसि, in ... semen) and then the remedy in the instrumental.
questions.section: कुणप, ग्रंथि, पूय आदि दोषों की चिकित्सा

questions.q: What does the card take the dual ending of परूषकादिन्यग्रोधादिभ्याम् to mean?
options: Two persons, the woman and the man
Two single plants, with no others at all
optionExplain: Right: आदि = beginning with; the dual counts the two named groups.
